blips.name: A2A Agents
blips.description:
Why?

It unlocks collaboration between different systems instead of being stuck in silos.

Description

Protocol that lets AI agents talk, share tasks, and work together across platforms.

blips.name: Spec-Driven Development
blips.description:
Why?

Turns vague ideas into concrete specs fast, reducing back and forth and misalignment.

Description

An AI-assisted toolkit for generating technical specifications, requirements, and design docs from high-level prompts.

blips.name: Agent-2-UI
blips.description:
Why?

Exploring frameworks that allow AI agents to dynamically generate or interact with user interface elements in real-time.

Description

An AI agent framework that translates natural language instructions into UI interactions, enabling autonomous browsing and task execution in web applications.

blips.name: Agentic AI
blips.description:
Why?

Try Agentic AI to build autonomous, goal-driven systems that can plan, reason, and act across tasks with minimal human intervention.

Description

Agentic AI systems act autonomously to achieve goals — breaking tasks into steps, using tools, interacting with APIs, and adapting based on feedback. Unlike single-prompt models, they handle multi-step workflows with minimal human intervention.

blips.name: DevLake
blips.description:
Why?

DevLake worth evaluating. Shows potential. Test before full commitment.

Description

An open-source dev data platform that aggregates data from GitHub, Jira, Jenkins, and other DevOps tools to provide insights into engineering productivity and DORA metrics.

blips.name: Elastic VMware Service  in AWS
blips.description:
Why?

Lets you move VMware workloads to AWS without refactoring, buying time while you modernize at your own pace.

Description

A managed service that runs VMware Cloud Foundation natively on AWS infrastructure, fully integrated with AWS services.

blips.name: AI driven IDE and code editors
blips.description:
Why?

Developers should start using AI-powered IDEs because they boost productivity by automating repetitive tasks, suggesting smarter code completions, and catching bugs early. These tools accelerate development, reduce context switching, and help teams write cleaner, more efficient code—making them especially valuable in fast-paced or complex projects.

Description

AI-driven IDEs embed LLMs directly into the development environment, offering intelligent code completion, automated refactoring, bug detection, and chat-based assistance. Examples include Cursor, Windsurf, and JetBrains AI.

blips.name: AI Productivity Tools
blips.description:
Why?

Teams should continue using AI productivity tools because they consistently save time, reduce manual effort, and improve the quality of work across workflows. By automating routine tasks and offering intelligent suggestions, these tools allow people to focus on more strategic, high-value activities—leading to greater efficiency and better results. As the tools evolve, they keep delivering value by adapting to changing needs and driving ongoing productivity gains.

Description

AI Productivity Tools are AI-powered applications that automate repetitive tasks, enhance decision-making, and streamline workflows — covering writing assistants (Notion AI, Grammarly), meeting tools (Otter.ai, Fireflies), and task automation platforms (Zapier AI, Make).

blips.name: AI-Driven App Builders
blips.description:
Why?

AI-driven app builders (like Builder.ai or other no-code/low-code platforms that incorporate AI) are an emerging trend aiming to speed up development by automating UI layout and even logic generation.

Description

AI-driven app builders are platforms that leverage artificial intelligence to help create software with minimal or no hand-coding.

blips.name: Vercel AI SDK
blips.description:
Why?

The Vercel standard library for integrating streaming LLM responses and UI components into web apps.

Description

A TypeScript toolkit for building AI-powered applications with streaming, structured output, and tool calling support across multiple LLM providers.

blips.name: k8sGPT
blips.description:
Why?

A CNCF project that is gaining momentum, riding on the LLM trend.

Description

k8sGPT is a tool for scanning Kubernetes clusters, diagnosing issues, and explaining them in plain English. It has SRE experience codified into its analyzers and integrates with AI backends like OpenAI, Ollama, and others to triage problems quickly.

blips.name: Kro: Kube Resource Orchestrator
blips.description:
Why?

It simplifies complex deployments and makes them more maintainable.

Description

Groups multiple Kubernetes resources into a single custom API and handles dependencies for you.

blips.name: Airbyte
blips.description:
Why?

The CDC continues to be a trend, and developers who are looking for solutions which would not only support databases, should assess AirByte to see how it fits their problem. Data integration of APIs, applications and databases, should simplify the data integrations and allow one place to monitor all.

Description

AirByte is an open source data integration standard to sync data from applications, APIs and databases. It supports:

  • Builtin extensibility
  • Scheduler
  • R/T monitoring AirByte supports local deployments and AirByte cloud for a fully managed service.

blips.name: Internal Developer Portals (IDPs) (e.g., Port.io. Backstage)
blips.description:
Why?

It gives dev teams self-service without chaos. Less Slack, fewer tickets, more consistency, and guardrails that actually stick.

Description

Internal Developer Portals (IDPs) provide a self-service hub for developers to discover services, manage environments, track ownership, and run workflows — reducing cognitive load and engineering toil. Popular implementations include Backstage (open-source) and Port.io (SaaS).

blips.name: Airflow 2
blips.description:
Why?

Airflow 2 is reaching end-of-life, lacks native support for dynamic, event-driven, and async-first workflows that modern data and AI pipelines demand, leaving teams with mounting technical debt and no migration path forward.

Description

Airflow 2 is the second major version of the popular Airflow 1. It brings an improved API, better scheduler, full REST API and DAG versioning and serialization.

blips.name: Airflow 3
blips.description:
Why?

Apache Airflow 3 is the next major release of the most widely adopted workflow orchestration platform, featuring a decoupled architecture, native event-driven triggers, a redesigned UI, and improved support for dynamic task mapping and async execution — positioning it as a serious modernization over Airflow 2.

Description

Over the last four years, Airflow has grown to power business critical data workflows within organizations of all sizes. We have seen an exponential increase in the use cases for Airflow from its beginnings with ETL, ELT, and Reverse ETL, with over 30% of Airflow users using it for MLOps, and 10% using it for GenAI workflows. Airflow 3 is a response to this use case expansion and is the standard for data application development across the enterprise.

blips.name: Akka
blips.description:
Why?

Akka's shift to a Business Source License (BSL) in 2022 effectively made it non-free for most commercial users, while the open-source fork (Apache Pekko) has emerged as the natural successor, making continued Akka 2 investment a liability.

Description

Akka is a free and open-source toolkit and runtime simplifying the construction of concurrent and distributed applications on the JVM. Akka supports multiple programming models for concurrency, but it emphasizes actor-based concurrency, with inspiration drawn from Erlang

blips.name: Angular
blips.description:
Why?

Angular, although less popular than react, has proven stability and is a dependable framework for large-scale applications.

Description

Angular is a TypeScript-based web application framework maintained by Google.

blips.name: Ant Design
blips.description:
Why?

Ant Design is moved to STOP due to its excessive bundle size and rigid component architecture, which hinders performance and fails to provide the "pixel-perfect" customization required for modern UI standards.

Description

Ant Design is an enterprise-class UI design language and React component library with a large collection of components.

blips.name: Apache Amoro
blips.description:
Why?

If your team runs Iceberg or Paimon tables on S3 or HDFS, Amoro eliminates the custom maintenance jobs and cron scripts most teams write to keep table health in check — plugging in as a management layer on top of your existing lakehouse without replacing your query engine or catalog, making it especially valuable for Flink + Paimon or Spark + Iceberg pipelines that need production-grade table ops without full vendor lock-in.

Description

A lakehouse management system built on Apache Iceberg, providing self-optimizing tables, streaming ingestion, and unified batch/stream processing for data lakes.

blips.name: Apache Arrow
blips.description:
Why?

Apache Arrow is used for efficient, cross-language data processing. It provides a standardized in-memory columnar data format, enabling fast data exchange between different systems, frameworks, and programming languages. Its benefits include high-performance analytics, zero-copy data sharing, and reduced serialization overhead, making it ideal for big data, machine learning, and analytics tasks.

Description

Apache Arrow is a language-agnostic software framework for developing data analytics applications that process columnar data. It contains a standardized column-oriented memory format that is able to represent flat and hierarchical data for efficient analytic operations on modern CPU and GPU hardware.

blips.name: Apache Beam
blips.description:
Why?

Apache beam is now a leading force for the whole area of streaming. With its unified SDK, it is forcing competitor frameworks to reevaluate what they have to offer. In addition, google dataflow hosted beam is a great SAAS service

Description

Apache Beam is an open-source, unified model for defining both batch and streaming data-parallel processing pipelines. Beam supplies an SDK in different languages (java, python, scala) to express the flow and processing of the data). The SDK then applies the runner according to the chosen platform (spark, Flink, gear…). Beam aims to lead the industry on the proper way to deal with batch and streaming in the same pipeline. In addition, Beam addresses issues like process time vs event time and handling late data.

blips.name: Apache Doris
blips.description:
Why?

Apache Doris is a battle-tested, production-grade alternative to ClickHouse and StarRocks with a stronger open-source community and more mature ecosystem — for teams needing unified real-time + historical analytics with flexible ingestion from Kafka, Flink, or CDC sources, Doris delivers high performance without the operational complexity of stitching together multiple specialized systems.

Description

Apache Doris is a high-performance, real-time analytical database designed for low-latency, high-concurrency query workloads. It combines fast data ingestion with a massively parallel processing (MPP) engine, making it ideal for interactive dashboards, ad hoc queries, and big data analytics at scale.

blips.name: Apache Flink
blips.description:
Why?

Streaming systems have become part of almost every project. For batch, a processing spark is a great tool. But as more system moves to streaming Flink brings a better SDK model for dealing with an event to event processing.

Description

The core of Apache Flink is a distributed streaming dataflow engine written in Java and Scala. Flink executes arbitrary dataflow programs in a data-parallel and pipelined manner. Flink’s pipelined runtime system enables the execution of bulk/batch and stream processing programs. Furthermore, Flink’s runtime supports the execution of iterative algorithms natively. Flink provides a high-throughput, low-latency streaming engine as well as support for event-time processing and state management. Flink applications are fault-tolerant in the event of machine failure and support exactly-once semantics

blips.name: Apache Gravitino
blips.description:
Why?

Gravitino eliminates the fragmented metadata problem in modern lakehouses — if your team is managing multiple engines and formats with no single source of truth for schemas and permissions, Gravitino gives you cross-engine governance and discoverability without vendor lock-in or replacing your existing infrastructure.

Description

Apache Gravitino is an open-source, high-performance metadata lake and unified catalog for managing data and AI assets across heterogeneous systems. It provides a single access layer for metadata from data lakes, warehouses, and ML platforms, supporting engines like Spark, Trino, and Flink through a REST API and a Kerberos-compatible security model.

blips.name: Apache Hudi
blips.description:
Why?

Hudi's complex operational overhead, inconsistent query performance compared to Delta Lake and Iceberg, and weaker ecosystem momentum make it the least compelling choice in the modern open table format race.

Description

Apache Hudi manages the storage for BigData. It supports any HDFS compatible storage and enables ACID transactions in a data lake.

blips.name: Apache Iceberg
blips.description:
Why?

Apache Iceberg provides us reliable , maintainable and efficient way to work with data lake. It hides implementation details and makes it much more robust.

Description

Apache Iceberg is an open table format for huge analytic datasets. Iceberg adds tables to Presto and Spark that use a high-performance format that works just like a SQL table.

blips.name: Apache Paimon
blips.description:
Why?

Paimon is the strongest choice for teams running Flink-based streaming pipelines who need a lakehouse table format with first-class CDC support, low-latency upserts, and unified batch/stream reads without the operational complexity of Kafka + Iceberg stitched together.

Description

Apache Paimon is an open table format (like Delta Lake or Iceberg) optimized for streaming-first lakehouse architectures, enabling real-time data ingestion, CDC (Change Data Capture) pipelines, and unified batch/stream processing — with native Flink integration as its primary differentiator.

blips.name: Apache Pinot
blips.description:
Why?

Apache Pinot enables ultra-low-latency analytics on real-time and batch data at scale, making it ideal for powering user-facing dashboards and high-throughput applications. Pinot supports fast ingestion, flexible indexing, and high-concurrency querying with millisecond response times, even on large datasets. Its ability to handle both streaming and historical data in a single system simplifies architecture while delivering real-time insights. As data volumes and performance demands grow, Pinot remains a reliable choice for interactive analytics with speed, scalability, and precision.

Description

Apache Pinot is a Realtime distributed OLAP datastore. It is built originally Linkedin and is currently and Apache Incubating project. It is intended to to answer OLAP queries with low latency and therefore fits into the monitoring database section, just as Apache Druid and others.

It boasts many interesting features such as real-time data ingestion, highly scalable, hybrid tables and many more mainstream capabilities. A pluggable indexing solution promises blazing fast response times.

The feature which sets this tool apart is its integrated Anomaly Detection and Alerting solution called ThirdEye.

blips.name: Apache Polaris
blips.description:
Why?

Apache Polaris is the emerging open-source catalog standard for Iceberg tables — its vendor-neutral governance, fine-grained access control, and multi-engine interoperability make it the most future-proof foundation for teams building open lakehouse architectures.

Description

An open-source catalog service for Apache Iceberg tables, providing a vendor-neutral REST API for managing table metadata across cloud storage systems.

blips.name: Apache Pulsar
blips.description:
Why?

Apache Pulsar is the new Kafka. This product has the strengths of Kafka but also adds multiple features that are missing in Kafka and exists in other messaging platform such as rabbit, while maintaining the ability to scale.

Description

Apache Pulsar is an open-source distributed pub-sub messaging system originally created at Yahoo and now part of the Apache Software Foundation

blips.name: Apache Spark 3.0
blips.description:
Why?

Spark 3.0 will move to Python3 and Scala version is upgraded to version 2.12. A major performance improvement for SQL analytics is provided by Dynamic Partition Pruning. Enhanced Support for Deep Learning is integrated with features such as support for different GPUs and special Vectorized UDFs. A better Kubernetes Integration now allows dynamic scale up and down. Bottom line, many new incredible features for an already incredible tool.

Description

Apache Spark is an open-source distributed general-purpose cluster-computing framework. Today it is the de facto standard tool for batch processing, although it also supports stream processing by way of micro batches. Customers such as Amazon, eBay, and Yahoo are only a few of many who run Spark clusters with thousands of nodes processing many terabytes of data. A DAG scheduler, a query optimizer, and a physical execution engine provide low execution times.

Under the hood, its API is provided for the Java, Scala and Python languages while the most extensive API is written in Scala followed by Python. One can also write the pipelines in a SQL derivative called SparkSQL. Riding on the Hadoop ecosystem it has a huge ecosystem for integration and collaboration

blips.name: Apache Spark 4.0
blips.description:
Why?

Spark 4.0's Spark Connect architecture decouples client code from the cluster — enabling lightweight, IDE-friendly PySpark development without a local Spark install, while the Python-first improvements make it significantly less painful for data/AI teams to build and maintain large-scale pipelines without needing Scala expertise.

Description

Apache Spark 4.0 is the next major release of the distributed compute engine, featuring a redesigned Python-first API (PySpark parity with Scala), Spark Connect as the default client-server architecture, improved structured streaming with watermark enhancements, and deeper Iceberg/Delta Lake integration.

blips.name: SigNoz
blips.description:
Why?

Helps you understand your apps at a glance and troubleshoot issues quickly — without expensive SaaS bills.

Description

SigNoz is a self-hosted open-source alternative to Datadog. It offers logs, metrics, and traces in one place to monitor app performance and behavior.

blips.name: Multi-Agent Claude Code Review
blips.description:
Why?

Increases code review quality and coverage by parallelizing analysis across multiple perspectives, reducing the chance of bugs or security issues slipping through.

Description

An AI-powered code review system that uses multiple specialized Claude agents to analyze pull requests for security, performance, style, and correctness in parallel.

blips.name: Openclaw
blips.description:
Why?

Enables full automation of complex workflows by letting AI agents take real actions across systems, but comes with serious risk if not tightly controlled due to its level of access.

Description

An open-source AI web scraping framework that uses vision-language models to extract structured data from websites without writing CSS selectors.

blips.name: Jsonnet/Ksonnet
blips.description:
Why?

Ksonnet project has stopped the development and the git repo is archived.

Description

Jsonnet Ksonnet

Ksonnet project is no longer being developed. see Bottom line the Ksonnet project has stopped the development and the git repo is archived

blips.name: Base UI
blips.description:
Why?

A promising headless successor to Radix UI, offering even greater flexibility for building custom design systems.

Description

A headless React component library from MUI providing unstyled, accessible UI primitives that can be fully customized without overriding styles.

blips.name: Beartype
blips.description:
Why?

beartype adds real runtime type safety to Python codebases with near-zero overhead — ideal for catching subtle type bugs in data pipelines, LLM output validators, or API layers where Pydantic is overkill but silent type errors are costly.

Description

A pure-Python runtime type checker that enforces type hints at runtime with near-zero overhead, catching type errors during execution rather than static analysis.

blips.name: Node.js
blips.description:
Why?

Stop using Node.js + JavaScript for backend development if you're hitting scalability, maintainability, or performance walls. Modern alternatives like Go, Rust, or Python (FastAPI) offer better type safety, concurrency, and developer experience for complex systems. JavaScript’s dynamic typing and callback-heavy history make large projects harder to manage. Unless you're building something lightweight or already deeply invested, it might be time to move on.

Description

Node.js is a JavaScript runtime built on Chrome’s V8 engine that allows JavaScript to be run on the server (outside the browser). It introduced an event loop and non-blocking I/O model which make it efficient for building applications that handle a lot of I/O (like network requests or filesystem operations) concurrently.

blips.name: OpenStack
blips.description:
Why?

The domination of docker and Kubernetes as the standard way to run your workload, Along with better Kubernetes on-premise solutions. Made a full-featured private cloud unnecessary for most organizations. That made OpenStack a niche technology for those who really need cloud services in the (private) data center.

Description

OpenStack is a free and open-source software platform for cloud computing, mostly deployed as infrastructure-as-a-service (IaaS), whereby virtual servers and other resources are made available to customers. The software platform consists of interrelated components that control diverse, multi-vendor hardware pools of processing, storage, and networking resources throughout a data center. Users either manage it through a web-based dashboard, through command-line tools or through RESTful web services.

On top of OpenStack core services, that provide the basic cloud functionality of managing to compute, storage and networking resources. OpenStack project contains a set of services (sometimes named ‘The big tenet’) that provide a lot of complementary functionality such as shared storage, databases, monitoring, orchestrating and much more.

blips.name: BigQuery
blips.description:
Why?

Many companies have already adopted this DB as its Data Warehousing solution and we suggest to keep it this way.

Description

BigQuery is Google Cloud's fully managed, serverless data warehouse for running fast SQL analytics over petabyte-scale datasets. It separates storage from compute, supports real-time ingestion, and integrates natively with the Google Cloud AI and data ecosystem.

blips.name: Biome
blips.description:
Why?

Biome (the successor to the Rome project) aims to be an all-in-one toolchain for web development, written in Rust for high performance.

Description

Biome is a unified, high-performance toolchain written in Rust that provides linting, formatting, and other developer tools in a single package. It evolved from the Rome project (officially forking it) with the goal of simplifying the fragmented JS tooling ecosystem.

blips.name: Python 2
blips.description:
Why?

Python 2.7 will not be maintained past 2020. Originally, there was no official date. Recently, that date has been updated to January 1, 2020. We suggest stopping using this version, especially for new projects.

Description

Python is a powerful high-level, interpreted, open source, object-oriented programming language, portable, extensible and embeddable with simple syntax and large standard libraries to solve common tasks. Python is a general-purpose language. It has a wide range of applications from Web development (like Django and Bottle), scientific and mathematical computing (Orange, SymPy, NumPy) to desktop graphical user Interfaces (Pygame, Panda3D).

blips.name: Ruby
blips.description:
Why?

We assume that there will always be something written in ruby but it will most definitely not be the language of choice when we are required to develop a utility / micro-app.

Description

It seems like the utilization of Ruby as a software development language which was very popular in the DevOps movement mainly with tools like Chef and Puppet Logstash Fluentd and a lot of scripting and utilities around ruby and ruby on rails application lifecycle such as Capistrano, has taken a punch in favor of python go and javascript. With the rise of popularity of these langs & frameworks, we see less and less use of ruby.

blips.name: Swarm
blips.description:
Why?

We identify a large client base in the process of either living within the limits of the swarm or moving to Kubernetes.

Description

Docker Compose is a tool for defining and running multi-container Docker applications. With Compose, you use a YAML file to configure your application’s services. Then, with a single command, you create and start all the services from your configuration.

Docker Compose is used for running multi-container applications on a single machine or on multiple machines with Swarm mostly in Dev and QA environments, and in some places in Production as well.

The cluster management and orchestration features embedded in the Docker Engine

blips.name: Bun
blips.description:
Why?

Bun offers an all-in-one JavaScript runtime, package manager, and bundler that is significantly faster than traditional Node.js tooling. By streamlining dependency management, script execution, and bundling into a single, high-performance tool, Bun reduces setup complexity and speeds up development workflows. It supports modern JavaScript and TypeScript out of the box, making it ideal for building fast, efficient web apps and server-side projects. As the ecosystem matures, Bun continues to deliver performance gains and developer convenience in one cohesive package.

Description

Bun is an all-in-one JavaScript runtime and toolkit designed for speed.

blips.name: CDC
blips.description:
Why?

In the world of Micro-Service and cloud computing, we are in constant need to enrich data and view data combined from multiple sources. Developing CDC solutions or building on open-source solutions, allows viewing the complete data in any application.

Description

Change Data Capture (aka CDC) is a design pattern for tracking data changes and performing actions according to the change.

blips.name: Apache Zeppelin
blips.description:
Why?

Stop using Apache Zeppelin because it's outdated, with slow development and poor community momentum. Tools like Jupyter and JupyterLab offer better UX, richer ecosystems, and stronger multi-language support. Zeppelin’s UI is clunky, plotting is limited, and integration with modern platforms like Kubernetes or cloud-native workflows is weak. Unless you're locked into legacy Spark setups, there's little reason to stick with it.

Description

Apache Zeppelin is a notebook for managing and visualizing Data and Data-lake. With Apache Zeppelin, one can perform Data Ingestion, Data Discovery, Data Analytics and also have Data Visualization & Collaboration. Apache Zeppelin is a Java runtime and supports the following languages and frameworks: Scala as Apache Spark, Python, JDBC, Markdown and Shell. It also supports many plugins The results of the queries can be shown in nice built-in visuals like graphs, pie charts and more.

Apache Zeppelin supports many additional interpreters that can be loaded or integrated using Helium, Among those interpreters are for example Cassandra, Elasticsearch, Flink, Ignite, bean, angular and many more.

blips.name: Chai
blips.description:
Why?

Most modern testing frameworks come with their own assertion libraries, making standalone libraries like Chai less necessary.

Description

A BDD/TDD assertion library for Node.js that pairs with test frameworks like Mocha, providing expressive syntax for writing test assertions.

blips.name: Agentic AI
blips.description:
Why?

If you’re curious about adding AI to your app — summaries, Q&A, content creation — this is a plug-and-play way to get started using industry-grade models.

Description

Agentic AI systems act autonomously to achieve goals — breaking tasks into steps, using tools, interacting with APIs, and adapting based on feedback. Unlike single-prompt models, they handle multi-step workflows with minimal human intervention.

blips.name: AI Agents
blips.description:
Why?

they can automate multi-step work with minimal babysitting, freeing up time for higher-value work.

Description

Autonomous “AI” software that senses, plans, and acts toward goals - beyond chatbots, they independently handle tasks with minimal supervision.

blips.name: CircleCI
blips.description:
Why?

Users have criticized the organization of options in the config file, finding it arbitrary and unhelpful for managing their configurations effectively. This confusion has led to difficulties in setting up and maintaining their projects on CircleCI

Description

CircleCI: Continuous Integration and Deliveryhttps://circleci.com

blips.name: Context Engineering
blips.description:
Why?

Bigger context helps, but too much context hurts agents. Long windows can slow reasoning, increase noise, and lead to worse decisions. The goal is the right amount, not the maximum.

Description

Context Engineering is the practice of deliberately designing, structuring, and optimizing the information fed into an LLM's context window — including system prompts, retrieved documents, memory summaries, tool outputs, and conversation history — to maximize model performance, reduce hallucination, and stay within token budget constraints.

blips.name: Arc: Github Runners on demand
blips.description:
Why?

You stop paying for idle CI runners and get fast, isolated builds exactly when you need them.

Description

A Kubernetes operator that provisions self-hosted GitHub Actions runners on-demand, scaling them up and down based on workflow demand. It enables cost-efficient, secure CI/CD by running GitHub Actions in your own infrastructure.

blips.name: Claude-mem
blips.description:
Why?

If you use Claude Code heavily for complex, multi-session projects, Claude-Mem solves the most painful friction point — losing context between sessions — without manual summarization or copy-pasting. For AI-heavy development workflows like building agents, LLM pipelines, or long-running codebases, it effectively gives Claude persistent project memory with zero manual overhead, turning each new session into a continuation rather than a cold start.

Description

An open-source Claude Code plugin that automatically captures tool usage and observations during coding sessions, compresses them into AI-generated semantic summaries, and injects relevant context back into future sessions — using a SQLite + ChromaDB hybrid search backend with an MCP interface and a local web viewer UI.

blips.name: ClearML
blips.description:
Why?

ClearML enhances collaboration, automates processes, and improves visibility in teams, ultimately setting new standards for seamless integration between experiment management, MLOps, and data management. Its open architecture allows for easy customization and integration with existing tools, making it a versatile and efficient choice for enterprise MLOps needs.

Description

All in one tool for machine learning software development. It gives data scientists tools to manage experiments, orchestrate workloads, and manage data. It's an open-source and integrates with whatever toolchain a team is using already.

blips.name: ClickHouse
blips.description:
Why?

ClickHouse is best used for analytics over a stream of clean, well structured and immutable events or logs. ClickHouse has unique advantages when comparing it to competing solutions:

  •  It's completely open source and free of vendor locking (compared to proprietary products such as Amazon Redshift, Google BigQuery and Snowflake)
  • It can run on cloud as well as on premise (compared to the solutions above)
  • It's hardware efficient, optimizing CPU and disk drive access while minimizing data transfers, resulting in fast response times (compared to Hadoop / Spark ecosystem solutions)

Description

ClickHouse is a fast open-source OLAP database management system. ClickHouse's performance exceeds comparable column-oriented database management systems currently available on the market. It processes hundreds of millions to more than a billion rows and tens of gigabytes of data per single server per second.

blips.name: Bedrock
blips.description:
Why?

If you’re curious about adding AI to your app — summaries, Q&A, content creation — this is a plug-and-play way to get started using industry-grade models.

Description

Bedrock lets you access powerful foundation models (like Claude or Amazon Titan) via an API, without managing infrastructure.

blips.name: Chaos Toolkit
blips.description:
Why?

ChaosToolkit was one of the first frameworks we tested for running Chaos Experiments. From the Hypothesis to the Experiment and Desired result.

Description

cert-manager is a powerful, general-purpose certificate management controller for Kubernetes.

blips.name: CloudQuery
blips.description:
Why?

As an opensource scalable tool, CloudQuery is optimized for performance, utilizing the excellent Go concurrency model with light-weight goroutines. In addition the plugins are single-binary executables and can be deployed and run anywhere. It comes with a number of out-of-the-box security and compliance policies for cloud infrastructure. 

Description

CloudQuery is an open-source, high-performance data integration framework built for developers, with support for a wide range of plugins. CloudQuery extracts, transforms, and loads configuration from cloud APIs, files or databases to variety of supported destinations such as databases, data lakes, or streaming platforms for further analysis.

blips.name: Colima
blips.description:
Why?

Colima offers a fast, lightweight, and reliable Docker and Kubernetes environment on macOS and Linux—often outperforming Docker Desktop in speed and resource efficiency. Built on Lima and containerd, Colima provides seamless compatibility with Docker CLI and Compose, while being open-source and free of licensing restrictions. It’s especially valuable for developers who want a stable, configurable, and performant local container runtime without the overhead or limitations of proprietary solutions. As container-based workflows grow, Colima remains a dependable and developer-friendly choice.

Description

Colima is a free, open-source container runtime for macOS and Linux, serving as a lightweight alternative to Docker Desktop. It is CLI-based and supports Docker and containerd runtimes, port forwarding, volumes, and optional Kubernetes.

blips.name: Context Engineering
blips.description:
Why?

Without it, even the best model gives shallow or wrong answers.

Description

Context Engineering is the practice of deliberately designing, structuring, and optimizing the information fed into an LLM's context window — including system prompts, retrieved documents, memory summaries, tool outputs, and conversation history — to maximize model performance, reduce hallucination, and stay within token budget constraints.

blips.name: Cursor
blips.description:
Why?

Cursor gained significant popularity among software engineers due to its integration of advanced language models, such as Claude Sonnet 3.5. It's ideal for professional developers who want powerful AI assistance while maintaining the familiar VS Code interface and ecosystem. Best suited for complex projects requiring sophisticated code understanding, refactoring large codebases, and teams that need reliable AI pair programming capabilities.

Description

Cursor is the most popular AI IDE. It's built as a fork of VS Code but with deep AI integration throughout the development workflow. It enhances developer productivity by integrating advanced AI features, such as code generation, smart rewrites, and natural language codebase queries, directly into the coding workflow. With real-time collaboration, context-aware suggestions, predictive completions, and an agent mode for autonomous task handling, CursorAI targets both individual developers and teams. It operates on a freemium model and is rapidly growing, supported by significant investment and a focus on continuous AI-driven innovation in software development.

blips.name: Gardener
blips.description:
Why?

A project designed to manage multiple Kubernetes clusters. Gardener by SAP, Following the botanical terminology, the end-user clusters when ready to sprout are called "shoot" clusters. Which are managed by a "Seed" cluster which sprouts those "shoot" clusters used by the end-user.

Description

Gardener is a Kubernetes-native project that manages the full lifecycle of Kubernetes clusters across cloud providers and on-premises environments. It uses Kubernetes itself as an API server to provision and reconcile 'shoot' clusters, enabling teams to operate large fleets of clusters with consistent configuration, automated upgrades, and built-in shoot reconciliation.

blips.name: Context Engineering
blips.description:
Why?

As LLM applications mature, context engineering is emerging as the highest-leverage skill in AI development — prompt engineering gets you started, but context engineering is what separates brittle demos from reliable production systems. For agent pipelines, RAG architectures, and multi-step workflows, how you structure, compress, prioritize, and inject context directly determines output quality, latency, and cost — making it an essential discipline for any team serious about shipping dependable AI products.

Description

Context Engineering is the practice of deliberately designing, structuring, and optimizing the information fed into an LLM's context window — including system prompts, retrieved documents, memory summaries, tool outputs, and conversation history — to maximize model performance, reduce hallucination, and stay within token budget constraints.

blips.name: Gloo
blips.description:
Why?

Gloo is mature enough for production use, offering a flexible and powerful solution for managing north-south traffic and internal service-to-service communication. Its ability to integrate with a wide range of cloud-native tools and environments makes it a strong candidate for modernizing API management and ingress control.

Description

A feature-rich Kubernetes-native API gateway built on Envoy Proxy, offering advanced traffic management, security, and observability for microservices and serverless workloads.

blips.name: Create React App
blips.description:
Why?

Create React App (CRA) has fallen out of favor as the community has moved to faster, more flexible tooling. The project is deprecated by the team.

Description

Create React App is a command line tool developed by Facebook that enables developers to quickly create and set up a new single-page React.js application.

blips.name: k6
blips.description:
Why?

Whether you’re launching a site or a product, this tool helps make sure it won’t crash under real-world use.

Description

k3s is wrapped in a simple package that reduces the dependencies and steps needed to run a production Kubernetes cluster. Packaged as a single binary, k3s makes installation and upgrade as simple as copying a file. TLS certificates are automatically generated to ensure that all communication is secure by default.

Used in Edge & IoT to enable a standard distro across the board.

blips.name: kube-score
blips.description:
Why?

This tool alongside many similar ones is designed to help its users identify security & policy violations at runtime.

Description

Kong Inc. is a software company offering open-source platforms and cloud services to manage, monitor and scale Application Programming Interfaces and Microservices.

blips.name: kubeaudit
blips.description:
Why?

Kubeaudit, similar to scanning tools like Popeye. KubeAudit is focused on security. kubeaudit is a command-line tool used to audit Kubernetes clusters for various different security concerns, such as:

  • run as non-root
  • use a read-only root filesystem
  • drop scary capabilities, don't add new ones
  • don't run privileged

Kubeaudit also comes with an Autofix feature that can be used to mitigate misconfiguration in real-time, a great tool that can be used by developers & SRE during prototyping and in runtime.

Description

kubeaudit is a command line tool and a Go package to audit Kubernetes clusters for various different security concerns

blips.name: Cypress
blips.description:
Why?

Cypress is a widely adopted end-to-end testing framework that runs in the browser and offers a great developer experience (automatic waiting, time-travel debugging, etc.).

Description

Cypress is an end-to-end testing framework for web applications. It runs tests directly in a real browser environment, giving developers visibility into each step of a test run with features like DOM snapshots and detailed logs.

blips.name: Dagster
blips.description:
Why?

There are multiple reason to choose to work witrh Dagster today. It puts an emphasis on type safety, and its design encourages modular and reusable components through its use of "solids" and "composites. It offers an integrated web-based user interface called Dagit. Dagit offers rich features for developing, visualizing, and debugging pipelines. Also, it allows for easy testing and all in all is just better suited for many tasks in the modern data orchestartion world. I endorse this tool wholeheartedly

Description

Dagster is a data orchestrator for machine learning, analytics, and ETL. It lets you define pipelines in terms of the data flow between reusable, logical components, then test locally and run anywhere. At a high level Dagster lets you define data pipelines, or data flows between solids. A Solid in Dagster is some computation, when you combine different solids you get a Pipeline.

blips.name: Dart
blips.description:
Why?

undefined

Description

Dart is the Google's programming language that is optimised for client side. Many rich frameworks such as Flutter are using Dart as their development language. 

Approach ==========  Dart is a light wight, object oriented language that utilise modern programming paradigms such as reactive functional programming.  Dart syntax is very familiar to C#, C++, Java and Kotlin developers.  Furthermore, Dart code is highly expressive

blips.name: Dask
blips.description:
Why?

Dask enables scalable data processing in Python with a familiar, flexible API that integrates seamlessly with tools like Pandas, NumPy, and scikit-learn. Dask makes it easy to handle larger-than-memory datasets and parallelize computations across cores or clusters without rewriting code. It’s especially valuable for teams working on data science, machine learning, or ETL pipelines who want to scale workflows without leaving the Python ecosystem. As data workloads grow, Dask remains a powerful and accessible solution for distributed computing.

Description

Parallel computing Python library

blips.name: Data Catalog
blips.description:
Why?

Data Catalogs are important to allow visibility into data lakes and data warehouses. In the world of ever growing data, and its importance to drive business value, the number of tables and datasets are hard to control. Applying a data catalog becomes crucial for companies which collect, transform and analyze data in masses.

Description

A Data Catalog is a collection of metadata, combined with data management and search tools, that helps analysts and other data users to find the data that they need, serves as an inventory of available data, and provides information to evaluate fitness data for intended uses.

blips.name: Data Lake
blips.description:
Why?

A Data Lake is a must in any project that accumulates data. This is needed as a source of truth, and gives the flexibility to change the data model in the future.

Description

A data lake is a storage repository that holds a big amount of raw data in its native format until it is needed

blips.name: Data Mesh
blips.description:
Why?

Data Mesh is worth keeping if your organization has multiple autonomous domain teams drowning in centralized data team bottlenecks — it scales data ownership, accountability, and quality in ways no centralized architecture can match at org complexity.

Description

Data Mesh is an architectural approach that decentralizes data management within an organization. The data is owned and managed by individual domain teams. Key principles include:

  • decentralized data ownership, federated computational governance
  • self-serve infrastructure as a platform
  • thinking with cross-functional teams
  • and a distributed data architecture

blips.name: Data Monitoring
blips.description:
Why?

Data monitoring helps you make better decisions by ensuring that your data is reliable, accurate and up to date, identify areas for performance improvements, and early error detection

Description

Companies are monitoring the health and performance of applications for long time. Lately, the need to monitor data as well is also rising. The ability to tell that data characteristics is changed over time is important today, as many statistical and machine learning models rely on that data, and their accuracy is changed when data is changed. Therefore, there is a need for tools that monitor and alert significant data changes.

blips.name: Databricks
blips.description:
Why?

Databricks equips developers with an all-in-one platform for efficient collaboration, streamlined machine learning workflows, and easy management of large-scale data operations.

Description

Databricks is an advanced unified analytics platform that leverages Apache Spark to enable collaborative data science and analytics at scale.

blips.name: DataHub
blips.description:
Why?

LinkedIn DataHub stands out as a top choice for data cataloging due to its comprehensive metadata management, offering insights into technical, business, and social metadata. Its powerful search and discovery capabilities enable quick and efficient data asset location. DataHub's flexible and extensible architecture allows seamless integration with existing data ecosystems and customization to meet organizational needs. These features collectively enhance data discovery, governance, and collaboration, making DataHub an ideal solution for modern data teams.

Description

DataHub is an open-source metadata management platform for the modern data stack that enables data discovery, data observability, and federated governance. It was built by Linkedin in their third(!) attempt to create an open, extensible and pluggable data catalog and it seems the third time's a charm. It works by pushing the metadata to the catalog, but it also has its own data discovery features including lineage, statistics, data preview and many more features.

blips.name: date-fns
blips.description:
Why?

date-fns is a lightweight date utility library that delivers much of Moment.js’s functionality in a modular way. Its functions can be imported individually, which keeps bundle sizes small.

Description

A modern JavaScript date utility library offering immutable, pure functions for date manipulation and formatting, providing a lightweight alternative to Moment.js.

blips.name: day.js
blips.description:
Why?

day.js serves as a minimalist alternative to Moment.js, offering a similar API but with a much smaller footprint.

Description

day.js is a tiny (2KB) JavaScript date library with a Moment.js-compatible API.

blips.name: dbt
blips.description:
Why?

DBT creates a new standard for transformations of data in the data warehouse. DBT is a generic library with adapters per data warehouse and has become one of the most popular tools.

Description

DBT enables data analysts and engineers to transform their data using the same practices that software engineers use to build applications.

blips.name: Debezium
blips.description:
Why?

Some typical use cases for CDC include: purge a cache, update search indexes, generate derived views and data, keep other data sources in sync, and much more. The advantages of Debezium's approach to infer changes by reading database logs instead of polling data, include reducing resource load, as well as code complexity. Another great advantage is fault tolerance. Even if your apps go down, Debezium keeps monitoring and continues exactly where they left off. No matter what, Debezium keeps the events in the same order and makes sure that you always see every event, even when things go wrong. Debezium is built on top of Apache Kafka, which is proven, scalable, and handles very large volumes of data very quickly.

Description

Debezium stream changes from your databases. Debezium is an open-source distributed platform for change data capture. Start it up, point it at your databases, and your apps can start responding to all of the inserts, updates, and deletes that other apps commit to your databases. Debezium is durable and fast, so your apps can respond quickly and never miss an event, even when things go wrong.

blips.name: DeepEval
blips.description:
Why?

DeepEval is worth trying as an LLM evaluation framework because it's specifically designed for testing LLM applications with a pytest-like syntax that developers already understand. It offers built-in metrics for essential dimensions like correctness, relevance, hallucination detection, and context utilization, while supporting multiple LLM providers. The framework enables consistent, objective evaluation that can be integrated into CI/CD pipelines, helping teams measure and improve their LLM application quality over time.

Description

DeepEval is an open-source LLM evaluation framework for benchmarking, regression-testing, and monitoring LLM applications. It provides research-backed metrics including hallucination detection, answer relevancy, faithfulness, and contextual recall, with a pytest-style test interface.

blips.name: Delta Lake
blips.description:
Why?

Delta Lake’s ACID transactions, UPSERT/MERGE support and time travel features allow organizations to reuse existing SQL queries to perform their ETL process directly on the object store, and to leverage familiar maintenance features such as rollbacks, time travel and audit logs. Moreover, using a single storage system (Delta Lake) instead of a separate data lake and warehouse reduces the latency to make new data queryable by removing the need for a separate ingest process. Finally, Delta Lake’s support of both SQL and programmatic APIs (via Apache Spark) makes it easy to write data engineering pipelines using a variety of tools. For users that want to run ad-hoc query and BI workloads against their lakehouse datasets, either through SQL directly or through BI software such as Tableau, Delta Lake can support all these features directly for tables in a cloud object store, through its combination of columnar formats, data layout optimization, max-min statistics, and SSD caching

Description

Delta Lake is a storage layer that brings ACID transactions to Apache Spark and big data workloads. It allows storage options and operations that were missing since the start of the BigData era, mostly transaction-related options and storage updates, such as add, merge and delete. The BigData world has sacrificed attributes such as ACID and updates for the sake of speed and volume. But, since the growth of computing power, libraries, and techniques, those important attributes can be used again, along with the challenge of ever-growing data volumes. Delta Lake is an important endeavor, lead by DataBricks, to combine the important attributes of the traditional relational world with the power brought by BigData and parallel computing development of the past 10 years.

blips.name: Deno
blips.description:
Why?

Deno is a secure, modern runtime for JavaScript and TypeScript that addresses some of Node.js’s historical pain points (built-in TypeScript support, no need for a package manager, and a permission system).

Description

Deno is an open-source runtime for JavaScript and TypeScript created by Node’s original author. It is built with security in mind – by default, Deno scripts have no file system or network access unless explicitly enabled.

blips.name: Deno
blips.description:
Why?

Deno's built-in TypeScript support, secure-by-default permissions, native Web APIs, and built-in toolchain eliminate the Node.js configuration overhead — making it the cleanest modern JavaScript runtime for teams starting fresh.

Description

Deno is an open-source runtime for JavaScript and TypeScript created by Node’s original author. It is built with security in mind – by default, Deno scripts have no file system or network access unless explicitly enabled.

blips.name: Desktop PWA
blips.description:
Why?

Allowing users to install our web app as a desktop PWA can increase engagement, as many users prefer launching an app directly rather than navigating via a browser.

Description

A Desktop PWA is a Progressive Web App that a user can install on their desktop OS, making it accessible like a native application. When installed, it runs in a standalone window (without browser UI) and can integrate with system features

blips.name: Kubeflow
blips.description:
Why?

As a relatively new project, it supports cloud-native distribution as it can be installed on any Kubernetes system. It uses the k8s infrastructure to execute model training and serving. It is part of a broader area of MLOps and its popularity is constantly growing.

Description

Kubeflow is a framework for deploying ML workflows on Kubernetes cluster. It is based on Argo Workflow and provides a Python API to easily create Argo workflows without the need to write YAML files. Kubeflow include all the ingredients for a full ML development: research with JupyterLabs, training and experimenting via pipelines and model lifecycle management.

blips.name: Kyverno
blips.description:
Why?

As Kubernetes environments grow more complex, the need for effective policy management becomes crucial. Kyverno offers a native, declarative approach to policy enforcement that is easy to adopt and integrate into existing workflows. Its maturity and active community support make it suitable for immediate use.

Description

Kyverno is a policy engine designed specifically for Kubernetes. It enables administrators to enforce, validate, and mutate Kubernetes resource configurations using a simple, Kubernetes-native language.

blips.name: LM Studio
blips.description:
Why?

Perfect for experimenting with AI while keeping your data local. You can build your own ChatGPT-like assistant without sending anything to the clou

Description

LM Studio is a desktop app for discovering, downloading, and running large language models locally on your own hardware, with no cloud dependency. It provides a chat UI, an OpenAI-compatible local API server, and supports models from Hugging Face in GGUF format.

blips.name: Diskless
blips.description:
Why?

Diskless architectures dramatically simplify node management, reduce hardware failure points, and enable instant provisioning and recovery — making them compelling for teams running large compute clusters, GPU nodes, or ephemeral workloads where local disk is a bottleneck and operational overhead.

Description

Diskless refers to a computing architecture where nodes boot and operate entirely from network-based or in-memory storage rather than local disks — relying on protocols like PXE, NFS, or iSCSI to serve the OS and data remotely.

blips.name: dlt
blips.description:
Why?

dlt replaces heavy EL/ETL frameworks with pure Python pipeline code that handles schema evolution, state management, and incremental loads out of the box — making it the fastest way to ship reliable data ingestion pipelines from APIs, databases, or LLM outputs into warehouses like BigQuery, Snowflake, or DuckDB without managing infrastructure or writing transformation glue code.

Description

dlt (data load tool) is a lightweight, open-source Python library that lets you build declarative, self-evolving data pipelines with automatic schema inference, incremental loading, and built-in normalization — turning any Python data source into a production-ready pipeline with minimal boilerplate.

blips.name: n8n
blips.description:
Why?

Customizable and self-hosted automation platform. Great for automating personal tasks or complex business workflows without code .

Description

n8n is a free and open-source tool to connect services and automate tasks — like syncing databases, sending alerts, or triggering scripts.

blips.name: Drizzle ORM
blips.description:
Why?

Drizzle ORM is a new type-safe ORM for TypeScript that embraces SQL rather than hiding it. It provides both a fluent API and the ability to write raw SQL with safety guarantees, giving developers control and type inference.

Description

Drizzle ORM is a TypeScript ORM for SQL databases that is designed to be type-safe and flexible. It offers two ways to interact with the database: a relational object API and a SQL-like tagged template API, combining the familiarity of SQL with the safety of TypeScript.

blips.name: Druid
blips.description:
Why?

In the analytics DB category there are now a few options to choose from. This makes this category very interesting to watch as the industry has seen the benefits of solutions such as Druid. Apache Druid has emerged as the leader in this section as it is the most mature, stable, plugable and all round easy to use solution. Many companies have already embraces Druid as their solution and we recommend to keep it that way.

Description

Apache Druid is a real-time analytics database designed for fast analytics queries on large data sets. it  combines ideas from OLAP/analytic databases, timeseries databases, and search systems to create a unified system for operational analytics. Among their customers you can find companies such as Airbnb, ebay, Hulu and many more.

It has a Cloud-native architecture making it easy to deploy on K8s. Each functionality of this system can be separated into its own distributed service which provides for a scalable distributed system.

It supports Realtime or batch ingestion at very high rates either by its own methods or via external sources such as Kafka or Hadoop. Query latency is very low and is most suited for aggregation and reporting queries

blips.name: Port.io
blips.description:
Why?

Port is an emerging tool that promises to simplify and enhance the developer experience by centralizing resources and reducing cognitive load. It's worth trying out to see if it can effectively consolidate and streamline your development processes, although its long-term production viability is still being evaluated.

Description

Port.io is an internal developer platform that centralizes services, environments, ownership, and workflows into a single developer portal, built to standardize how teams ship and operate software.

blips.name: DuckDB
blips.description:
Why?

DuckDB is an open-source database designed to support analytical query workloads. It is simple to install and embed in the process, and it offers full SQL capabilities. DuckDB is suitable for both transactional and analytical workloads. Additionally, it is designed to be extensible, fast, and compatible across different platforms, making it an excellent choice for modern data-driven applications.

Description

DuckDB is an in-process SQL OLAP database management system. It is designed to work with big datasets all the while still being highly performant. It works with JSON, CSV, and PARQUET file formats, but community plugins support even more. The application of this tool is very versatile, but it is mostly used as a data analytics and processing tool, replacing complex systems like Apache Spark or Trino whenever applicable. It brings data analytics and processing to the laptop.

blips.name: LLM PR Review
blips.description:
Why?

It saves time on repetitive communication and makes pull requests clearer and faster to handle.

Description

Code review is a critical practice in software development that ensures quality, maintains standards, and facilitates knowledge sharing. LLM PR Review leverages large language models to automate aspects of this process, analyzing pull requests to identify potential bugs, security vulnerabilities, and coding standard violations. These AI-powered tools can provide contextual suggestions, explain complex code changes to team members, and highlight areas that need human attention—all while reducing the cognitive load on developers. By handling routine checks and providing intelligent insights, LLM PR Review tools such as PR Agent,Qudo, Code Rabbit, etc., streamline the development workflow, allowing human reviewers to focus on higher-level architectural considerations and complex logic issues that require deeper expertise and judgment.

blips.name: Robusta
blips.description:
Why?

The Robusta Kubernetes deployment tool simplifies cluster management and enhances deployment processes with automated troubleshooting and real-time monitoring. It empowers teams to deploy with confidence, reduce downtime, and optimize resource usage, making Kubernetes operations more efficient and reliable.

Description

Robusta is both an automations engine for Kubernetes, and a multi-cluster observability platform. Robusta is commonly used alongside Prometheus, but other tools are supported too. By listening to all the events in your cluster, Robusta can tell you why alerts fired, what happened at the same time, and what you can do about it. Robusta can either improve your existing alerts, or be used to define new alerts triggered by APIServer changes.

blips.name: SLSA
blips.description:
Why?

Artifact integrity has become a big issue when dealing with many repositories or many registries. with zero Trust policies this set of standards should help adopt tools that implement a policy that should cover all types of artifacts in one tool to analize Security vulnerabilities ahead of time due to this common standard

Description

SLSA is a set of standards and technical controls you can adopt to improve artifact integrity, and build towards completely resilient systems. It’s not a single tool, but a step-by-step outline to prevent artifacts being tampered with and tampered artifacts from being used, and at the higher levels, hardening up the platforms that make up a supply chain. These requirements are explained below, along with the rest of the essential specifications.

blips.name: Stackgres Database Operator
blips.description:
Why?

If we need a quick Postgres solution on K8S, this is an excellent approach to start with.

Description

StackGres is a fully-featured platform for running PostgreSQL on Kubernetes. Deploy in minutes an Enterprise-Grade Postgres-as-a-Service, in your infrastructure. 100% Open Source.

blips.name: Steampipe
blips.description:
Why?

Steampipe ready for production adoption. Solves key problems. Start using now.

Description

"select * from cloud;" Query cloud resources with SQL sentences. Steampipe exposes APIs and services as a high-performance relational database, giving you the ability to write SQL-based queries to explore dynamic data. Mods extend Steampipe's capabilities with dashboards, reports, and controls built with simple HCL.

blips.name: Electron
blips.description:
Why?

Electron has enabled countless cross-platform desktop applications using web technologies (including high-profile apps like VS Code, Slack, and Discord). It has a vast ecosystem and many years of stability.

Description

A framework for building cross-platform desktop applications using web technologies (HTML, CSS, JavaScript), combining Chromium and Node.js into a single runtime.

blips.name: Elementary
blips.description:
Why?

Elementary-data brings robust data observability to dbt projects, helping ensure data quality, reliability, and trust across modern data stacks. With built-in monitoring, anomaly detection, and alerting, Elementary makes it easy to catch issues like data freshness problems, schema changes, or unexpected volume shifts before they impact downstream consumers. It integrates seamlessly with dbt and modern data warehouses, providing clear, actionable insights without adding engineering overhead. As data pipelines scale, Elementary remains a lightweight yet powerful tool for maintaining confidence in your data.

Description

Electron is a framework for building desktop applications with web technologies (HTML, CSS, JS). It bundles a Chromium browser and Node.js runtime, allowing developers to create apps that run on Windows, macOS, and Linux from a single codebase.

blips.name: Embedding search
blips.description:
Why?

Advantages of embedding search:

  1. Semantic understanding – Finds results based on meaning, not just exact words.
  2. Handles synonyms – Matches “car” with “vehicle,” for example.
  3. Multilingual support – Can match meaning across languages.
  4. Works on any data – Useful for text, images, code, etc.
  5. Improved recall – Finds more relevant results even with vague or different phrasing.

Description

Embedding search is a technique used to find similar items (like documents, images, or products) based on their meaning or content, rather than just keyword matching. It works by converting data (like text) into vectors—numerical representations—using a process called embedding.

blips.name: es-toolkit
blips.description:
Why?

es-toolkit is a modern JavaScript utility library that positions itself as a successor to Lodash with far better performance and smaller bundle size.

Description

es-toolkit is a high-performance, modern JavaScript utility library for everyday functions. It is built to be fully tree-shakable and has robust TypeScript types for all its utilities.

blips.name: esbuild
blips.description:
Why?

Esbuild is much faster compared to alternatives such as Webpack or Rollup.

Description

An extremely fast JavaScript/TypeScript bundler and minifier written in Go, often 10-100x faster than alternatives like webpack or Parcel.

blips.name: Testkube
blips.description:
Why?

Testkube ready for production adoption. Solves key problems. Start using now.

Description

Testkube natively integrates test orchestration and execution into Kubernetes and your CI/CD/GitOps pipeline. It decouples test artifacts and execution from CI/CD tooling; tests are meant to be part of your clusters state and can be executed as needed.

blips.name: Zero Trust with Cloudflare
blips.description:
Why?

it’s safer, easier to scale, and cuts the friction of managing old-school VPNs.

Description

Cloudflare’s Zero Trust model: verifies every user/device and replaces VPNs for secure access.

blips.name: Express
blips.description:
Why?

Express.js remains the de facto web server framework for Node.js due to its minimalistic core and extensive middleware ecosystem. It’s well-known, stable, and many existing projects and libraries are built around it.

Description

Express is a fast, unopinionated web framework for Node.js. It provides basic mechanisms for routing and middleware in a web server, allowing developers to define endpoints and attach middleware functions for handling requests and responses.

blips.name: Local AI models over EKS using Nvidia: run:ai
blips.description:
Why?

Simplifies development over the infrastructure. Gives you full control over data and performance while leveraging Kubernetes scalability, and improves GPU utilization so you’re not wasting expensive resources.

Description

A Kubernetes-based platform for orchestrating GPU workloads on EKS, enabling teams to run and serve AI models efficiently with resource pooling, fractional GPU allocation, and job scheduling.

blips.name: FastAPI
blips.description:
Why?

We recommend starting to use FastAPI in any Python project that exposes a web server. It is a better alternative to Flask, which blocks every call. Its community is already big and growing fast.

Description

FastAPI is a python web framework based on Starette and Pydantic. This gives FastAPI its speed - it runs with AsyncIO. Implementing a web server with FastAPI is easy, fast coding and high performance.

blips.name: Fastify
blips.description:
Why?

Fastify is easy to use and offers great performance. It is a mature and stable project with a thriving ecosystem, making it a great choice for writing API servers

Description

Fast and low overhead web framework, for Node.js

blips.name: Feature Store
blips.description:
Why?

A feature store is an essential tool for organizations with multiple teams working on machine learning, as it enables efficient reuse of features, improves collaboration and consistency, provides governance and versioning, reduces redundant computation, and prevents data leakage issues.

Description

Feature Store is a database built specifically for the needs of Machine Learning projects. Its aim is to share features built for one model with other models. The centralized nature of model data allows multiple models to use the same features and reduce data engineering time and cost. The data is served in two ways: offline historical data for training and online latest-value data for prediction.  The data is divided into entities and each entity has multiple features, which are columns of data, stating current or accumulated data about the entity.

blips.name: Fine-tune LLM
blips.description:
Why?

Start using fine-tuned LLMs to tailor model behavior to your specific data and tasks, improving accuracy, relevance, and performance.

Description

The process of adapting a pre-trained large language model to a specific task or domain by continuing training on task-specific data, improving performance for specialized use cases.

blips.name: Flink 2.0
blips.description:
Why?

Flink 2.0's disaggregated state architecture decouples compute from state storage — making it significantly more cloud-native and cost-efficient for teams running large stateful streaming pipelines, while the unified API and PyFlink improvements lower the barrier for Python-first data teams who previously needed Scala/Java expertise to unlock Flink's full power.

Description

The next major version of Apache Flink, introducing improved SQL capabilities, enhanced state management, and better Kubernetes-native operations for stream processing.

blips.name: Flutter Web
blips.description:
Why?

Flutter Web allows us to reuse Flutter (Dart) code to target web browsers, meaning one codebase can serve mobile, desktop, and web. This “write once” approach is attractive for productivity.

Description

Flutter Web is an extension of the Flutter framework that compiles Dart code to web-friendly output (HTML, CSS, Canvas, and JavaScript). It allows Flutter apps to run in the browser, meaning the same UI code that builds a native mobile app can also produce a web app.

blips.name: MirrorD
blips.description:
Why?

Removes the need for constant redeployments during development by letting you test against real cluster conditions locally, which massively speeds up iteration.

Description

A tool for mirroring and synchronizing container images across registries, enabling air-gapped deployments and multi-cloud image distribution.

blips.name: Flyte
blips.description:
Why?

Flyte aims to manage business-critical ML and data processes at scale. You can use Flyte in deployment, maintenance, lifecycle management, version control, and training, and combine it with other platforms like Feast, PyTorch, Tensorflow, and whylogs to implement tasks pertaining to the complete model lifecycle

Description

Flyte is a Kubernetes-native workflow automation platform designed to enable the development, execution, and scaling of complex, computation-heavy processes across machine learning, data processing, and other operations.

blips.name: AWS Config - AWS Landing Zones
blips.description:
Why?

Ensures consistent governance and compliance across growing AWS environments, preventing configuration drift and reducing the risk of security gaps at scale.

Description

AWS-managed infrastructure templates that establish secure, multi-account AWS environments with governance guardrails, centralized logging, and compliance controls.

blips.name: (NSM) Network Service Mesh
blips.description:
Why?

NSM is taking the 7 layer approach we see in service meshes such as Istio in layers 2 & 3, this is mainly designed for multi cloud & multi cluster environments.

Description

Network Service Mesh (NSM) extends Kubernetes networking to handle complex L2/L3 use cases that the standard Kubernetes network model can't address, such as multi-cloud and telco workloads. It applies service mesh concepts to the network layer rather than the application layer.

blips.name: Airflow
blips.description:
Why?

Very few systems do not have the need for scheduling tasks. Airflow has become the main tool to solve this issue. Most could providers have a SAAS solution for airflow, so we will see it becoming even more mainstream.

Description

Airflow is today the most appreciated workflow engine in the distributed world. It allows building modular workflow with high scale, triggering, forking and joining and many more features. In addition, a good GUI that helps to audit the workflow.

This framework is run on Python, which makes it very attractive to DevOps groups.

The ramp-up seems easy in the beginning but requires deep knowledge on later phases. the solution is also based on other Python frameworks and databases for the queue management and databases, and for the webserver. Celery, RabbitMQ, MySQL or Postgres. Some drawbacks of this solution are the fact that all configuration is deployed and Python code. This may cause one bug to halt the whole of the server. Another problem with Python is the different versions that may be installed and updated on the different servers and may not be managed properly and cause bugs in Airflow itself.

blips.name: Ansible
blips.description:
Why?

Ansible is still the leading configuration tool when it is needed.

Description

Ansible is an open-source software provisioning, configuration management, and application-deployment tool enabling infrastructure as code.

blips.name: Argo Rollouts
blips.description:
Why?

This is a nice tool for advanced deployments. It supports blue-green, canary etc… and some more capabilities.

Description

Argo Rollouts is a Kubernetes controller and set of CRDs which provide advanced deployment capabilities such as blue-green, canary, canary analysis, experimentation, and progressive delivery features to Kubernetes.

blips.name: ArgoCD
blips.description:
Why?

If you want to control your application definitions, configurations, and environments, it should be declarative and version controlled. In addition, if you want automated application deployment and lifecycle management, use ArgoCD. ArgoCD is an easy tool to use, a very powerful tool, and has great visibility.

Description

Argo CD - Declarative GitOps CD for Kubernetes

This tool simplifies Apps deployment on K8S clusters. Its installation is easy, based on CDRs, it has a pretty fast learning curve to start using it in PROD. ArgoCD lives in your K8S cluster and can manage Apps deployment on a local and REMOTE cluster with no additional tools to be installed.

How it works Once installed, it tracks GIT repo with App deployment packages/manifests, it supports:

  • Kustomize
  • Helm
  • Ksonnet
  • Jsonnet

Detects whether local/remote cluster manifests are synced with GIT repo (by pooling GIT repo), in case there is a diff (image version, replica set changed, annotation added, etc.) - it will deploy the changes to the cluster.

In addition, it validates whether the entire app is healthy or not. In case someone somehow changed the app’s configuration on the cluster - the tool will restore its original state according to GIT repo. Thus, any change in-app configuration, version or setup, should be managed in GIT.

What else?

  • Great documentation with examples
  • Monitoring metrics exposed in Prometheus format
  • Roles and Policies management - in addition to 2 built-in roles (admin and read-only) there is an option to create your own!
  • SSO integration using DEX (OpenID, Google, GitHub, Okta, etc.)
  • Built-in backup/Restore tooling.

In addition to the CLI tool, it has very nice web UI which allows the same management possibilities.

blips.name: Go
blips.description:
Why?

Go isn't going away, but for data/AI engineering specifically, its lack of a mature ML/data ecosystem means Python dominates — making Go an awkward choice unless you're building infrastructure tooling or high-performance services.

Description

Gloo is an API Gateway and Ingress Controller that leverages Envoy Proxy to provide advanced traffic management, security, and observability features for microservices and serverless applications.

blips.name: Atlantis
blips.description:
Why?

This tool gives support for implementing pull request mechanism for Terraform changes. Which is a very good practice.

Description

Atlantis is an application for automating Terraform via pull requests. It is deployed as a standalone application into your infrastructure. No third-party has access to your credentials. Atlantis listens for GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket webhooks about Terraform pull requests. It then runs terraform plan and comments with the output back on the pull request. When you want to apply, comment atlantis apply on the pull request and Atlantis will run terraform apply and comment back with the output.

blips.name: Berglas
blips.description:
Why?

Managing secrets in Google using tools like Pulumi / Terraform is great for creating the secrets, but keeping them up2date is another thing. Berglas is a command-line tool and library for storing and retrieving secrets on Google Cloud. Berglas automates the process of encrypting, decrypting, and storing data on Google Cloud, you can use the CLI for administration or as a library in your infrastructure provisioning processes.

Description

Berglas is a command-line tool and library for storing and retrieving secrets on Google Cloud.Secrets are encrypted with Cloud KMS and stored in Cloud Storage As a CLI, Berglas automates the process of encrypting, decrypting, and storing data on Google Cloud.As a library, Berglas automates the inclusion of secrets into various Google Cloud runtimes

blips.name: Bitbucket Pipelines
blips.description:
Why?

A very powerful repo-oriented CI/CD tool, that is part of BitBucket.

Description

Bitbucket Pipelines is an integrated CI/CD service built into Bitbucket. It allows you to automatically build, test, and even deploy your code based on a configuration file in your repository. Essentially, we create containers in the cloud for you.

blips.name: Bitwarden
blips.description:
Why?

An easy and safe tool for teams and individuals to store and share sensitive data from any device.

Description

Bitwarden offers the easiest and safest way for teams and individuals to store and share sensitive data from any device.
