Bitwardern gives the full experience, starting with the fact it is OpenSource I can use their-saas version(they have a free account addition for personal use !), on the web (+browser extension), mobile-app Secure API & CLI, and the most important of all: All of your data is fully encrypted before it ever leaves your device, only you have access to it.  Not even the team at Bitwarden can read your data, even if they wanted to. data is sealed with end-to-end AES-256 bit encryption, salted hashing, and PBKDF2 SHA-256.

If in doubut you can run your own Biwarden tenant on your servers …

blips.name: Gradle
blips.description:
Why?

  • High performance
  • JVM foundation
  • Conventions
  • Extensibility
  • IDE support

Description

Gradle is a build tool. Following a build-by-convention approach, Gradle allows for declaratively modelling your problem domain using a powerful and expressive domain-specific language (DSL) implemented in Groovy instead of XML. Because Gradle is a JVM native, it allows you to write custom logic in the language you're most comfortable with, be it Java or Groovy. it too provides a powerful dependency management.

Although still many more developers use Maven (~60%) Gradle is a powerful contender/ally which needs to be considered when making the decision on which build tool to use.

The Android Studio build system is based on Gradle, and the Android Gradle plugin adds several features that are specific to building Android apps. 

Gradle is an open-source build automation tool that is designed to be flexible enough to build almost any type of software.

blips.name: BuildX
blips.description:
Why?

Extra features added like building against multiple nodes with multi-arch images concurrently, builder instances, building manifest lists, distributed caching, etc…

Description

Docker Buildx is a CLI plugin that extends the docker command with the full support of the features provided by Moby BuildKit builder toolkit.

blips.name: GraphQL
blips.description:
Why?

GraphQL has established itself as a powerful alternative to REST for APIs, enabling clients to request exactly the data they need and nothing more.

Description

GraphQL is a query language and runtime for APIs that allows clients to specify precisely what data they want from a server. Unlike REST, which might require multiple endpoints or round-trips, GraphQL uses a single endpoint and a schema that defines types and relationships.

blips.name: GraphRAG
blips.description:
Why?

GraphRAG enhances traditional RAG pipelines by structuring retrieved knowledge as a graph, enabling deeper reasoning, better context linking, and more accurate answers from language models. By capturing relationships between entities and concepts, GraphRAG helps models navigate complex information, reduce redundancy, and maintain coherence in multi-step queries. It’s especially valuable for domains like research, finance, and enterprise knowledge management, where understanding how facts connect is as important as retrieving them.

Description

GraphRAG is a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework that leverages a graph-based approach to enhance information retrieval and integration for text generation tasks. By incorporating relational knowledge from graphs, it improves the relevance and coherence of generated responses.

blips.name: Great Expectations
blips.description:
Why?

It’s declarative, flexible and extensible. Provides a rich vocabulary for data quality. Renders tests directly into clean, human-readable documentation. Your documentation is guaranteed to never go stale. Many tools like data catalogs or data ingestion pipelines already use the library for data profiling and quality assurance.

Description

Great Expectations helps data teams eliminate pipeline debt, through data testing, documentation, and profiling.

blips.name: Cert-manager (jetstack)
blips.description:
Why?

A major use case is an automated issuance and renewal of Let’s Encrypt certificate, using ACME, to secure Ingress with TLS.

Description

A Kubernetes add-on that automates the management and issuance of TLS certificates from various certificate authorities, including Let's Encrypt, HashiCorp Vault, and Venafi.

blips.name: GSAP
blips.description:
Why?

high-performance, timeline-based complex web animations.

Description

GreenSock Animation Platform, a professional-grade JavaScript animation library for creating high-performance, timeline-based animations in web applications.

blips.name: Cilium
blips.description:
Why?

If we need security and observing network connectivity between containers, this is a very good option.

Description

Cilium is an eBPF-based Kubernetes CNI that provides high-performance networking, security policies, load balancing, and observability for cloud-native workloads.

blips.name: CircleCI
blips.description:
Why?

CI/CD solution which integrates greatly with Github. Well documented, extensible and configurable. Can run managed and self-hosted. Allows debug pipelines with SSH. First-class Docker support and good caching system for speed-up builds.

Description

CircleCI: Continuous Integration and Deliveryhttps://circleci.com

blips.name: Hasura
blips.description:
Why?

Hasura is dramatically accelerates backend development by auto-generating a real-time GraphQL API over databases, reducing the need for custom server code. It supports fine-grained access control, event-driven workflows, and seamless integration with REST, GraphQL, and serverless functions—making it ideal for rapidly building scalable, secure applications. As projects grow, Hasura continues to offer flexibility, performance, and developer productivity without sacrificing control or extensibility.

Description

The Hasura GraphQL Engine is an open-source fast GraphQL server that gives you instant, real-time GraphQL APIs over several databases, with webhook triggers on database events, and remote schemas.

blips.name: Headless UI components
blips.description:
Why?

Headless UI libraries provide the functionality and accessibility of common components without enforcing any visual styling.

Description

Headless UI components are unstyled, logic-only components that manage state, accessibility (ARIA roles, keyboard navigation), and behavior for user interface patterns.

blips.name: Clair
blips.description:
Why?

This tool is mainly used to reveal vulnerabilities in containers. In regular intervals, Clair ingests vulnerability metadata from a configured set of sources and stores it in the database.

Clair usage is easy to integrate into CI Flow and is open source.

Description

Clair (French term - clear, bright, transparent) CoreOS project. Static analysis of vulnerabilities in application containers

This tool enables to reveal vulnerabilities in container images. Clair usage is easy to integrate into CI Flow and is open source. Vulnerabilities metadata are continuously stored in a database and exposed by Clair API. These vulnerabilities are ingested by Clair from a set of sources. Container images are indexed during the scan ; A list of revealed vulnerabilities-features in the image are stored in a local database. Each new Clair API request perform quicker because of it.No need to rescan already known images. When updates to vulnerability metadata occur, a notification can be sent to alert systems that a change has occurred. Integration of such tool in CI Flows is very needed and Clair is a great choice to the open source community.

blips.name: Hono
blips.description:
Why?

A high-performance, middleware-centric web framework optimized for Edge computing and Bun runtimes.

Description

Hono is a fast, lightweight web framework that runs on any JavaScript runtime: Node.js, Deno, Bun, or even edge environments like Cloudflare Workers. It has an API similar to Express/Koa (with middleware and context objects) but is extremely minimal and optimized.

blips.name: Hugging Face Transformers
blips.description:
Why?

Hugging Face Transformers remains the undisputed standard for accessing, fine-tuning, and deploying open-source models — with the largest model hub, deepest framework integrations, and most active community in the ML ecosystem.

Description

Hugging Face's Transformers is an open-source library designed for natural language processing tasks, offering pre-trained models for applications like text generation, sentiment analysis, and translation. It supports seamless integration with popular frameworks such as TensorFlow and PyTorch. The library simplifies the implementation of advanced NLP models by providing easy-to-use APIs. It also fosters collaboration and innovation through its extensive model hub and active community.

blips.name: Infrastructure as Code (IaC)
blips.description:
Why?

IaC remains essential for enabling consistent and scalable deployment environments in DevOps practices.

Description

Infrastructure as Code (IaC) is the practice of managing and provisioning infrastructure — servers, networks, databases, load balancers, and other cloud resources — through machine-readable configuration files rather than manual processes or interactive tools.

blips.name: Cloud FaaS
blips.description:
Why?

In case you need quick development, with scale support and pay as you use.

Description

AWS was the first provider to offer "functions as a service" already in AWS initially released AWS lambda as an event-driven provisioning/operations and took just under 3 years to become the standard name of serverless and FaaS offerings.

AWS, as it’s competitors, offer Lambdas (a.k.a functions), as a complementary to their BaaS offerings, stitching together services such as:  Incognito  S3  CloudFormation  DynamoDB  RDS and many more These integrations alongside Lambda’s “infinite” scalability and it’s newly introduced (at the time) “Price per 100ms” made it very popular among both startups achieving their MVP and enterprises wishing to scale out or experiment with Serverless and Micro Services Architectures. AWS Lambda provides many organizations the ability to write functions in a variety of Software languages and integrates well with many frameworks and other IaaS/PaaS/BaaS services.

More about AWS Lambda here

Google functions enable Serverless applications based on GCP IaaS offerings. Cloud Functions lets application developers spin up code on demand in response to events originating from any API / HTTP request. Serverless architectures utilizing Google Functions integrated with Google Endpoints and BaaS services could build applications that scale from zero to infinity, on-demand - without provisioning or managing a single server.

As other serverless and function providers, google’s functions are the best fitted for Backend services such as Firebase, Cloud Datastore, and ML solutions also offered by the GCP.

More info on google functions in the following

blips.name: Cluster API
blips.description:
Why?

Kubernetes is a complex system that relies on several components being configured correctly to have a working cluster. Cluster API simplifies the bootstrapping process by providing a single tool to address a set of common overlapping installation concerns, using kubeadm as the underlying bootstrapping tool.

Description

Cluster API is a Kubernetes sub-project focused on providing declarative APIs and tooling to simplify provisioning, upgrading, and operating multiple Kubernetes clusters supporting different infrastructure/bootstrap providers (AWS, Azure, GCP, vSphere, etc.). Cluster API project uses Kubernetes-style APIs and patterns to automate cluster creation, configuration and management. The supporting infrastructure, like virtual machines, networks, load balancers, and VPCs, as well as the Kubernetes cluster configuration are all defined as manifest like any other Kubernetes resource.

blips.name: Inngest
blips.description:
Why?

Inngest replaces the fragile DIY stack of queues + workers + retry logic with a developer-friendly SDK where durability, observability, and step-level retries are built in — making it the fastest path to production-grade background jobs and event-driven workflows for teams who don't want to operate Temporal or Celery themselves.

Description

Inngest is an event-driven workflow and background job platform that lets you write durable, retriable, multi-step functions in TypeScript or Python — triggered by events, schedules, or webhooks — without managing queues, workers, or infrastructure.

blips.name: confd
blips.description:
Why?

Templating your app’s configuration with confd, is a lightweight configuration management tool focused on: keeping local configuration files up-to-date using data stored in remote values providers and processing template resources. reloading applications to pick up new config file changes.

Description

Template your app’s configuration with confd Is a lightweight configuration management tool focused on: keeping local configuration files up-to-date using data stored in remote values providers and processing template resources. reloading applications to pick up new config file changes

Purpose Detach environment related configuration management from application code. This means that the app source repo will contain configuration files templates that fill be used to generate config files using external values providers at deployment time.

confd supports the following value stores:

  • etcd
  • consul
  • dynamodb
  • redis
  • vault
  • zookeeper
  • aws ssm parameter store
  • system environment variables yaml files

This tool can: Create environment-related config files at the deployment stage Can watch for changes in “value store”, update configuration and perform an action (reload the config, restart the app, etc.) It’s written in golang and all it’s templating is based on go-templates

blips.name: containerd
blips.description:
Why?

The Docker manager of CNCF officially from Feb 2019.

Description

containerd is available as a daemon for Linux and Windows. It manages the complete container lifecycle of its host system, from image transfer and storage to container execution and supervision to low-level storage to network attachments and beyond.

blips.name: Jasmine
blips.description:
Why?

Jasmine was a pioneering JavaScript testing framework, but newer testing ecosystems have largely superseded it. Jest, for example, incorporates Jasmine’s syntax with additional features and runs tests faster (without needing a browser).

Description

Jasmine is a behavior-driven testing framework for JavaScript. It provides a global describe/it syntax for structuring tests and built-in assertion functions to validate expected outcomes.

blips.name: Java
blips.description:
Why?

We recommend using this language as it has one of the largest eco-systems of any language, a vibrant community and it is actively maintained. It is very versatile, easy to use and learn and fits many applications.

  • The original language that Android was built in
  • many examples and libraries still use Java

Description

Robust, Age Proven, and Renewing The Java language although being with us already for a long time is renewing itself. Starting from Java 9 we now see a new version of Java every 6 months. This means more features much faster. I still believe that using Java gives a very strict and obvious structure to the program which is sometimes lacking in other programming languages.

Framework Support The rise if Reactive Frameworks (Vert.x, Spring Reactor and others) and Micro frameworks (Spark Java, javalite, ligth4k) make java very versatile in its use and use cases. With the above-mentioned frameworks, we can now easily program reactive systems and microservices with a minimal footprint. Java is always going with the Trends (although sometimes a bit behind) as we can see with Docker support in the JVM just recently.

The Java community is a huge community one which cannot be neglected.

blips.name: Java 17 LTS
blips.description:
Why?

Java v23 is out and there's no reason to keep using old versions.

Description

Java 17 was released on 14 September 2021. This is the latest LTS version and should be adopted as the last LTS version, Java 11 has already been announced as EOL for 30 Sep 2023.

blips.name: Contour
blips.description:
Why?

Contour ingress, use Envoy, Have the HttpProxy CRD's with allow, set HTTP header in ingress level (good support for multi-tenant, etc .. ), Contour Load Balancer support retry, rate Limit, and more…

Description

Contour is an Ingress controller for Kubernetes that works by deploying the Envoy proxy as a reverse proxy and load balancer. Contour supports dynamic configuration updates out of the box while maintaining a lightweight profile. Contour also introduces a new ingress API (HTTPProxy) which is implemented via a Custom Resource Definition (CRD). Its goal is to expand upon the functionality of the Ingress API to allow for a richer user experience as well as solve shortcomings in the original design.

blips.name: Crossplane
blips.description:
Why?

Crossplane is another way to manage your infrastructure (including Kubernetes clusters and managed cloud services) from a single point using unified "language". It aims to enable kubectl as one-stop shop for everything infrastructure and the kubernetes yaml resource descriptor - the only language you need.

Description

Crossplane is an open-source Kubernetes add-on that lets you provision and manage cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, Azure) using Kubernetes manifests and GitOps workflows. It turns your cluster into a universal control plane for any infrastructure resource.

blips.name: Jenkins
blips.description:
Why?

Jenkins' XML-based config, plugin hell, and steep maintenance burden make it a legacy relic compared to modern CI/CD platforms like GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or Tekton that offer better DX and cloud-native integration.

Description

The leading open source automation server, Jenkins provides hundreds of plugins to support building, deploying and automating any project

blips.name: Crunchydata Database Operator
blips.description:
Why?

Designed for your GitOps workflows, it is easy to get started with Postgres on Kubernetes with PGO. Within a few moments, you can have a production-grade Postgres cluster complete with high availability, disaster recovery, and monitoring, all over secure TLS communications. Even better, PGO lets you easily customize your Postgres cluster to tailor it to your workload!

Description

PGO, the Postgres Operator from Crunchy Data, gives you a declarative Postgres solution that automatically manages your PostgreSQL clusters.

blips.name: DevSpaces
blips.description:
Why?

With DevSpaces, you can just click from Github to start your Dev Environments. Click to code in just seconds.

Description

DevSpace is a Kubernetes development tool that lets developers build, deploy, sync code, and debug applications directly inside a cluster for faster local development workflows.

blips.name: Jupyter Lab
blips.description:
Why?

Jupyter notebook is the most go-to platform when it comes to performing data analysis or performing data science-intense data preprocessing, EDA and data visualizations. Jupyter also supports Big data tools such as Apache Spark for data analytics needs. Jupyter Notebook integration available in PyCharm, VSCode and many more.

Description

The next-generation web-based interface for Project Jupyter, offering a flexible, modular environment for notebooks, code, data, and interactive outputs.

blips.name: Dex
blips.description:
Why?

When you want to add user management to Kubernetes Dex can be the tool with the integration to external authentication providers. like Active Directory…

Description

Dex is an identity service that uses OpenID Connect to drive authentication for other apps. Dex acts as a portal to other identity providers through “connectors.” This lets dex defer authentication to LDAP servers, SAML providers, or established identity providers like GitHub, Google, and Active Directory. Clients write their authentication logic once to talk to dex, then dex handles the protocols for a given backend.

blips.name: Docker Compose
blips.description:
Why?

Is the most common and easy to use for running and managing multiple dockers, for development usage, and for the deployment of applications that run on a single node.

Description

Docker Compose is a tool for defining and running multi-container Docker applications. With Compose, you use a YAML file to configure your application’s services. Then, with a single command, you create and start all the services from your configuration.

blips.name: Druid
blips.description:
Why?

In the analytics DB category there are now a few options to choose from. This makes this category very interesting to watch as the industry has seen the benefits of solutions such as Druid. Apache Druid has emerged as the leader in this section as it is the most mature, stable, plugable and all round easy to use solution. Many companies have already embraces Druid as their solution and we recommend to keep it that way.

Description

Apache Druid is a real-time analytics database designed for fast analytics queries on large data sets. it  combines ideas from OLAP/analytic databases, timeseries databases, and search systems to create a unified system for operational analytics. Among their customers you can find companies such as Airbnb, ebay, Hulu and many more.

It has a Cloud-native architecture making it easy to deploy on K8s. Each functionality of this system can be separated into its own distributed service which provides for a scalable distributed system.

It supports Realtime or batch ingestion at very high rates either by its own methods or via external sources such as Kafka or Hadoop. Query latency is very low and is most suited for aggregation and reporting queries

blips.name: ECS
blips.description:
Why?

ECS is a proven, robust solution for container orchestration with seamless integration into the AWS ecosystem. It supports scalable, reliable, and secure deployment of containerized applications. Given its maturity and the extensive support and documentation provided by AWS, it is a tool worth keeping in your stack.

Description

Amazon Elastic Container Service is a fully managed container orchestration service that runs Docker containers on AWS, supporting both EC2 and Fargate launch types.

blips.name: EKS Blueprints
blips.description:
Why?

EKS becomes a commodity tool, where peripheral solutions are just simple configurations. In short, if we like to quickly bring up a full cluster, with the common "plugins" like ingress controller, etc.. This is an excellent tool for that.

Description

Amazon ECS is a fully managed container orchestration service provided by AWS. It allows you to run and manage Docker containers on a cluster of Amazon EC2 instances or using AWS Fargate for serverless compute.

blips.name: Kafka
blips.description:
Why?

Kafka is a reliable tool to quickly ingest data and serve it forward, with the addition of tools such as KSQL and Kafka streams Kafka is becoming a more comprehensive platform for a data platform.

Description

Apache Kafka is a distributed event streaming platform for high-throughput, fault-tolerant message processing. It enables publish-subscribe messaging, durable log-based storage, and real-time stream processing, making it the backbone of modern event-driven architectures.

blips.name: Kafka Connect
blips.description:
Why?

We think this eco-system is good for places where small/medium amount of data needs to be streamed to Kafka with minimum configuration.

Description

Kafka Connect is a framework for streaming data between Apache Kafka and external systems using pre-built connectors. Source connectors import data into Kafka; sink connectors export data out. It's configuration-driven with no custom code required for common integrations.

blips.name: Kafka Queues
blips.description:
Why?

Kafka Queues eliminates the need for separate queuing systems like SQS or RabbitMQ alongside Kafka — teams already on Kafka can handle both streaming and task queue workloads on a single platform, reducing infrastructure sprawl and operational overhead.

Description

Kafka Queues (KIP-932) adds native point-to-point queue semantics to Apache Kafka, allowing messages to be consumed exactly once by a single consumer in a group — without managing partition assignments or consumer group rebalancing. It simplifies use cases like task queues and work distribution that previously required workarounds on top of Kafka's log-based model.

blips.name: eks-node-viewer
blips.description:
Why?

A simple and tiny weight tool to get an immediate look on node current RAM and CPU usage, and get a picture of current utilization.

Description

eks-node-viewer is a tool for visualizing dynamic node usage within a cluster. It was originally developed as an internal tool at AWS for demonstrating consolidation with Karpenter. It displays the scheduled pod resource requests vs the allocatable capacity on the node. It does not look at the actual pod resource usage.

blips.name: Karma
blips.description:
Why?

Karma is a browser-based test runner that was essential in the past, but it tends to run tests slower and with more complexity compared to headless approaches now available.

Description

Karma is a test runner that launches real browsers (Chrome, Firefox, etc.) to run JavaScript tests, reporting the results back to the developer. It acts as a bridge between your tests and multiple browser environments, making it possible to ensure code works in each target browser.

blips.name: eksctl
blips.description:
Why?

Eksctl is a very useful CLI, for maintaining and managing AWS EKS.

Description

eksctl - eks command line utility

blips.name: Event-Driven Architecture
blips.description:
Why?

The kye for Automation is Event-driven.

Description

An extremely fast bundler for the web

blips.name: Everything as Code
blips.description:
Why?

As we see it, this practice is necessary for every product we develop these days. The ability to track changes, deploy, etc …

Description

“Everything as Code” is the practice of managing all the parts of the application In SCM and automate the execution of it, Include configuration, Infrastructure, security. This practice gives us:

  • Traceability: All in SCM
  • Repeatable: We can recreate every part
  • Testability: We can test the change and the infra creation

blips.name: Keycloak
blips.description:
Why?

Keycloak supports SAML, OpenID Connect, OAuth2 standards to provide SSO, Identity Broker, and more. Keycloak is extendable for customized authentication flows and UI themes. It is one of the best identity management out there.

Description

An open-source identity and access management solution providing single sign-on (SSO), user federation, identity brokerage, and social login with support for OAuth 2.0, SAML, and OpenID Connect.

blips.name: External Secrets Operator
blips.description:
Why?

As the trend moves to declarative, k8s operators should stay with us.

Description

A Kubernetes operator that synchronizes secrets from external secret management systems (AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault, Azure Key Vault) into Kubernetes Secret objects.

blips.name: Koa
blips.description:
Why?

Koa, developed by the team behind Express, uses modern JavaScript features (async/await) to simplify middleware and avoid callback hell.

Description

Koa is a minimalist web framework for Node.js that leverages async functions for cleaner, promise-free code.

blips.name: ExternalDNS
blips.description:
Why?

The end with manually manage and update DNS servers with changes in our K8S ingresses.

Description

External Secrets Operator is a Kubernetes operator that integrates external secret management systems like AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault, Google Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault and many more. The operator reads information from external APIs and automatically injects the values into a Kubernetes Secret.

blips.name: Flagger
blips.description:
Why?

Like other Progressive Delivery tools, Flagger improves the release of applications by supporting release strategies based on metrics and testing.

Description

Flagger is a progressive delivery tool that automates the release process for applications running on Kubernetes. It reduces the risk of introducing a new software version in production by gradually shifting traffic to the new version while measuring metrics and running conformance tests.Flagger implements several deployment strategies (Canary releases, A/B testing, Blue/Green mirroring) and integrates with various Kubernetes ingress controllers, service mesh and monitoring solutions. Flagger is a Cloud Native Computing Foundation project and part of Flux family of GitOps tools

blips.name: Flux CD
blips.description:
Why?

As GitOps becomes more and more popular, this is one of the best GitOps tools.

Description

GitOps tool - Flux and Flagger deploy apps with canaries, feature flags, and A/B rollouts. Flux can also manage any Kubernetes resource. Infrastructure and workload dependency management is built in.

blips.name: GitHub Actions
blips.description:
Why?

A robust ci/cd out of the bix tool, that is repo oriented in Github.

Description

GitHub Actions makes it easy to automate all your software workflows, now with world-class CI/CD. Build, test, and deploy your code right from GitHub. Make code reviews, branch management, and issue triaging work the way you want.

blips.name: Kubeflow
blips.description:
Why?

Kubeflow is an ideal choice for orchestrating machine learning workflows due to its ability to seamlessly integrate with Kubernetes. It simplifies the deployment, scaling, and management of complex machine learning models and pipelines, enabling data scientists and engineers to focus on development without worrying about infrastructure.

Description

Kubeflow is a framework for deploying ML workflows on Kubernetes cluster. It is based on Argo Workflow and provides a Python API to easily create Argo workflows without the need to write YAML files. Kubeflow include all the ingredients for a full ML development: research with JupyterLabs, training and experimenting via pipelines and model lifecycle management.

blips.name: GitHub Package Registry
blips.description:
Why?

GitHub Package Registry provides you with one centralized place to host and manage both your sources and packages. It's compatible with common package management tools and supports various types of packages. Easily integrated with GitHub APIs, GitHub Actions, and webhooks to create an end-to-end DevOps workflow that includes your code, CI, and deployment solutions.

Description

GitHub's integrated package hosting service supporting npm, Maven, NuGet, Docker, and RubyGems, with native GitHub Actions integration for CI/CD workflows.

blips.name: Kubernetes
blips.description:
Why?

The war of leading the container orchestration market seem to be dominated by Kubernetes and it’s fast growing ecosystem and standards. Alongside the standards of OCI, CNI, CSI and others we now have a platform which encourages extendability. In the past 5 years we've witnessed Operators and Controllers which take Kubernetes core values  and solve many long living problems such as stability, extendability and most importantly maintainability. A few key examples inspired by CNCF projects like:

  • Workflow and pipelines like Argo and Tekton, that can be used for data pipelines and CI/CD
  • ClusterApi and Crossplane for the creation and management of infrastructure
  • ArgoCD, Flux GitOps implementation as Kubernetes deployment tools
  • K3s and others for edge-computing
  • Kube Bench for security checks
  • Kube Cost for FinOps   These Are just a few examples why we name this trend the “Kubernetes platform”

Description

Kubernetes is an open-source container orchestration system for automating software deployment, scaling, and management. Google originally designed Kubernetes, but the Cloud Native Computing Foundation now maintains the project.

blips.name: GitLab CI
blips.description:
Why?

GitLab CI/CD pipeline is a great tool to integrate with the GitLab suite. Very easy to use with lots of predefined templates.

Description

GitHub Package Registry is a software package hosting service, similar to npmjs.org, rubygems.org, or hub.docker.com, which allows you to develop your code and host your packages in one place. You can host software packages privately or publicly and use them as dependencies in your projects.

GitHub Package Registry uses the native package tooling commands you’re already familiar with to publish, query, download, and change package versions and currently supports the following clients and formats: npm, gem, mvn, docker and nugat.

This approach can be useful when you want to host deployed artifacts next to their sources or when an artifact repository is unavailable or you don’t want to maintain one.

blips.name: GitOps
blips.description:
Why?

Terms like: Efficiency, Reliability, Stability, Consistency, Integrity, Cost-effectiveness, Developing fluency, and Productivity are all included once we implement the GitOps way.

Description

GitOps Is it possible to describe our applications, deployments, versioning, releases, changes over time only with code?   Is it possible easily and integrally recover, a rollback in a declarative manner?   Is it possible to manage such environments without the need to run any command at all, git commits will be enough?   GitOps today is a set of practices that enable us to do it.   In the same way we excepted and implemented the concept "Infrastructure As Code", we except these days the concept GitOps. Git a single source of truth for declarative infrastructure and applications   With Git at the center of your delivery pipelines, developers can make pull requests to accelerate and simplify application deployments and    a lot of the operations tasks Main GitOps Key Benefits

  • Continuous deployment productivity and integrability is greater
  • Environmental control is enhanced by the developer by pushing code
  • All cluster changes are logged. Stability is improved
  • A single source of truth, Higher reliability from Git’s built-in revert/rollback
  • end-to-end workflows consistency and standardization

Some Tools that helps us to implement GitOps practices:

  • ArgoCD
  • Flux
  • GitKube
  • JenkinsX
  • Helm Operator
  • wksctl

blips.name: Goldilocks - VPA
blips.description:
Why?

This robust tool helps to estimate the resource limit and the request needed for each pod. Be aware that this tool uses VPA and validates the VPA is in Recommender mode.

Description

Goldilocks is a utility that can help you identify a starting point for resource requests and limits. By using the kubernetes vertical-pod-autoscaler (opens new window)in recommendation mode, we can see a suggestion for resource requests on each of our apps. This tool creates a VPA for each workload in a namespace and then queries them for information.

blips.name: Google Config Connector
blips.description:
Why?

Google config connector allows you to manage Google Cloud resources through Kubernetes manifest and avoid using provisioning tools like Terraform.

Description

Config Connector is a Kubernetes addon that allows you to manage Google Cloud resources through Kubernetes.

blips.name: Gradle
blips.description:
Why?

Gradle is still here as a robust tool for JVM builds.

Description

Gradle is a build tool. Following a build-by-convention approach, Gradle allows for declaratively modelling your problem domain using a powerful and expressive domain-specific language (DSL) implemented in Groovy instead of XML. Because Gradle is a JVM native, it allows you to write custom logic in the language you're most comfortable with, be it Java or Groovy. it too provides a powerful dependency management.

Although still many more developers use Maven (~60%) Gradle is a powerful contender/ally which needs to be considered when making the decision on which build tool to use.

The Android Studio build system is based on Gradle, and the Android Gradle plugin adds several features that are specific to building Android apps. 

Gradle is an open-source build automation tool that is designed to be flexible enough to build almost any type of software.

blips.name: LakeFS
blips.description:
Why?

LakeFS is included due to its innovative approach to data versioning and management, addressing challenges in handling large-scale data across distributed environments.

Description

LakeFS provides a git-like approach to manage data versions. Branching, merges, commits and reverts for large datasets

  • Provides ACID transactions
  • Uses S3 and GCS for storage
  • Format agnostic
  • Supporting very large data lakes
  • On prem and SaaS

blips.name: Lakehouse
blips.description:
Why?

Keep using a Lakehouse to simplify your data stack, reduce duplication, and enable real-time analytics and AI on a single, scalable platform.

Description

A Lakehouse is a unified data architecture that combines the scalability of data lakes with the structure and performance of data warehouses, enabling both analytical and machine learning workloads on the same data platform.

blips.name: LlamaIndex
blips.description:
Why?

Keep using LlamaIndex because it provides a powerful and flexible framework for connecting large language models (LLMs) to external data sources, enabling more accurate and context-aware responses. With features like structured data ingestion, customizable retrieval pipelines, and evaluation tools, LlamaIndex helps developers build robust, production-ready RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) systems. As LLM use cases expand, LlamaIndex remains a reliable foundation for managing context, ensuring data relevance, and scaling intelligent applications efficiently.

Description

LlamaIndex is an open-source data orchestration framework for building context-augmented LLM applications. It handles ingesting, indexing, and querying data from diverse sources, making it a popular foundation for RAG pipelines.

blips.name: LangChain
blips.description:
Why?

Teams should keep using LangChain this year because it continues to be a leading framework for building complex, production-grade applications powered by large language models (LLMs). With its modular architecture, LangChain simplifies integrating components like retrieval, tools, agents, memory, and external APIs—all while supporting both open-source and proprietary models. It also offers strong ecosystem support, including LangSmith for debugging and evaluation, and growing compatibility with vector databases, model providers, and orchestration tools. As LLM-powered apps mature, LangChain remains a flexible, well-supported foundation for rapid prototyping and scalable deployment.

Description

LangChain is a framework for developing applications powered by language models.

blips.name: Langfuse
blips.description:
Why?

Use Langfuse to gain deep visibility into their LLM-powered applications through structured observability, evaluation, and analytics. LangFuse helps track prompts, responses, latency, and performance metrics across the entire LLM pipeline, making it easier to debug, optimize, and improve AI-driven features. With support for both manual and automated feedback, A/B testing, and prompt versioning, it empowers teams to build more reliable and effective LLM applications faster and with confidence.

Description

Langfuse is an open-source LLM (large language model) engineering platform that helps teams collaboratively build, debug, and iterate on complex applications powered by generative AI models like GPT. It provides features like: Traces, evals, prompt management and metrics to debug and improve your LLM application.

blips.name: LangGraph
blips.description:
Why?

Start using LangGraph to build stateful, multi-step LLM applications with dynamic control flow using a flexible graph-based architecture.

Description

LangGraph is a library built on top of LangChain that enables developers to create stateful, multi-step LLM applications using graph-based workflows. It allows for defining complex control flows, such as loops, branches, and conditional logic, by modeling conversations or tasks as nodes and edges in a graph. LangGraph is particularly useful for building agentic systems, multi-turn interactions, or dynamic decision-making processes where state and context need to persist across steps.

blips.name: LangSmith
blips.description:
Why?

its tracing and eval tooling is mature, the UI is polished, and it significantly cuts debugging time for complex multi-step LLM pipelines.

Description

A developer platform from LangChain for debugging, testing, evaluating, and monitoring LLM applications, providing observability into chains, agents, and retrieval pipelines.

blips.name: Grafana
blips.description:
Why?

Grafana is mature and the "go-to dashboard" framework And included in many frameworks such as Prometheus.

Description

Grafana’s motto is “The analytics platform for all your metrics”, in the past ~5 years or so Granfana has done just that, becoming a centralized hub of data processing and visualization. Grafana has a big Datasource variety supported, enabling processing and real-time visualization of time series data originating from many data sources simultaneously. From traditional databases such as MySql and Postgresql and to time series databases such as OpenTSDB, Graphite, Prometheus, Elasticsearch, and others.

Grafana also provides an extensible plugin interface adding the ability to enrich both visualizations with plugins or custom “data sources”.

The Suger Coating of Grafana is the Grafana community website, which maintains a centralized hub for hosting "plugins" and "dashboard" which the community can download & manage via source control. In many cases, there is either a ready dashboard for your use case or at least a good starting point.

Grafana also supports an HA installation method, authentication [Basic/LDAP/OAuth/etc] & authorization schemes and organization management. Read more

blips.name: Lit-Element, lit html
blips.description:
Why?

Lit (formerly LitElement and lit-html) provides a simple way to build Web Components with efficient rendering.

Description

Lit is a library for building Web Components using a declarative template syntax and reactive properties. It consists of lit-html (for efficient templating) and a lightweight base class that simplifies defining custom elements.

blips.name: LiteLLM
blips.description:
Why?

LiteLLM is a lightweight, fast, and efficient framework for running large language models. It's designed to be easy to use, allowing developers to quickly deploy and integrate language models into applications without the overhead of complex infrastructure. It's particularly useful for creating cost-effective, high-performance solutions with simpler setup and management compared to other frameworks.

Description

Python SDK, Proxy Server (LLM Gateway) to call 100+ LLM APIs in OpenAI format - [Bedrock, Azure, OpenAI, VertexAI, Cohere, Anthropic, Sagemaker, HuggingFace, Replicate, Groq]

blips.name: Llama
blips.description:
Why?

Open weights, serious brains. LLaMA gives developers and DevOps high-performance LLMs to run locally, fine-tune, or build on — no strings attached. If you want cutting-edge AI without cloud dependency, start here.

Description

LLaMA (Large Language Model Meta AI) is Meta’s open-source family of powerful language models, designed to rival the best in the field — but freely available to run locally. From LLaMA 2 to the newly optimized LLaMA 3, these models deliver top-tier performance for code, reasoning, and language tasks without vendor lock-in. Whether you're deploying in production or hacking in your terminal, LLaMA gives DevOps and developers full control over their AI stack. It’s the foundation for many fine-tuned models (like Code LLaMA) and a go-to choice for those who want speed, quality, and flexibility on their own terms.

blips.name: LLM
blips.description:
Why?

LLMs are pivotal in the AI space for their transformative impact on natural language processing and generation, deserving early adoption and in-depth experimentation.

Description

Large Language Models are advanced AI models capable of understanding and generating human-like text, driving new frontiers in AI interactions. Models such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek and Llama

blips.name: LLM OpenSource Models
blips.description:
Why?

Companies should start using open-source LLMs because they offer greater control, customization, and cost-efficiency compared to proprietary models. With open-source models, businesses can fine-tune the AI on their own data, ensuring better relevance and performance for their specific use cases—while keeping sensitive information secure within their infrastructure. They also avoid vendor lock-in and can adapt the technology at their own pace, benefiting from a growing community of contributors and rapid innovation without the high costs of closed platforms.

Description

Open-source large language models like Llama, Mistral, Falcon, and BLOOM that can be self-hosted, fine-tuned, and deployed without vendor lock-in or API costs.

blips.name: LLM PR Review
blips.description:
Why?

Code review is a critical practice in software development that ensures quality, maintains standards, and facilitates knowledge sharing. LLM PR Review leverages large language models to automate aspects of this process, analyzing pull requests to identify potential bugs, security vulnerabilities, and coding standard violations. These AI-powered tools can provide contextual suggestions, explain complex code changes to team members, and highlight areas that need human attention—all while reducing the cognitive load on developers. By handling routine checks and providing intelligent insights, LLM PR Review tools streamline the development workflow, allowing human reviewers to focus on higher-level architectural considerations and complex logic issues that require deeper expertise and judgment.

Description

Code review is a critical practice in software development that ensures quality, maintains standards, and facilitates knowledge sharing. LLM PR Review leverages large language models to automate aspects of this process, analyzing pull requests to identify potential bugs, security vulnerabilities, and coding standard violations. These AI-powered tools can provide contextual suggestions, explain complex code changes to team members, and highlight areas that need human attention—all while reducing the cognitive load on developers. By handling routine checks and providing intelligent insights, LLM PR Review tools such as PR Agent,Qudo, Code Rabbit, etc., streamline the development workflow, allowing human reviewers to focus on higher-level architectural considerations and complex logic issues that require deeper expertise and judgment.

blips.name: gRPC
blips.description:
Why?

gRPC is a Cloud Native Computing Foundation, it enables bidirectional streaming and flow control over HTTP/2.

Many of our clients show interest and integrate gRPC in their systems. It is another open-source from Google and is wildly used in the industry.

Description

A high-performance, open-source RPC framework that uses HTTP/2 for transport and Protocol Buffers for serialization, enabling efficient communication between microservices.

blips.name: gVisor
blips.description:
Why?

gVisor provides an additional layer of isolation between running applications and the host operating system.

Description

gVisor is an application kernel for containers that provides efficient defense-in-depth anywhere.

blips.name: Lodash
blips.description:
Why?

Lodash was a great utility belt for JavaScript, but today many of its functions are available natively (or via smaller targeted libraries like es-toolkit)

Description

Lodash is a JavaScript utility library that provides dozens of handy functions for tasks like deep cloning, object merging, debouncing functions, and manipulating arrays/objects. It became popular as a successor to Underscore.js by offering more performance and features.

blips.name: Logfire
blips.description:
Why?

If your stack is Python-first — especially FastAPI, PydanticAI, or any LLM pipeline — Logfire gives you production observability with near-zero setup, automatic request tracing, and LLM call instrumentation that would take days to wire manually with OpenTelemetry alone, making it the fastest path to seeing exactly what's happening inside your agents and APIs in production.

Description

From the team behind Pydantic, Logfire is a new type of observability platform built on the same belief as our open source library — that the most powerful tools can be easy to use.

Logfire is built on OpenTelemetry, and supports monitoring your application from any language, with particularly great support for Python!

blips.name: Loguru
blips.description:
Why?

Loguru simplifies logging in Python by eliminating boilerplate and offering a powerful, user-friendly interface out of the box. It supports features like colorful logs, automatic exception catching, file rotation, and structured logging without needing complex setup. As projects grow, Loguru continues to provide clear, flexible, and reliable logging that helps developers debug faster and maintain better observability across their applications.

Description

Loguru is a lightweight and easy-to-use logging library for Python that simplifies logging setup and usage with minimal configuration. It offers powerful features like colorful output, automatic file rotation, exception catching, and structured logging—all accessible through a single, intuitive interface.

blips.name: Harbor
blips.description:
Why?

Need a private docker hub like ECR, DockerHub. Harbor is a good candidate.

Description

Harbor is an open-source cloud-native registry that stores, signs, and scans container images for vulnerabilities. Harbor solves common challenges by delivering trust, compliance, performance, and interoperability. It fills a gap for organizations and applications that cannot use a public or cloud-based registry or want a consistent experience across clouds.

Harbor is a private registry for docker images and helm charts with user management support, It can manage and synchronize multiple docker registries in different regions. In summary, if you need a private docker hub like ECR, DockerHub. Harbor is a good candidate.

blips.name: Lottie
blips.description:
Why?

Maintained for its broad industry asset support and reliability in existing animation workflows.

Description

An open-source animation library that renders Adobe After Effects animations natively on mobile and web, exported as JSON via the Bodymovin plugin.

blips.name: Low code / No code
blips.description:
Why?

LCNC allows businesses to create applications without relying solely on professional programmers. it gives you faster development cycles and cost effectiveness. Note that LCNC is not suitable for any use case

Description

Development platforms that enable application creation through visual interfaces and configuration rather than traditional programming, lowering technical barriers to software development.

blips.name: Luxon
blips.description:
Why?

moved to STOP due to unpatched security vulnerabilities in its zone management system and a lack of active maintenance, making it a liability compared to more secure and modern alternatives like Day.js.

Description

Luxon is a JavaScript library for working with dates and times, developed by a Moment.js author as a modern alternative.

blips.name: Mantine.dev
blips.description:
Why?

Mantine is a rapidly growing React component library that offers a wide array of accessible, customizable components.

Description

Mantine is a full-featured React UI library that includes 100+ customizable components and hooks. It comes with default styles out of the box but allows extensive theme overriding to match your brand.

blips.name: Material UI
blips.description:
Why?

Material UI (MUI) provides a robust set of React components that implement Google’s Material Design, which accelerates development of attractive UIs.

Description

Material UI (MUI) is a popular React UI framework that implements Google’s Material Design guidelines.

blips.name: MCPApps
blips.description:
Why?

Investigating standardized applications of the Model Context Protocol for cross-tool AI communication.

Description

Applications built using the Model Context Protocol (MCP), enabling AI assistants to interact with external data sources and tools through a standardized interface.

blips.name: Mem0 / OpenMemory MCP
blips.description:
Why?

Mem0 solves the statelessness problem of LLM agents without building custom memory infrastructure — if you're running multi-session agents, personal assistants, or coding copilots that need to remember user preferences, past decisions, and project context across conversations, OpenMemory MCP plugs directly into Claude, Cursor, or any MCP-compatible tool with minimal setup.

Description

An MCP server implementation providing persistent memory capabilities for AI agents, enabling them to store and retrieve context across conversations.

blips.name: Micro Frontends
blips.description:
Why?

Micro-frontend architecture has matured into a viable strategy for large applications, enabling independent development and deployment of different UI segments.

Description

Micro-frontends refer to a design approach where a web application is decomposed into smaller, semi-independent “frontend” applications.

blips.name: Microservice Architecture
blips.description:
Why?

MSA has long since become an industry-standard in writing complex applications as a bunch of simple services. This simple, language-agnostic coding gives organizations more agility and the ability to quickly deliver changes.

Description

Apart from the old monolithic paradigm of software engineering, the Micro-Service-Architecture (MSA) or Service-Oriented-Architecture (SOA) orients software engineers to break apart their software design to different self-contained, independent services, maintained by small teams of no more than 4 engineers, on a rather small codebase.

This new approach makes it possible to design logic parts of the entire application as more generic services, for the future use of other clients.

For more info and best practices about MSA design, refer here:

blips.name: MindsDB
blips.description:
Why?

MindsDB offers several key advantages:

  1. Ease of Use: Integrates directly with SQL databases, allowing users to build and query ML models using SQL.
  2. AutoML: Automates model training, tuning, and deployment.
  3. Real-Time Predictions: Enables live predictions within database queries.
  4. Broad Integrations: Works with popular databases (MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB) and tools (BI dashboards, etc.).
  5. No-Code/Low-Code: Ideal for developers and analysts with limited ML experience. In short, MindsDB simplifies and speeds up the use of machine learning directly within existing data workflows.

Description

MindsDB is an open-source AI layer for existing databases which allows easy training and using of ML models. All user needs is SQL knowledge. By providing SQL with data, the system selects the appropriate model and configuration. Nevertheless, the user can customize the model.

blips.name: HELM / Umbrella Chart
blips.description:
Why?

The Umbrella pattern allows you to deploy assembly of multiple microservice has one version and use it as a kind of release to install in different datacenters.

Description

Helm, short for Helm Charts which help manage Kubernetes applications — Helm Charts helps you define, install, and upgrade even the most complex Kubernetes applications.

Charts are easy to create, version, share, and publish. There are Helm Registry offerings from both Quay.io and Artifactory. HELM helps to manage Services, Deployment, Secrets and all parts related to Kubernetes ready applications. **Umbrella chart **, To install a complex application with helm — There is something called umbrella chart Umbrella chart is a chart with dependency (requirements.yaml) on other charts. and value.yaml (override charts values) To install umbrella-chart you run “helm dep update” will download depended on chart , then “helm install” or “helm upgrade” will install the charts

blips.name: MinIO
blips.description:
Why?

MinIO's community edition shifted to AGPL-3.0 licensing, meaning any networked service built on top of it must also open-source its code — a legal landmine for most commercial products. Combined with the removal of the distributed mode from the community build (now paywalled under the commercial license), teams running multi-node MinIO clusters for production lakehouses are effectively forced to either pay for the enterprise tier or migrate to truly open alternatives like SeaweedFS or Ceph.

Description

The open-source, S3-compatible object storage server that can be self-hosted on any infrastructure. Widely adopted as a drop-in local alternative to AWS S3 for lakehouses, ML pipelines, and on-prem data platforms.

blips.name: ML Engineering
blips.description:
Why?

We recommend start combining ML engineers in DataScience teams, in order to bring their engineering expertise, which contribute to model using in production applications.

Description

ML Engineers are software engineers that specialize in ML area. They bring into teams and projects the engineering expertise, and allow models developed by Data Scientist to reach production in a safe and iterative ways. They build the lifecycle of application development, starting from data engineering, API integration, application development, through CI-CD, ML pipeline all the way through monitoring and maintenance. Their understanding of the special needs and processes of ML allows them to produce effective ML applications.

blips.name: MLflow
blips.description:
Why?

Using MLflow provides a centralized platform for tracking experiments, enabling data scientists to compare models, iterate efficiently, and collaborate effectively. Additionally, MLflow's model packaging and deployment features simplify the transition of models from development to production

Description

MLflow is an open-source platform to manage the ML lifecycle, including experimentation, reproducibility, and deployment. Maintained and developed by Databricks (Apache Spark maintainer), it offers the following components:

  • MLflow Tracking - ability to record and query ML experiments
  • MLflow Projects - packaging format for reproducible runs on any platform.
  • MLflow Models - General format for sending models to diverse deployment tools

Mastering this tool in Tikal provides us with production-level capabilities we can offer to customers.

We recommend trying this tool as It’s mature, lightweight and easy to use

blips.name: Infrastructure as Code (IaC)
blips.description:
Why?

IaC remains essential for enabling consistent and scalable deployment environments in DevOps practices.

Description

Infrastructure as Code (IaC) is the practice of managing and provisioning infrastructure — servers, networks, databases, load balancers, and other cloud resources — through machine-readable configuration files rather than manual processes or interactive tools.

blips.name: MobX
blips.description:
Why?

MobX provides a simple yet powerful reactive state management solution. It allows us to have a single source of truth for state and automatically updates the UI when that state changes, with minimal boilerplate.

Description

A simple, scalable state management library that makes state management transparent through reactive programming, using observables and automatic tracking of state dependencies.

blips.name: Mocha
blips.description:
Why?

Mocha is a flexible test framework, but using it often requires assembling other tools (assertion libraries, test runners) to get a full testing experience.

Description

MobX is a reactive state management library that makes state changes in JavaScript applications automatic.

blips.name: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
blips.description:
Why?

If you're a developer or DevOps pro building AI-powered workflows or tools, MCP is your missing glue. Try it to make LLMs context-aware, responsive, and actually useful across your stack.

Description

Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard by Anthropic for connecting LLM applications to external tools, data sources, and services through a unified client-server interface. It lets AI agents discover and call capabilities (tools, resources, prompts) exposed by MCP servers, enabling interoperability across different hosts and agent frameworks.

blips.name: Module Federation
blips.description:
Why?

Module Federation (Webpack 5) enables micro-frontends by allowing dynamic loading of code from other builds at runtime. This means teams can deploy independent parts of the application and have them integrate without a full redeploy of the whole app.

Description

A webpack feature that enables multiple independent builds to share code at runtime, allowing micro-frontends to dynamically load and share dependencies.

blips.name: Moment.js
blips.description:
Why?

Moment.js has been officially labeled a legacy project and is in maintenance mode, with no new features being added. Its authors recommend switching to alternatives (like Luxon or date-fns) for new projects.

Description

Module Federation is a feature of Webpack that allows multiple separate bundles/applications to interoperate by sharing and loading modules at runtime.

blips.name: Lerna
blips.description:
Why?

Lerna was instrumental in managing JavaScript monorepos, but the ecosystem has evolved with native package manager workspaces and advanced tools like Nx.

Description

Lerna is a fast modern build system for managing and publishing multiple JavaScript/TypeScript packages from the same repository.

blips.name: Monorepo
blips.description:
Why?

Monorepo practices have shown clear benefits for large codebases: easier code sharing, unified versioning, and streamlined refactoring across projects.

Description

A monorepo is a version control strategy where multiple projects — packages, libraries, or apps — reside in a single repository, enabling shared tooling, simplified dependency management, and atomic cross-project changes.

blips.name: Monorepo
blips.description:
Why?

Monorepos become a liability when CI/CD pipelines can't scope builds intelligently, turning every small change into a full repo rebuild that slows down every team sharing the codebase.

Description

A monorepo is a version control strategy where multiple projects — packages, libraries, or apps — reside in a single repository, enabling shared tooling, simplified dependency management, and atomic cross-project changes.

blips.name: Motion
blips.description:
Why?

The preferred animation library for React due to its intuitive declarative API and seamless layout transitions.

Description

A production-ready motion library for React, providing declarative animations with layout animations, gestures, and spring physics built-in.

blips.name: MSW
blips.description:
Why?

Mock Service Worker (MSW) has quickly become indispensable for front-end development and testing.

Description

Mock Service Worker (MSW) is a library for JavaScript applications that allows you to intercept and control the behavior of HTTP requests. It works on both the client (browser) and server (Node.js), allowing developers to establish unified APIs for mocking requests in their applications.

blips.name: n8n
blips.description:
Why?

n8n makes it easy to automate workflows across apps and APIs with a visual interface, reducing manual effort and coding overhead.

Description

n8n is a free and open-source tool to connect services and automate tasks — like syncing databases, sending alerts, or triggering scripts.

blips.name: ingress-nginx
blips.description:
Why?

NGINX started off as the faster Apache alternative and it seems to be the most popular ingress used out there among our clientele, and gaining popularity due to its seamless integration with Kubernetes.

Description

The NGINX controller is built around the Kubernetes Ingress resource that uses ConfigMaps to store the NGINX configuration.

NGINX is in the route path of many applications, which all vary in needs. From basic ones like routing (a.k.a proxying) and authentication to advanced services like load balancing SSL termination and integrations with other projects like cert-manager (Kube-lego) and many more.

blips.name: Narwhals
blips.description:
Why?

Start using this if your team is building internal data utilities or shared libraries. It ensures your logic works regardless of whether the input is a classic Pandas table or a high-performance Polars/Arrow object.

Description

A lightweight DataFrame-agnostic API layer that provides a unified interface across pandas, Polars, and other dataframe libraries, enabling library authors to write engine-agnostic code.

blips.name: NATS
blips.description:
Why?

This message broker has differentiated itself from others by its high scalability and performance abilities. As such, many more companies have adopted this solution as a viable message broker for their needs.

Description

NATS is an incredibly fast open-source cloud-native messaging system written in the Go programming language. The core design principles of NATS are performance, scalability, and ease of use. NATS supports Pub/Sub, Scatter-Gather, but also Request-Reply Messaging Models. It seems that there is a need in the industry for even more variety than what we have today in the messaging system’s domain. Kafka is very complex and there is a need for a simple solution that is highly scalable and lightning fast. The added value of the Request-Reply model might be interesting as this is something lacking in most other messaging systems including popular solutions such as Kafka and RabbitMQ. This might open doors to as of yet unavailable communication patterns between micros services.

blips.name: NestJS
blips.description:
Why?

NestJS brings a lot of structure to Node.js development, using decorators and modules to organize code in a highly scalable way.

Description

NestJS is a progressive Node.js framework built with TypeScript that adopts many design patterns from Angular. It encourages an architectural pattern with modules, controllers, and providers, which results in highly testable and scalable applications.

blips.name: Next.js
blips.description:
Why?

Next.js has become the standard for building React applications that need server-side rendering, static site generation, or incremental static regeneration.

Description

Next.js is a React framework for building web applications with hybrid rendering capabilities.

blips.name: node:test
blips.description:
Why?

Node’s built-in test runner (accessible via node:test) is a recent addition that provides a zero-dependency way to write tests. It's still evolving, but it already supports key features like subtests, mocking, and parallel execution.

Description

node:test is Node.js’s native testing module (introduced experimentally in Node v18 and becoming stable in later versions). It allows writing test files that Node can execute with the --test flag, without needing Jest, Mocha, or other frameworks.

blips.name: Internal Developer Portals (IDPs) (e.g., Port.io. Backstage)
blips.description:
Why?

Managing all the knowledge about our systems is now a standard in development world.

Description

Internal Developer Portals (IDPs) provide a self-service hub for developers to discover services, manage environments, track ownership, and run workflows — reducing cognitive load and engineering toil. Popular implementations include Backstage (open-source) and Port.io (SaaS).

blips.name: Istio
blips.description:
Why?

Istio lets you connect, secure, control, and observe services. At a high level, Istio helps reduce the complexity of these deployments and eases the strain on your development teams. It is a completely open-source service mesh that layers transparently onto existing distributed applications.

Description

Istio’s diverse feature set lets you successfully, and efficiently, run a distributed microservice architecture, and provides a uniform way to secure, connect, and monitor microservices - implementing all the technics and methodologies mentioned above (which used to be part of the Backend).

blips.name: Node.js + Typescript
blips.description:
Why?

Node.js uses an event-driven, non-blocking I/O model that makes it lightweight and efficient.

Typescript adds type safety to Node.js and it has become, for new project, in use, more than javascript written node.js,and we feel that typescript has become the standard language to rite node application with.

Description

Using TypeScript with Node.js provides numerous advantages that revolve around improving the reliability, scalability, and productivity of your application development process.

blips.name: JCasC (Jenkins Configuration as Code)
blips.description:
Why?

While Jenkins as a tool is fading out, the JCASC + Library is still here and serves existing systems.

Description

Thread also supports the creation of virtual threads. Virtual threads are typically user-mode threads scheduled by the Java runtime rather than the operating system. Virtual threads will typically require few resources and a single Java virtual machine may support millions of virtual threads. Virtual threads are suitable for executing tasks that spend most of the time blocked, often waiting for I/O operations to complete. Virtual threads are not intended for long running CPU intensive operations.

blips.name: NotebookLM
blips.description:
Why?

Try NotebookLM to explore, summarize, and generate insights from your documents using an AI assistant grounded in your personal notes and sources.

Description

Google's AI-powered research and note-taking assistant that uses Gemini to synthesize information from uploaded documents, generating summaries, insights, and answering questions grounded in your sources.

blips.name: Jenkins
blips.description:
Why?

Jenkins as a CI/CD tool is becoming irrelevant, while we have repo-oriented tools (like Gitlab ci and more) that can do almost everything Jenkins can. In addition, the rise of GitOps is a newly popular approach that is taking out tools like Jenkins. It is still in "keep" because it is still very popular amongst DevOps, but it looks like it's last year here.

Description

The leading open source automation server, Jenkins provides hundreds of plugins to support building, deploying and automating any project

blips.name: Jib
blips.description:
Why?

When developing a java application that should run on docker, Jib gives us an optimized image build, with no dependency on docker daemon, and with Gradle/Maven integration the docker build/push are part of the build system.

Description

Jib builds optimized Docker and OCI images for your Java applications without a Docker daemon - and without deep mastery of Docker best-practices. It is available as plugins for Maven and Gradle and as a Java library

blips.name: Nx
blips.description:
Why?

Nx (by Nrwl) has made managing monorepos much more efficient through features like affected-builds (only rebuilding what changed) and distributed caching.

Description

Nx is a set of extensible dev tools for monorepos, which helps manage projects with multiple applications and libraries. It provides features like code generation, dependency management, and build optimization.

blips.name: Just-in-Time Infrastructure (JiTI)
blips.description:
Why?

As compute management is becoming a complex mission, the industry is moving to "just in time infrastructure".

Description

JupyterLab is a true IDE for interactive computing. You have everything you need for your work (especially for a Data Scientist or a Data Engineer) in one window: file browser, terminal and code/notebook editor. In addition it has a robust and thriving third-party extension community.

blips.name: k3d
blips.description:
Why?

The easiest way to bring up a local k8s cluster on a personal machine or a light vm.

Description

This trend deals with avoiding on going compute capacity management. It can be achieved in several ways and using a variety of tools. One can be FaaS (Function as a Service), where we trigger a Serverless function per need, without bothering the compute capacity needed. In the Kubernetes arena we can use AWS - Karpenter and GCP Node auto-provisioning, to optimize needed compute resources by monitoring the cluster's activities and loads.

blips.name: k3s
blips.description:
Why?

lightweight local k8s cluster for local development.

Description

A lightweight, certified Kubernetes distribution designed for edge, IoT, and resource-constrained environments. It packages all components into a single binary under 100MB.

blips.name: Ollama
blips.description:
Why?

Devs and DevOps who want fast, local access to LLMs — no cloud, no setup pain. Perfect for building, testing, or experimenting with AI workflows on your own hardware.

Description

Ollama is a fast, local runtime for large language models (LLMs), letting developers run models like LLaMA, Mistral, and Code Llama directly on their machine with a simple CLI. It handles downloading, setup, and serving the models out-of-the-box — no infrastructure, Docker, or huggingface wrangling needed. Ollama makes it easy to integrate local LLMs into your development workflow, scripts, or custom tooling with minimal friction. For DevOps, it’s an ideal way to test prompts, prototype agents, or run secure AI workflows without relying on external APIs or exposing data to the cloud.

blips.name: k9s
blips.description:
Why?

A robust k8s terminal based UI that makes it easier to work with k8s clusters instead of the regular kubectl cli command.

Description

K9s is a terminal based UI to interact with your Kubernetes clusters. The aim of this project is to make it easier to navigate, observe and manage your deployed applications in the wild. K9s continually watches Kubernetes for changes and offers subsequent commands to interact with your observed resources.

blips.name: Kaniko
blips.description:
Why?

A good solution to enable building container images in environments that can't easily or securely run a Docker daemon, such as a standard Kubernetes cluster.

Description

A tool to build container images from a Dockerfile inside a Kubernetes cluster without requiring Docker daemon, making it ideal for CI/CD pipelines running in Kubernetes.

blips.name: Karpenter
blips.description:
Why?

K8S HPA and node autoscaling are great. But this tool is taking one step ahead. It analyzes usage and based on that, decides upon the amount of the needed compute resources.

Description

Karpenter automatically launches just the right compute resources to handle your k8s cluster's applications. It is designed to let you take full advantage of the cloud with fast and simple compute provisioning for Kubernetes clusters.

blips.name: OpenAPI
blips.description:
Why?

The OpenAPI defines a standard, language-agnostic interface to RESTful APIs.

it serves both as the documentation and a means to run api calls

The most common implementation, Swagger and the 3rd version of OpenAPI are wildly used, and has become a standard in writing Rest APIs

Description

OpenAPI (formerly Swagger Specification), allows you to describe your API using YAML or JSON.

Swagger is a set of open-source tools built around the OpenAPI, it enables:

  • automatic creation of stubs from the Specification
  • automatically creating/updating Specification from code
  • a GUI for testing api calls
  • connect API-related tools to your API

blips.name: Openclaw
blips.description:
Why?

OpenClaw is the most complete open-source alternative to proprietary AI assistant services — if you want a persistent, always-on AI assistant that lives on your infra, responds in your existing chat apps, and can be extended with custom skills and agent-to-agent workflows, it's a serious contender with 356k stars and an active community behind it.

Description

An open-source AI web scraping framework that uses vision-language models to extract structured data from websites without writing CSS selectors.

blips.name: KEDA
blips.description:
Why?

KEDA is a great choice when you need support in HPA based on Queue, Database, etc… KEDA also has an out-of-the-box scaler for (Kafka, influx dB, …). Keda also supports Scaled deployments/pods to zero and triggered Kubernetes jobs which is a great advantage.

Description

KEDA is a Kubernetes autoscaling tool that scales workloads based on external events or metrics, such as queues, messages, requests, or custom triggers.

blips.name: OpenSearch
blips.description:
Why?

OpenSearch provides a powerful, open-source search and analytics engine that supports scalable log analytics, full-text search, and real-time observability—all without vendor lock-in. Built as a community-driven fork of Elasticsearch, OpenSearch offers a flexible and extensible platform with features like distributed search, alerting, dashboards, and anomaly detection. It integrates easily with popular data pipelines and supports a wide range of use cases from application monitoring to security analytics. As the need for transparent, high-performance search grows, OpenSearch remains a cost-effective and reliable solution.

Description

An open-source search engine technology, self-hosted, free.
OpenSearch was originally derived from the Elasticsearch project because th changes in Elasticsearch's license

blips.name: Keybase
blips.description:
Why?

When working together online, chat tools like Slack are useful, but allow the service provider to read your messages. Keybase simplifies the process of sharing files and having conversations securely.

Description

Keybase has become for me one of the central tools, it enables me to securely correspond with my peers share files and even entire git repositories if needed. One main benefit of using keybase is your very own hosted free pgp server so all your public certs are stored on keybase servers which means using pgp encryption and sharing encrypted data (even outside of keybase) has become a breeze. In addition, the keybase cli enables you to run clean code without worrying about storing sensitive data in it.

We are now checking how a ci bot user could be part of the keybase network which could potentially provide storing secure build artifacts that are discoverable only by users that follow that bot user (gpg wise). With this ci capability signing git commits, decrypting secrets in build time has just become much faster.

The alternative solutions are much more expensive to operate not only in money … Managing servers for solutions such as Vault which of course could provide this type of solution in addition to other features of course. (and I also found a reference by hasicorp recommending th use of keybase for the initial password / cert of Vault).

blips.name: OpenTelemetry
blips.description:
Why?

A vendor-agnostic proxy that can receive, process, and export telemetry data.

Description

OpenTelemetry collector is a tool that in a powerful way receives data from multiple sources, transforms it, and sends it to the destinations you like. We can scrape Prometheus metrics with the OpenTelemetry Collector and send them to a remote write destination like Grafana Cloud.
