blips.name: kind
blips.description:
Why?

Quickly run Kubernetes nodes as Docker containers, a great tool for testing, development, and CI.

Description

kind is a local Kubernetes tool that runs clusters inside Docker containers, mainly for testing, development, and CI workflows.

blips.name: OXC
blips.description:
Why?

A high-performance JS/TS transformer and linter written in Rust, significantly faster than Babel or ESLint.

Description

A collection of high-performance JavaScript tools written in Rust, including a parser, linter, and formatter designed as faster alternatives to existing JS tooling.

blips.name: Pandas 1
blips.description:
Why?

Pandas 1 lacks Copy-on-Write semantics, has inconsistent nullable dtypes, and misses the Arrow-backed performance improvements introduced in Pandas 2 — there's no reason to stay on it.

Description

Pandas is a python software library for analysis and manipulation of data. It provides a plethora of mathematical and analytical tools around data. Today, it is one of the most popular data manipulation libraries in the world. It goes hand-in-hand with data science, AI and machine learning fields.

More and more companies and projects around the world are switching to Python to enjoy the benefits of this library. Along with NumPy, they are the leading software libraries in the data science world. Gaining knowledge and experience in Pandas opens great opportunities in the current software industry.

blips.name: Pandas 2
blips.description:
Why?

Pandas 2 remains the most universally understood data manipulation library in Python — its Copy-on-Write semantics, Arrow-backed dtypes, and improved nullable types make it fast enough for most single-machine workloads, and its ecosystem compatibility (scikit-learn, matplotlib, SQLAlchemy, dbt) means it's still the lowest-friction choice for data exploration, prototyping, and pipeline steps that don't need distributed or out-of-core processing.

Description

Pandas is a python software library for analysis and manipulation of data. It provides a plethora of mathematical and analytical tools around data. Today, it is one of the most popular data manipulation libraries in the world. It goes hand-in-hand with data science, AI and machine learning fields.

Pandas 2.0 with Apache Arrow as the backend, aims to provide better performance, scalability and integration benefits for data analysis workflows while preserving Pandas' user-friendly data manipulation capabilities.

blips.name: Pandas 3
blips.description:
Why?

Pandas 3 makes Copy-on-Write non-optional — eliminating the silent mutation bugs that plagued Pandas 1/2 codebases — and the new pd.col() expression API enables cleaner, more composable DataFrame transformations. If your pipelines are already on Pandas 2, upgrading to 3 is a low-risk correctness and performance win, especially for teams dealing with complex dtype handling or Arrow-backed data flows.

Description

Pandas 3 was released on January 21, 2026.It is the latest major version of the most widely used Python data manipulation library, bringing Copy-on-Write enforcement by default, a new pd.col() expression API for declarative column operations, Arrow-backed strings as the default string dtype, and further performance and dtype consistency improvements over the 2.x line.

blips.name: Payload CMS
blips.description:
Why?

The leading TypeScript-native headless CMS, offering a superior developer experience and deep Next.js integration.'

Description

Payload CMS is an open-source, full-stack TypeScript framework that functions as both a headless CMS and an application backend. Built with Express and MongoDB (or other databases via adapters), it lets developers define collections (content types) and fields in a schema file, and automatically generates a rich admin UI for content editors.

blips.name: PGlite
blips.description:
Why?

PGlite unlocks local-first, offline-capable applications with real Postgres semantics — making it ideal for prototyping, testing without a database server, edge deployments, or building collaborative apps where client-side SQL reduces round-trips and infrastructure complexity.

Description

A lightweight, embeddable version of PostgreSQL compiled to WebAssembly, allowing a full Postgres database to run entirely in the browser, Node.js, or edge environments — with no server required and full SQL compatibility.

blips.name: Kong
blips.description:
Why?

A powerful and popular tool for Application Programming Interfaces and Microservices management.

Description

Kong is an API gateway that manages, secures, routes, and monitors API traffic between clients and backend services.

blips.name: Kubernetes
blips.description:
Why?

Kubernetes is still here, and nothing is currently seen as a candidate for replacement on the horizon.

Description

Kubernetes is an open-source container orchestration system for automating software deployment, scaling, and management. Google originally designed Kubernetes, but the Cloud Native Computing Foundation now maintains the project.

blips.name: Playwright
blips.description:
Why?

Playwright has rapidly become a top choice for end-to-end web testing thanks to its reliability and multi-browser support. Backed by Microsoft, it provides a unified API to automate Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit, and includes powerful features like auto-waiting, web-first assertions, and trace viewing for debugging.

Description

Playwright is an open-source end-to-end testing and browser automation framework by Microsoft that enables reliable testing across all major browsers. It can automate Chromium (Chrome/Edge), Firefox, and WebKit (Safari) with a single API.

blips.name: Kubernetes Operator Pattern
blips.description:
Why?

A Way to keep code more secure and without storing passwords in git, This operator gives access to the k8s cluster to a secure backend (i.e secret-manager, vault, ext) and creates a k8s secret for the workloads.

Description

The Operator Pattern A Kubernetes Operator is simply a domain specific controller that can manage, configure and automate the lifecycle of stateful applications. Managing stateful applications, such as databases, caches and monitoring systems running on Kubernetes is notoriously difficult. By leveraging the power of Kubernetes API we can now build self managing, self driving infrastructure by encoding operational knowledge and best practices directly into code. For instance, if a MySQL instance dies, we can use an Operator to react and take the appropriate action to bring the system back online.

blips.name: Poetry
blips.description:
Why?

Poetry's slow dependency resolver, lack of workspace support for monorepos, and the rise of uv — which is orders of magnitude faster — make it hard to recommend for new Python projects in 2026.

Description

Poetry is a dependency management tool for Python that simplifies package creation, version management, and distribution.

blips.name: Polars
blips.description:
Why?

Polars delivers lightning-fast, memory-efficient data processing with a modern, Rust-based engine and a user-friendly Python API. Compared to traditional tools like Pandas, Polars excels at handling large datasets and complex transformations with significantly better performance and parallelism. Its lazy evaluation model and type safety further optimize workloads, making it ideal for both exploratory data analysis and production pipelines. As data volumes grow and performance demands increase, Polars remains a powerful, scalable alternative for efficient data manipulation.

Description

Polars is a very fast DataFrame API which is written in Rust and has a Python API. It is an alternative to the famous Pandas dataframe, surpassing it in speed and lower memory management. The fact it is based on Apache Arrow and Rust, gives it tremendous speed and lower memory footprint.

blips.name: KubeVela
blips.description:
Why?

When you have a complex deployment flow that involves orchestration involving IaC and cloud-native components or you want to define promoting flow for the release versions of your product that you want to apply Kubevela can definitely be a good option.

Description

KubeVela is a Kubernetes application delivery platform that simplifies deploying and managing apps across clusters using higher-level abstractions.

blips.name: Kuma
blips.description:
Why?

Kuma gives you a good visuality of your service mesh implementation, The major supporter of this tool is kong, so if you use kong is the most relevant tool.

Description

The open-source control plane for service mesh, delivering security, observability, routing and more

blips.name: Lens
blips.description:
Why?

A very nice and free desktop app that will help you visualize and control your Kubernetes cluster(s).

Description

THE KUBERNETES IDE FOR OPERATIONS

blips.name: PostgreSQL
blips.description:
Why?

PostgreSQL supports data embedding for vector similarity queries

Description

PostgreSQL is a powerful, open source object-relational database system (ORDMBS) that uses and extends the SQL language combined with many features that safely store and scale the most complicated data workloads.

blips.name: LLM PR Review
blips.description:
Why?

Tired of writing PR summaries and nitpicking code? PR Agent handles reviews, comments, and changelogs with AI — so you can focus on building, not paperwork. Devs and DevOps: this one actually saves time.

Description

Code review is a critical practice in software development that ensures quality, maintains standards, and facilitates knowledge sharing. LLM PR Review leverages large language models to automate aspects of this process, analyzing pull requests to identify potential bugs, security vulnerabilities, and coding standard violations. These AI-powered tools can provide contextual suggestions, explain complex code changes to team members, and highlight areas that need human attention—all while reducing the cognitive load on developers. By handling routine checks and providing intelligent insights, LLM PR Review tools such as PR Agent,Qudo, Code Rabbit, etc., streamline the development workflow, allowing human reviewers to focus on higher-level architectural considerations and complex logic issues that require deeper expertise and judgment.

blips.name: Linkerd
blips.description:
Why?

A service mesh tool for K8S.

Description

Linkerd is a service mesh for Kubernetes. It makes running services easier and safer by giving you runtime debugging, observability, reliability, and security—all without requiring any changes to your code.

blips.name: pre-commit
blips.description:
Why?

Ensures code quality and consistency Automates boring checks Prevents "oops" moments (e.g., committing debug code or secrets) Works with many languages and tools

Description

Pre-Commit is a framework for managing and maintaining multi-language pre-commit hooks. It helps you automatically run checks (like linting, formatting, security scans, etc.) on your code before you commit it to version control (usually Git).

blips.name: Preact
blips.description:
Why?

Preact offers a nearly drop-in replacement for React with a much smaller footprint (around 3 KB). For projects where every kilobyte counts or performance on low-end devices is critical, Preact can be a big win.

Description

Preact is a fast, lightweight library that implements the core ideas of React (components, JSX, virtual DOM) in a tiny package. It achieves much of the same functionality as React but sacrifices some of the less commonly used features to remain small.

blips.name: Prefect
blips.description:
Why?

Prefect provides API access to pipelines and business logic, allowing other teams to programmatically access workflows. In addition, it helps standardize workflow development and deployment across your organization. Python decorators enable Prefect to extend pipelines with automatic retries, distributed execution, scheduling, and caching. It is possible to monitor every activity either using a self-hosted Prefect server instance or using a Prefect Cloud dashboard managed by Prefect.

Description

Prefect is an open-source automation and scheduling engine used for taking any code and transforming it into a robust, distributed workflow. It was developed in order to address some faults in the popular workflow Airflow. Airflow restricted the developers to stick to its very strict vocabulary.

Prefect addresses many features that were missing in Airflow, like:

  • DAGs which need to be run off-schedule or with no schedule at all
  • DAGs that run concurrently with the same start time
  • DAGs with complicated branching logic
  • DAGs with many fast tasks
  • DAGs which rely on the exchange of data
  • Parametrized DAGs
  • Dynamic DAGs

blips.name: LocalStack
blips.description:
Why?

An excellent tool for mocking AWS resources on a local machine.

Description

LocalStack - A fully functional local AWS cloud stack - LocalStack provides an easy-to-use test/mocking framework for developing Cloud applications.

Currently, the focus is primarily on supporting the AWS cloud stack. The tool has good support for Docker and enables developers to test services such as API Gateway, Kinesis & DynamoDB from the comfort of their laptop.

blips.name: Prisma
blips.description:
Why?

Prisma has quickly become a go-to ORM for Node.js thanks to its intuitive schema and the auto-generated TypeScript client that provides compile-time assurance of query correctness.

Description

Prisma is an open-source ORM (Object-Relational Mapping) and database toolkit for Node.js and TypeScript. It uses a schema definition to generate a type-safe database client that makes queries easy to write and less error-prone.

blips.name: Promptfoo
blips.description:
Why?

Promptfoo turns LLM evaluation from a manual, ad-hoc process into a repeatable, automated pipeline — catching prompt regressions, model degradation, and safety issues before they hit production, with zero vendor lock-in and native CI/CD integration.

Description

Promptfoo is an open-source LLM evaluation and red-teaming framework that lets teams define test suites in YAML, run assertions across multiple providers, and compare prompt/model performance — bringing CI/CD-style testing discipline to LLM development workflows.

blips.name: Loki
blips.description:
Why?

Loki is light in resources compared to the competitors (ELK, EFK). Very easy to maintain and give lots of value out of the box. Because is good integration with Grafana can give the correlation between logs and metrics.

Description

Loki is like Prometheus, but for logs. It is designed to be very cost effective and easy to operate, and does not index the contents of the logs, but rather a set of labels for each log stream.

blips.name: MinIO
blips.description:
Why?

Object storage becoming a good alternative to big-data storage solutions. S3 API is the most common way of using object storage. These 2 facts make Minio a perfect solution for managing your own object storage when needed (on-prem environment or cloudless infrastructure are good examples)

Description

The open-source, S3-compatible object storage server that can be self-hosted on any infrastructure. Widely adopted as a drop-in local alternative to AWS S3 for lakehouses, ML pipelines, and on-prem data platforms.

blips.name: Pulumi
blips.description:
Why?

By using Pulumi over the likes of terraform, you can move from static configuration to procedural programming, and enhance the scenarios that you can support.

Description

Pulumi lets you define infrastructure using real programming languages (TypeScript, Python, Go, etc.) instead of declarative configs, giving you more flexibility and reuse for complex infrastructure setups.

blips.name: MLOps
blips.description:
Why?

MLOps are crucial to the success of ML projects. Part of the reasons ML projects often fail is lack of adequate practices and infrastructure. Adopting MLOps practices reduces time to market and increases confidence in the product. We recommend starting using MLOps practices, as ML projects become popular in almost every technology company, from start-ups to enterprises.

Description

MLOPs is a set of actions and practices from the DevOps world, aiming to develop and deploy ML projects in a reliable way. It includes tools to provide CI-CD-CT (Continuous Training) for ML projects, which differ from standard software projects.

blips.name: PydanticAI
blips.description:
Why?

PydanticAI brings type-safe, structured LLM interactions with first-class Pydantic validation, dependency injection, and multi-agent support — making it the most Pythonic framework for building production-grade AI agents with minimal boilerplate.

Description

PydanticAI is a Python agent framework designed to make it less painful to build production-grade applications with Generative AI

blips.name: Node.js
blips.description:
Why?

Node.js remains a cornerstone of our stack – its non-blocking, event-driven architecture is well-suited for the scalable network services we build.

Description

Node.js is a JavaScript runtime built on Chrome’s V8 engine that allows JavaScript to be run on the server (outside the browser). It introduced an event loop and non-blocking I/O model which make it efficient for building applications that handle a lot of I/O (like network requests or filesystem operations) concurrently.

blips.name: Python 3.14 (No-GIL)
blips.description:
Why?

Free-threaded Python unlocks genuine multi-core parallelism without multiprocessing overhead — making it compelling for CPU-bound data processing, LLM inference pipelines, and concurrent agent workloads where the GIL has historically forced workarounds like ProcessPoolExecutor or moving logic to C extensions.

Description

A fast, zero-dependency Python library that enforces type hints at runtime using a novel "O(1)" checking algorithm — catching type mismatches on function calls without the performance overhead of traditional runtime type checkers like typeguard.

blips.name: Python 3.9 and Lower
blips.description:
Why?

Python 3.9 reached end-of-life in October 2025, meaning no security patches, no bug fixes, and no support for newer libraries increasingly requiring 3.11+ to leverage performance improvements and modern typing features.

Description

Python versions 3.9 and earlier, which reached end-of-life in October 2025. These versions lack modern features like structural pattern matching and improved error messages from 3.10+.

blips.name: Python for WebUI
blips.description:
Why?

Keep working with Python for WebUI in POC LLM apps because it enables rapid prototyping with minimal code using tools like Streamlit, Gradio, or FastAPI.

Description

Using Python for WebUI is an excellent choice for building proof-of-concept (POC) LLM apps, thanks to its simplicity, rapid prototyping capabilities, and strong ecosystem. Frameworks like Streamlit, Gradio, and FastAPI allow developers to quickly create interactive interfaces to test prompts, visualize responses, and connect to LLMs via APIs. These tools require minimal front-end code and offer seamless integration with libraries like LangChain, Hugging Face Transformers, or OpenAI’s SDKs. For early-stage experimentation and user feedback, Python-based WebUIs enable fast iteration and deployment without the need for complex UI development.

blips.name: Python multithreading - Loky, JobLib
blips.description:
Why?

✅ Advantages of Loky

  1. Bypasses the GIL
    • Uses separate processes, enabling true parallel execution of CPU-bound tasks.
  2. Cross-platform compatibility
    • Works reliably on Windows, macOS, and Linux, unlike some issues with Python’s built-in multiprocessing.
  3. Reusable Executors
    • Avoids the overhead of creating new processes repeatedly (via getreusableexecutor).
  4. Robust error handling
    • Better traceback, exception propagation, and child process management.
  5. Supports complex objects
    • Can serialize and handle functions with closures or lambda expressions. ✅ Advantages of Joblib
  6. High-level simplicity
    • Makes parallelizing loops and function calls very easy with just a few lines of code.
  7. Built-in caching
    • Can cache function outputs to avoid recomputation — great for expensive or repeated operations.
  8. Optimized for numerical tasks
    • Works well with NumPy, pandas, and is heavily used in scikit-learn for model training.
  9. Automatic backend selection
    • Uses Loky by default, but can switch to threading or dask if needed.
  10. Scales easily
    • Efficient use of multi-core CPUs, helping speed up data-intensive or compute-heavy applications. 💡 Summary Feature Loky Joblib GIL Bypass ✅ ✅ (via Loky) Parallelism Type Process-based High-level abstraction Ease of Use Moderate Very easy Best Use Case Custom task execution Parallel loops, ML tasks Advanced Features Reusable executors, robust Caching, seamless loop parallelism Let me know if you'd like help integrating either of these into a real project or benchmark example.

Description

Python multithreading is a way to run multiple threads (smaller units of a process) simultaneously within a single Python program. However, because of the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) in CPython, true parallel execution of threads is limited, especially for CPU-bound tasks. That's where alternatives like Loky and Joblib come in — they work around these limitations.

blips.name: PyTorch
blips.description:
Why?

Today PyTorch is very popular, head to head with TensorFlow. Very easy to use (much more easy to develop then in TensorFlow) and to deploy. It’s becoming the new benchmark and definitely gaining more popularity than TensorFlow in terms of ease if use and model deployment.

Description

PyTorch is an open source deep learning framework built to be flexible and modular for research, with the stability and support needed for production deployment. PyTorch provides a Python package for high-level features like tensor computation (like NumPy) with strong GPU acceleration and TorchScript for an easy transition between eager mode and graph mode. With the latest release of PyTorch, the framework provides graph-based execution, distributed training, mobile deployment, and quantization.

blips.name: Quarkus
blips.description:
Why?

This framework brings JVM based languages back into micro-services and cloud environments. It provides fast boot time, low RSS memory, offers near instant scale up and high density memory utilization in container orchestration platforms like Kubernetes. By understanding JavaScript, TypeScript saves you time catching errors and providing fixes before you run code.agen

Description

Quarkus is an Open Source stack to write Java applications offering unparalleled startup time, memory footprint and developer experience. It offers familiar programming models and APIs (Hibernate, JAX-RS, Eclipse Vert.x, Apache Camel, Eclipse MicroProfile, Spring API compatibility and more).

It should be on our “Try”, as this framework brings JVM based languages back into microservices and cloud environments.

blips.name: RabbitMQ
blips.description:
Why?

A solid a long time queue messaging system. It has been around for a long time, and has multiple queue features. GUI is very intuitive to use

Description

RabbitMQ is lightweight and easy to deploy on premises and in the cloud. It supports multiple messaging protocols. RabbitMQ can be deployed in distributed and federated configurations to meet high-scale, high-availability requirements

blips.name: Radix UI
blips.description:
Why?

Radix UI is moved to KEEP as the current industry standard for accessible, headless UI components, offering complete design flexibility and superior performance without the styling bloat of traditional libraries.

Description

Radix UI is an open-source set of headless React UI components (primitives) focused on accessibility and customization.

blips.name: RAG
blips.description:
Why?

RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) enhances the accuracy, relevance, and reliability of language model outputs by grounding them in real, up-to-date information. Unlike standalone LLMs, RAG systems reduce hallucinations and improve trust by retrieving and incorporating external knowledge at query time. This makes them ideal for dynamic, domain-specific use cases—such as customer support, search, and internal knowledge tools—where context and correctness are critical. As AI demands grow, RAG remains a scalable and adaptable foundation for building intelligent, context-aware applications.

Description

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a technique in natural language processing that combines the strengths of retrieval-based and generative models by fetching relevant documents from a large corpus and using them to generate more accurate and contextually appropriate responses. This approach enhances the quality of generated text by grounding it in retrieved information, improving the factuality and relevance of the output.

blips.name: Node.js + Typescript
blips.description:
Why?

Node.js uses an event-driven, non-blocking I/O model that makes it lightweight and efficient.

Typescript adds type safety to Node.js and it has become, for new project, in use, more than javascript written node.js,and we feel that typescript has become the standard language to rite node application with.

Description

Using TypeScript with Node.js provides numerous advantages that revolve around improving the reliability, scalability, and productivity of your application development process.

blips.name: Rancher Desktop
blips.description:
Why?

Rancher desktop offers a simple local Kubernetes setup, intuitive UI. you can use it for local development and testing kubernetes based applications

Description

an open-source desktop application that brings Kubernetes and container management to the desktop. It runs on Windows, macOS and Linux. Rancher Desktop uses the same container runtime as Kubernetes. Built images are immediately available to use in your local workloads without any pushing, pulling, or copying.

blips.name: Ray
blips.description:
Why?

Ray simplifies building and scaling distributed applications, making it easier to run complex workloads like machine learning, data processing, and model serving across multiple machines. Ray provides a unified framework with powerful libraries for tasks like training (Ray Train), hyperparameter tuning (Ray Tune), and reinforcement learning (RLlib), all while handling the hard parts of parallelism and resource scheduling. Its flexibility and ecosystem continue to grow, making it a reliable foundation for high-performance, scalable AI and Python applications.

Description

Ray is a framework for scaling AI and Python applications

blips.name: React
blips.description:
Why?

React is still the most popular front-end library, and its ecosystem and community support are unparalleled. It continuously adapts (e.g., introducing Hooks, and more recently Concurrent Mode and Server Components) to stay on the cutting edge of web development.

Description

React is a JavaScript library for building user interfaces, originally released by Facebook (Meta). It uses a component-based architecture and a virtual DOM diffing algorithm to efficiently update the UI in response to data changes. Developers create components either as classes or (more commonly now) as functions using Hooks for state and lifecycle management.

blips.name: React Compiler
blips.description:
Why?

Evaluating its ability to automatically optimize re-renders and eliminate the need for manual memoization (useMemo/useCallback).

Description

An experimental Rust-based compiler that automatically optimizes React components by memoizing renders, reducing the need for manual useMemo/useCallback.

blips.name: React Router 7
blips.description:
Why?

React Router 7 introduces significant enhancements that align it more closely with full-stack needs (like data loading and mutations in route definitions, inspired by Remix). It builds on the solid foundation of v6 but adds these new “framework” capabilities.

Description

React Router 7 is the latest major version of the popular routing library for React. It maintains the declarative routing approach of v6 (nested routes, etc.) but adds new features such as built-in data loaders and actions for routes, enabling fetching and mutations as part of the routing logic.

blips.name: React Server Components
blips.description:
Why?

React Server Components (RSC) represent a new paradigm that can drastically improve performance by offloading component rendering to the server when appropriate. This means less JavaScript sent to the client for those parts of the UI, which can speed up load times.

Description

React Server Components (RSC) are a feature that allows components to run on the server side, then be seamlessly stitched into a client-side React application.

blips.name: Reactive Programming
blips.description:
Why?

Reactive programming (with tools like RxJS) remains highly relevant for managing complex asynchronous workflows, especially when multiple events or data streams interact.

Description

Reactive Programming is a programming paradigm oriented around data flows and the propagation of change. In practice, this often means using observables or similar constructs to represent streams of values over time, and observers (or subscribers) to react to new values. When an observable emits a new value, all dependent computations automatically react and update.

blips.name: Recoil
blips.description:
Why?

Recoil was an experimental state management library from Facebook that showed promise for managing React state in an atom/selectors model.

Description

Recoil is a state management library for React that introduces a global state paradigm using atoms and selectors. An atom is a piece of state, and components can subscribe to atoms (similar to using React’s Context but more granular). Selectors derive new pieces of state from atoms, and are updated automatically when their upstream atoms change.

blips.name: Redux
blips.description:
Why?

Writing Redux without helper libraries (“vanilla” Redux) involves a lot of boilerplate and ceremony, which is why Redux Toolkit was created. Maintaining action type constants, action creators, and switch-case reducers by hand is error-prone and slow.

Description

Vanilla Redux refers to using Redux in the traditional way: defining action type constants, creating action creator functions, and writing reducers (typically big switch statements or if/else chains) to update state based on those actions. This approach served well to enforce a predictable flow of data in apps, but it required a lot of repetitive code.

blips.name: Redux Toolkit
blips.description:
Why?

moved to STOP because its boilerplate-heavy architecture introduces unnecessary "noise" and complexity compared to modern, leaner alternatives like Zustand and TanStack Query, which provide more efficient state management with significantly less overhead.

Description

Redux Toolkit (RTK) is the official toolkit for Redux that simplifies configuring a Redux store and writing reducers and actions.

blips.name: npm Workspaces
blips.description:
Why?

Workspaces were introduced with NPM 7 and come as native node alternatives to Yarn workspaces & Lerna. We suggest trying those because on one hand it comes from NPM itself, and on the other hand there may be some better alternatives such as Nrwl Nx.

npm workspaces have the same abilities as yarn workspaces, including running a script inside a workspace, linking between workspaces as dependencies, and faster installation in case of shared dependencies.

Description

npm workspaces is an npm feature for managing multiple packages in one repository, sharing dependencies, and linking local packages automatically.

blips.name: Nx
blips.description:
Why?

For teams managing monorepos, Nx provides significant productivity boosts through its integrated toolset. It simplifies the management of complex project structures, optimizes build processes, and improves code sharing and reuse. Its maturity and broad adoption in the developer community make it a reliable choice for new projects.

Description

Nx is a set of extensible dev tools for monorepos, which helps manage projects with multiple applications and libraries. It provides features like code generation, dependency management, and build optimization.

blips.name: OCI Images
blips.description:
Why?

OCI images are the next thing after "Docker images". Docker was the pioneer in defining and implementing a container image format. However, these days, the Cloud-Native ecosystem prefer to work with open standards and decouple the image format from the executable that runs it. So the "Open Container Initiative" (OCI) community wrote an open specification, how a container image should look like from binary format point of view. The specification is very close to the original Docker image format, however, because it's now an open standard, we start seeing tools from other vendors that do OCI image creation (RedHat's Buildah) and OCI image running (RedHat's Podman).

Description

The Open Container Initiative is an open governance structure for the express purpose of creating open industry standards around container formats and runtimes.

blips.name: Repo-Aware Context Tools
blips.description:
Why?

Developers adopt repo-aware context tools primarily to overcome the limitations of context-isolated AI assistants. These tools eliminate the repetitive task of explaining codebase architecture and conventions to AI systems, which consumes valuable developer time and often results in suggestions that violate project-specific patterns. By automatically understanding code relationships, inheritance hierarchies, and custom abstractions across the entire repository, they reduce cognitive overhead and minimize friction in the development workflow. The integration allows AI assistance to align with team-specific coding standards and architectural decisions, generating more accurate and immediately usable suggestions while decreasing the likelihood of introducing inconsistencies or architectural violations.

Description

Repo-aware context tools index entire codebases to build semantic representations of project structure, dependencies, and patterns. Unlike traditional AI assistants that process isolated snippets, these systems construct knowledge graphs of project-specific APIs, custom abstractions, and control flows. They leverage file hierarchies, git history, and import relationships to provide context-aware code completion, refactoring suggestions, and documentation that respect existing conventions without requiring manual context explanation from developers.

blips.name: Requirements.txt in Python
blips.description:
Why?

requirements.txt has no lockfile semantics, no dependency resolution, no dev/prod separation, and no environment management — replaced by modern tools like uv or Poetry that handle all of this properly.

Description

A requirements.txt file is a simple text file used in Python projects to specify the external packages and libraries that your project depends on, along with their versions. It serves as a package dependency declaration.

blips.name: Restate.dev
blips.description:
Why?

If you're building AI agents, data pipelines, or microservice workflows that need guaranteed execution and resumability without the operational weight of Temporal or the complexity of rolling your own retry/state logic, Restate lets you write durable workflows as plain async functions — making it the fastest path to production-grade reliability for event-driven or agent orchestration workloads where partial failures and long-running processes are the norm.

Description

A durable execution platform that combines workflow orchestration with durable promises, enabling reliable distributed applications without manual state management or retry logic.

blips.name: RisingWave
blips.description:
Why?

RisingWave replaces the complex Kafka + Flink + serving database stack with a single Postgres-compatible system — dramatically reducing operational overhead for teams that need real-time materialized views, streaming aggregations, or CDC pipelines without the engineering cost of maintaining a full Flink deployment.

Description

A cloud-native streaming SQL database that ingests data from Kafka, Kinesis, and CDC sources, processes it with incremental materialized views, and serves results via a Postgres-compatible API — combining stream processing and serving in a single system.

blips.name: Rive
blips.description:
Why?

Positioned as the successor to Lottie, offering significantly smaller file sizes and real-time interactive animations.

Description

A real-time interactive design and animation tool that renders vector animations and state machines natively across platforms, offering an alternative to Lottie with built-in interactivity.

blips.name: Octant
blips.description:
Why?

If we need easy and clear observability on our K8S cluster, OCTANT is a very useful option.

Description

Octant is an open source developer-centric web interface for Kubernetes that lets you inspect a Kubernetes cluster and its applications

blips.name: Rolldown
blips.description:
Why?

Rolldown is the "future of Vite." By moving the bundling logic to Rust while maintaining API compatibility with Rollup, it solves the performance gap between development (usually handled by Esbuild) and production builds. Adopting it or following its progress now prepares you for the next generation of ultra-fast web build pipelines.

Description

A Rust-based JavaScript bundler from the Vite team, designed as a faster, Rollup-compatible alternative built for the next generation of Vite.

blips.name: Rollup - library bundling
blips.description:
Why?

Rollup specializes in bundling libraries and is known for producing smaller, tree-shakable bundles. It’s easier to configure for library outputs than Webpack and often yields better results for that use-case (like publishing NPM packages or design systems).

Description

Rollup is a module bundler often used for bundling JavaScript libraries. It has a focus on ES module input and output, which enables powerful tree-shaking – dead code elimination to remove unused exports. Rollup is commonly used to bundle libraries into formats like UMD or ESM for distribution.

blips.name: OIDC
blips.description:
Why?

OIDC is still popular and successful in the security world.

Description

OpenID Connect (OIDC) is an open authentication protocol that profiles and extends OAuth 2.0 to add an identity layer. OIDC allows clients to confirm an end user’s identity using authentication by an authorization server. Implementing OIDC on top of OAuth 2.0 creates a single framework that promises to secure APIs, mobile native applications and browser applications in a single, cohesive architecture.

blips.name: Rust
blips.description:
Why?

Rust can be a great choice when you are developing an application where performance and safety are crucial. It's good for web, backend, embedded, and system.

Description

Performance Rust is blazingly fast and memory-efficient: with no runtime or garbage collector, it can power performance-critical services, run on embedded devices, and easily integrate with other languages.

Reliability Rust’s rich type system and ownership model guarantee memory-safety and thread-safety — and enable you to eliminate many classes of bugs at compile-time.

Productivity Rust has great documentation, a friendly compiler with useful error messages, and top-notch tooling — an integrated package manager and build tool, smart multi-editor support with auto-completion and type inspections, an auto-formatter, and more.

blips.name: S3 tables
blips.description:
Why?

S3 Tables removes the biggest pain point of self-managed Iceberg on S3 — compaction, file management, and catalog ops — making it compelling for AWS-native lakehouse teams who want production-grade Iceberg tables without running a separate catalog (Glue, Polaris, Nessie) or managing table maintenance jobs themselves.

Description

S3 tables refer to a data architecture pattern where structured data is stored directly in Amazon S3 using open table formats like Iceberg, Delta Lake, or Hudi. These tables enable scalable, cost-effective analytics by separating storage from compute and allowing query engines like Athena, Trino, or Spark to read data in place. S3 tables support features like schema evolution, ACID transactions, and time travel, making them ideal for modern data lakehouse architectures.

blips.name: S3 Vectors
blips.description:
Why?

S3 Vectors eliminates the operational overhead of running a dedicated vector store like Pinecone or Weaviate for teams already on AWS — if your RAG pipeline lives in the AWS ecosystem, native vector search directly on S3 dramatically simplifies architecture and reduces infrastructure cost and latency.

Description

S3 Vectors is Amazon's native vector storage capability built directly into S3, allowing teams to store, index, and query vector embeddings as first-class objects within S3 buckets — without provisioning a separate vector database

blips.name: Sass & Less
blips.description:
Why?

With the advent of CSS custom properties, native CSS nesting (coming in CSS spec), and improved CSS capabilities, the need for a preprocessor like SCSS has diminished for many projects.

Description

Sass and Less are dynamic preprocessor style sheet languages that compile to CSS.

blips.name: Scala Applications
blips.description:
Why?

Scala's steep learning curve, slow compile times, and JVM overhead make it hard to justify for new projects — with Python dominating data/AI and Go/Rust taking systems work, Scala's niche is shrinking to legacy Spark codebases.

Description

Scala combines object-oriented and functional programming in one concise, high-level language. Scala’s static types help avoid bugs in complex applications, and its JVM and JavaScript runtimes let you build high-performance systems with easy access to huge ecosystems of libraries.

Due to the over academization of the language and abundance of features, it has had low adoption.

Our current position is that scala has moved to the maintenance only, and new projects should shy away from using scala

blips.name: OnPrem FaaS
blips.description:
Why?

The function framework based on Kubernetes can give a framework to implement the event-driven architecture, It gives easy to deploy with scale and monitor out of the box.

Description

AWS was the first provider to offer "functions as a service" already in AWS initially released AWS lambda as an event-driven provisioning/operations and took just under 3 years to become the standard name of serverless and FaaS offerings.

AWS, as it’s competitors, offer Lambdas (a.k.a functions), as a complementary to their BaaS offerings, stitching together services such as:  Incognito  S3  CloudFormation  DynamoDB  RDS and many more These integrations alongside Lambda’s “infinite” scalability and it’s newly introduced (at the time) “Price per 100ms” made it very popular among both startups achieving their MVP and enterprises wishing to scale out or experiment with Serverless and Micro Services Architectures. AWS Lambda provides many organizations the ability to write functions in a variety of Software languages and integrates well with many frameworks and other IaaS/PaaS/BaaS services.

More about AWS Lambda here

Google functions enable Serverless applications based on GCP IaaS offerings. Cloud Functions lets application developers spin up code on demand in response to events originating from any API / HTTP request. Serverless architectures utilizing Google Functions integrated with Google Endpoints and BaaS services could build applications that scale from zero to infinity, on-demand - without provisioning or managing a single server.

As other serverless and function providers, google’s functions are the best fitted for Backend services such as Firebase, Cloud Datastore, and ML solutions also offered by the GCP.

More info on google functions in the following

blips.name: Selenium
blips.description:
Why?

Selenium’s browser automation has been a standard for years, but it requires managing browser drivers and infrastructure which is cumbersome.

Description

Selenium is a suite of tools for automating web browsers. Its most well-known component, Selenium WebDriver, controls a browser by simulating user actions, which allowed QA engineers to write end-to-end tests in various programming languages. Selenium supports a wide range of browsers and was a key tool for cross-browser testing.

blips.name: Self-Serving Data Platform
blips.description:
Why?

The best way to bring data to the full range of the company without the need to teach all of the technologies

Description

The self serving platform is a tooling platform that brings the implementation of the data mesh concept to developers across the company

blips.name: OPA - Open Policy Agent
blips.description:
Why?

Managing organization-level policies has always been a challenge, in the era of Kubernetes and Container orchestration, OPA is a framework that enables Cluster Administrators to provide a framework of managing policies in a common and declarative manner. OPA is a lightweight general-purpose policy engine that can be co-located with your service. You can integrate OPA as a sidecar, host-level daemon, or library.

Description

Policy-based control for cloud native environments

blips.name: Server-Side Rendering (SSR)
blips.description:
Why?

Despite the rise of client-side single-page apps, SSR remains crucial for performance and SEO. Serving HTML content from the server (especially for the initial page load) gives users a faster first paint and allows search engines and social media crawlers to easily parse content.

Description

Server-side rendering (SSR) is the process of generating the HTML of a web page on the server instead of in the browser. The server produces the full HTML for a page (often based on application state or data), which the client can display immediately.

blips.name: OpenEBS
blips.description:
Why?

Since OpenEBS volumes are managed independently, organizations can enable collaboration between small, loosely coupled teams. Storage parameters for each volume and workload can be monitored independently, allowing for the granular management of storage policies.

Description

OpenEBS builds on Kubernetes to enable Stateful applications to easily access Dynamic Local PVs or Replicated PVs. By using the Container Attached Storage pattern users report lower costs, easier management, and more control for their teams

blips.name: OpenShift
blips.description:
Why?

OpenShift is a comprehensive, enterprise-ready solution that extends Kubernetes with additional features tailored for production environments. Its robust security, scalability, and support for hybrid cloud deployments make it a strong candidate for continued use, especially in large organizations seeking a mature, supported Kubernetes distribution.

Description

OpenShift is a Kubernetes platform by Red Hat that offers enterprise-grade features for container orchestration, including enhanced security, developer productivity tools, and integrated CI/CD pipelines.

blips.name: OpenTelemetry
blips.description:
Why?

A vendor-agnostic proxy that can receive, process, and export telemetry data.

Description

OpenTelemetry collector is a tool that in a powerful way receives data from multiple sources, transforms it, and sends it to the destinations you like. We can scrape Prometheus metrics with the OpenTelemetry Collector and send them to a remote write destination like Grafana Cloud.

blips.name: shadcn/ui
blips.description:
Why?

shadcn/ui is moved to KEEP because it provides full code ownership with zero runtime abstraction, and a CLI-first architecture optimized for AI coding agents and "v0-style" rapid development.

Description

shadcn/ui is a set of beautifully-designed, accessible React components and a code distribution platform. Rather than a traditional install-and-use component library, it provides the actual source code of each component (via a CLI or copy-paste) so that developers can fully customize and own the code.

blips.name: Podman
blips.description:
Why?

Does not require a daemon and can run rootless (the container can still run as a root inside).

Description

Podman: A tool for managing OCI containers and pods https://github.com/containers/podman

blips.name: Polyglot Programming
blips.description:
Why?

With the architecture of micro-services and platforms such as GraalVM, it is becoming more and more rewarding to choose the right language for the right service.

Description

Polyglot programming is the practice of writing code in multiple languages to capture additional functionality and efficiency not available in a single language. The use of domain-specific languages (DSLs) has become a standard practice for enterprise application development. For example, a mobile development team might employ Java, JavaScript and HTML5 to create a fully functional application. Other DSLs such as SQL (for data queries), XML (embedded configuration) and CSS (document formatting) are often built into enterprise applications as well. One developer may be proficient in multiple languages, or a team with varying language skills may work together to perform polyglot programming.

blips.name: Popeye
blips.description:
Why?

A very good tool to scan k8s and report on potential issues. it detects misconfigurations and helps you to ensure that best practices are in place, thus preventing future headaches.

Description

Popeye is a utility that scans live Kubernetes clusters and reports potential issues with deployed resources and configurations. It sanitizes your cluster based on what's deployed and not what's sitting on disk.

By scanning your cluster, it detects misconfigurations and helps you to ensure that best practices are in place, thus preventing future headaches. It aims at reducing the cognitive overload one faces when operating a Kubernetes cluster in the wild.

Furthermore, if your cluster employs a metric-server, it reports potential resources over/under allocations and attempts to warn you should your cluster run out of capacity.

blips.name: SLMs
blips.description:
Why?

SLMs make on-device and low-latency LLM inference practical without GPU clusters — for teams building agents, copilots, or classification pipelines where data privacy, inference cost, or edge deployment matter, a well-chosen SLM often matches GPT-4-class performance on narrow tasks at a fraction of the cost and complexity.

Description

Small language models (SLMs) are computational models that can respond to and generate natural language. SLMs are trained to perform specific tasks using fewer resources than larger models.

blips.name: Presto
blips.description:
Why?

As data keeps piling up and more and more data lakes are being created the need to query it all in an efficient manner is just getting higher. Presto is a great solution to perform simple SQL queries on any underlying data. Many companies have already adopted this query engine and we suggest keeping this technology.

Description

Presto is a meta-search engine. Its 2 killer features are:

  • Able to join from a multitude of different DBs (i.e. join a MySql table with a Hive table)
  • Uses a distributed architecture to run the query so it is able to query very BIG amounts DATA without the need to use workarounds such as map/reduce or spark to run SQL queries

blips.name: Snowflake
blips.description:
Why?

Snowflake is commonly used, scalable, with SQL support, and very good performance

Description

SaaS data-lake and data-warehouse

blips.name: SolidJS
blips.description:
Why?

SolidJS is a highly performant reactive UI library, but its ecosystem and community are still relatively small compared to React, Vue, or Angular. Adopting SolidJS could introduce risk in terms of hiring developers or finding support, given its niche status.

Description

SolidJS is a front-end library for building UIs that emphasizes performance through fine-grained reactivity. Inspired by React’s JSX syntax but without a virtual DOM, Solid tracks direct dependencies and updates only the necessary parts of the DOM on state changes.

blips.name: Promxy
blips.description:
Why?

Promxy is a Prometheus proxy that makes many shards of Prometheus appear as a single API endpoint to the user. This significantly simplifies operations and use of Prometheus at scale (when you have more than one Prometheus host). Promxy delivers this unified access endpoint without requiring any sidecars, custom builds, or other changes to your Prometheus infrastructure.

Description

A Prometheus proxy that aggregates and deduplicates queries across multiple Prometheus servers, enabling unified querying of federated Prometheus deployments.

blips.name: Spec-Driven Development
blips.description:
Why?

Spec-Driven Development forces clarity before code — reducing LLM hallucination drift, aligning teams on intent upfront, and creating auditable, versionable specs that make AI-generated code more predictable, reviewable, and maintainable at scale.

Description

An AI-assisted toolkit for generating technical specifications, requirements, and design docs from high-level prompts.

blips.name: Spring Boot
blips.description:
Why?

Spring boot's opinionated view of your application configuration makes developing a Spring application much easier than it used to be prior to its introduction. In addition it allows creating self contained application which are much more suitable to micro-services architecture.

Description

Spring Boot makes it easy to create stand-alone, production-grade Spring based Applications that you can "just run". By creating an opinionated view of the Spring platform and third-party libraries, you can get started with minimum fuss.

blips.name: Spring Cloud
blips.description:
Why?

Spring Cloud's heavyweight XML/annotation config, slow startup times, and Java-first assumptions make it a poor fit for modern cloud-native architectures — where lighter alternatives like Quarkus, Micronaut, or non-JVM service meshes (Istio, Linkerd) do the job with far less overhead.

Description

Spring Cloud provides tools for developers to quickly build some of the common patterns in distributed systems. Coordination of distributed systems leads to boilerplate patterns, and using Spring Cloud developers can quickly span up services and applications that implement those patterns. They will work well in any distributed environment, including the developer’s own laptop, bare metal data centers, and managed platforms such as Cloud Foundry.

blips.name: SQLMesh
blips.description:
Why?

SQLMesh brings software engineering rigor to SQL transformations — with built-in state awareness, virtual environments for zero-copy testing, automatic change impact analysis, and dbt compatibility — making it the most compelling modern alternative for teams outgrowing dbt.

Description

SQLMesh is an open-source data transformation framework that brings the best practices of DevOps to data teams. It enables data scientists, analysts, and engineers to efficiently run and deploy data transformations written in SQL or Python. It has native support for running dbt projects.

blips.name: SQLModel
blips.description:
Why?

SQLModel is the natural choice for FastAPI + PostgreSQL stacks — defining your data model once for both database persistence and API validation cuts boilerplate significantly, and its Pydantic v2 foundation means you get type safety, serialization, and schema generation for free without maintaining parallel model definitions.

Description

SQLModel is a library for interacting with SQL databases from Python code, with Python objects. It is designed to be intuitive, easy to use, highly compatible, and robust.

blips.name: Prowler
blips.description:
Why?

Prowler is a command-line tool that helps you with AWS security assessment, auditing, hardening, and incident response.

Description

Prowler is small project which provides a CLI for AWS Security Best Practices Assessment, Auditing, Hardening and Forensics Readiness Tool. It follows guidelines of the CIS Amazon Web Services Foundations Benchmark (49 checks) and has more than 100 additional checks including related to GDPR, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, ISO-27001, FFIEC, SOC2 and others. Read more about CIS Amazon Web Services Foundations Benchmark v1.2.0 - 05-23-2018

blips.name: Pulumi
blips.description:
Why?

By using Pulumi over the likes of terraform, you can move from static configuration to procedural programming, and enhance the scenarios that you can support.

Description

Pulumi lets you define infrastructure using real programming languages (TypeScript, Python, Go, etc.) instead of declarative configs, giving you more flexibility and reuse for complex infrastructure setups.

blips.name: StarRocks
blips.description:
Why?

StarRocks bridges the gap between real-time serving and lake querying in a single engine — for teams needing Clickhouse-level query speed on live data plus the ability to query their lakehouse directly without ETL, it's a compelling alternative to maintaining separate OLAP and lake query engines like Trino + ClickHouse side by side.

Description

StarRocks s a high-performance, real-time SQL database for analytics. It’s designed to run super-fast queries on large data, supports real-time updates, and works well for dashboards, data lakes, and big data apps.

blips.name: Rancher
blips.description:
Why?

Rancher is a complete software stack for teams adopting containers. It addresses the operational and security challenges of managing multiple Kubernetes clusters across any infrastructure while providing DevOps teams with integrated tools for running containerized workloads.

Description

Rancher not only deploys production-grade Kubernetes clusters from datacenter to cloud to the edge, it also unites them with centralized authentication, access control and observability.

Rancher lets you streamline cluster deployment on bare metal, private clouds, public clouds or vSphere and secure them using global security policies.

blips.name: Streaming Databases
blips.description:
Why?

If your team is maintaining a brittle stack of Kafka + Flink + Redis/Postgres just to serve fresh aggregations or real-time dashboards, a streaming database collapses that complexity into a single SQL-first system — dramatically reducing engineering overhead for use cases like live metrics, fraud detection, CDC-powered projections, or AI feature stores where data freshness and query latency both matter.

Description

Streaming databases like RisingWave and Materialize are designed to process real-time data continuously as it arrives, enabling low-latency, SQL-based analytics without the need for batch ETL pipelines.

blips.name: Styled Components
blips.description:
Why?

Styled-components pioneered CSS-in-JS, but it comes with runtime costs (injecting styles via JavaScript) and can lead to larger bundle sizes due to its styling overhead. Moreover, the team announced that they are stopping its development.

Description

styled-components is a CSS-in-JS library for React and React Native. It lets you create React components with encapsulated styles, using tagged template literals to write actual CSS that gets attached to the components. This approach ensures that styles are tied to the components they belong to, avoiding conflicts in large applications.

blips.name: Supabase
blips.description:
Why?

Supabase delivers a full Postgres-backed backend with auth, realtime subscriptions, storage, and auto-generated APIs out of the box — making it the fastest path to production for teams that want Firebase-level DX without abandoning SQL or open-source portability.

Description

Supabase is an open-source backend-as-a-service (BaaS) that provides a scalable and feature-rich alternative to Firebase, built on top of PostgreSQL. It offers instant APIs, real-time subscriptions, authentication, and edge functions—allowing developers to build full-stack applications quickly with a powerful SQL database and modern tooling.

blips.name: Svelte
blips.description:
Why?

Svelte’s compile-time approach (no virtual DOM, compiling components to imperative code) gives it excellent performance and small bundles.

Description

Svelte is a front-end compiler and framework that takes a different approach than frameworks like React or Vue. Instead of doing heavy lifting in the browser, Svelte compiles your components to efficient JavaScript at build time. It reacts to state changes by updating the DOM directly, without an intermediate virtual DOM.

blips.name: Reflector
blips.description:
Why?

Using the Kubernetes Reflector tool enhances the efficiency and reliability of managing cluster state by mirroring critical resources and ensuring high availability. It simplifies the synchronization process, reduces downtime, and improves disaster recovery capabilities, making it an essential tool for robust Kubernetes operations.

Description

Reflector is a Kubernetes addon designed to monitor changes to resources (secrets and configmaps) and reflect changes to mirror resources in the same or other namespaces.

blips.name: Reloader
blips.description:
Why?

A robust tool to reload pods, if a relevant configmap or secret is changed.

Description

Reloader can watch changes in ConfigMap and Secret and do rolling upgrades on Pods with their associated DeploymentConfigs, Deployments, Daemonsets Statefulsets and Rollouts.

blips.name: Tailwind CSS
blips.description:
Why?

Tailwind CSS has drastically improved how we write and maintain styles by using utility classes.

Description

Tailwind CSS is a utility-first CSS framework that provides low-level utility classes (like mt-4 for margin-top or text-center for centering text) to construct custom designs. Instead of writing traditional CSS, developers compose these utility classes in their HTML.

blips.name: TanStack Form
blips.description:
Why?

TanStack Form is moved to KEEP because its framework-agnostic, type-safe architecture provides superior performance for complex forms compared to traditional libraries, and its headless nature allows for seamless integration with modern UI components like shadcn/ui.

Description

TanStack Form is a lightweight, headless form library for React applications. It provides a flexible and type-safe way to manage form state and validation with minimal boilerplate. Developers can define form schemas and use hooks to register inputs, track form values, and handle validation feedback.

blips.name: TanStack Query
blips.description:
Why?

TanStack Query (formerly React Query) has become the go-to solution for managing server state (data fetching and caching) in React.

Description

TanStack Query (React Query) is a library for managing asynchronous data (server state) in React applications. It provides hooks such as useQuery and useMutation to fetch, cache, update, and synchronize data between your client and servers with very little code.

blips.name: TanStack Ranger
blips.description:
Why?

Building custom range sliders with multiple handles or ranges can be quite complex. TanStack Ranger offers a modern “headless” solution where the heavy-lifting (state, math for slider positions) is handled for you, and you can plug in your own UI.

Description

TanStack Ranger is a headless range slider library for React (and other frameworks) that provides hooks to manage slider state and logic.

blips.name: TanStack Router
blips.description:
Why?

TanStack Router offers a fresh take on client-side routing with full TypeScript support and route definitions as code (instead of mainly JSX).

Description

TanStack Router is a type-safe routing library for React that treats routes as first-class objects with structured definitions. It enables features like static analysis of routes, code-splitting per route, and data loading mechanisms tied to routes (inspired by modern frameworks).

blips.name: TanStack Start
blips.description:
Why?

A promising full-stack framework leveraging TanStack Router for type-safe, SSR-ready applications.

Description

TanStack Start is a full-stack framework for building server-rendered React (and Solid) applications.

blips.name: TanStack Store
blips.description:
Why?

TanStack Store is a relatively new state management solution that is framework-agnostic and type-safe. It’s designed as the underlying store for TanStack libraries but can be used standalone.

Description

TanStack Store is a framework-agnostic data store library that emphasizes type safety and reactivity. It provides a minimal API to define and manage state, which can then be used across various front-end frameworks through adapters.

blips.name: TanStack Table
blips.description:
Why?

TanStack Table (formerly React Table) is a leading solution for building complex tables and data grids in React without sacrificing flexibility.

Description

TanStack Table is a headless UI library for building powerful tables and data grids for TS/JS frameworks including React, Vue, and Solid. It provides all the underlying functionality (like row/column sorting, filtering, pagination, and even virtual scrolling) without any default UI, so developers can render the table how they want.

blips.name: TanStack Virtual
blips.description:
Why?

TanStack Virtual has quickly become one of the most popular libraries for virtualized lists as of late 2024, standing out for its modern architecture and rich feature set.

Description

TanStack Virtual is a headless library for virtualizing large lists and grids, meaning it only renders items that are currently visible (plus a buffer) to maintain smooth scrolling performance. It's framework-agnostic and highly flexible, supporting variable item heights and horizontal as well as vertical virtualization.

blips.name: SecOps
blips.description:
Why?

As the industry is getting more mature in the "make it work" area, this trend is gaining more and more popularity.

Description

Security Operations, are not new. But we identify more focus on this arena, mainly on the containers world. The CISO position is becoming more dominant. There are several reason for this trends, we think that the main one is the high maturity of the base technologies. Generally, when entering the maturity phase, companies start focusing on security tools and processes.

blips.name: Tauri
blips.description:
Why?

Tauri is an emerging framework for building desktop apps using web technologies but with a Rust-based backend.

Description

Tauri is a framework for building tiny, fast desktop applications using web technologies. Unlike Electron, which bundles a Chromium browser, Tauri uses the OS’s native webview for UI and a Rust backend for application logic, resulting in significantly smaller apps.

blips.name: semantic-release
blips.description:
Why?

This tool manages all the release aspects of a component - including giving an automatic release number, managing release notes etc…

Description

semantic-release automates the whole package release workflow including: determining the next version number, generating the release notes, and publishing the package.

This removes the immediate connection between human emotions and version numbers, strictly following the Semantic Versioning specification and communicating the impact of changes to consumers.

blips.name: Serverless Architecture
blips.description:
Why?

We should put it on “Keep”, as many customers work with this Successful architecture trend, which provides cost-effective architecture from both technical and business levels.

Description

Serverless computing is a cloud computing execution model in which the cloud provider dynamically manages the allocation of machine resources. Serverless is a form of utility computing that helps provide complex infrastructure and security requirements as a part of managed services these services are managed by the provider hence the name serverless { less management of servers }. Serverless should not be confused with the serverless framework …

Serverless framework Serverless.com is a toolkit for deploying and operating serverless architectures, serverless utilizes the different cloud provider’s functions and API-gw API’s to expose backend services.

Highlights:

  • Integrates with main cloud providers - AWS, GCP, Azure Has Kubeless plugin
  • Yaml definition of both API gateway and lambdas
  • Utility to test functions locally using a local docker daemon

blips.name: Temporal
blips.description:
Why?

Temporal provides a reliable and scalable way to manage complex, long-running workflows with built-in state management, retries, and fault tolerance. By handling orchestration transparently and persisting workflow state, Temporal allows developers to write simple, intuitive code for distributed systems without worrying about failure recovery, timeouts, or manual compensation logic. As applications grow in complexity, Temporal continues to offer strong guarantees, operational visibility, and development velocity that traditional task queues or orchestrators often lack.

Description

Temporal is a microservice orchestration platform that enables developers to build scalable applications without sacrificing productivity or reliability. Temporal server executes units of application logic, Workflows, in a resilient manner that automatically handles intermittent failures, and retries failed operations.

blips.name: TensorFlow
blips.description:
Why?

TensorFlow is still very popular and enjoy the support of Google. Keras, which is another widely used ML/DL framework is included and supported in TF projects.

Description

TensorFlow is a set of libraries for building ML models. It is written in C with a facade in Python, which make it both very fast and usable for data scientists. It includes tools for data transformation, model training, evaluation and deployment. Its specialty is in the area of Deep Learning.

blips.name: TensorFlow mobile/lite
blips.description:
Why?

  • Prediction in mobile devices is already incorporated in most of the mobile devices. Having a lite version in TensorFlow gives another important tool for such causes.

Description

Machine learning on mobile devices is offering an array of new and unique user experiences for problems that are close to data people are working on. Experiences that were impossible before, like OCR, image recognition, machine translation, speech recognition, etc, were in the realm of Science Fiction, but they are being brought into our daily lives. Thanks to machine learning on mobile and IoT devices, universal translators from Star Trek, Babel Fish from Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy, “neural net processor, a learning computer” from Terminator 2, and more, are not a figments of writers’ imagination, but actual products that you can buy, or are in development stages.

TensorFlow is an opensource library for dataflow programming, often used in deep learning. It was developed for internal use by the Google Brain team. It was released to the public, and in 2017 mobile/lite version was released that is targeting mobile and embedded/IoT platforms, such as Android, iOS, Rasberry Pi, etc.

blips.name: Serverless DevOps Pipelines
blips.description:
Why?

As part of the serverless architecture trends, We see that this paradigm is also good for DevOps tasks and we use it more and more…

Description

As the growth in popularity of Functions in General and Serverless architecture in specific, varying from Cloud Native/Cloud-based to On-Prem solutions. Serverless architecture and especially the “Function part” has become the go-to tool for many DevOps processes that need automating and in many cases act as the binding context of the by design “loosely coupled” architecture.

As we grow in event-driven processes we will see more and more functions listening on event streams such as SNS on AWS, or NATS, Kafka, etc on tools like OpenFaaS,Knative. There tools/frameworks enable many DevOps teams to achieve their goals in a consistent, monitored and repetitive way, not to mention the replacement of many utilities such as CronJobs, etc.

blips.name: Service Mesh
blips.description:
Why?

Many of the features above are used to achieve all the above techniques using the operator pattern which is accompanied by a controller utilizing annotations and CRDs (Custome Resource Definitions) to manage service meshes @scale such as the following market leaders Netflix, Twitter, Amazon which utilize service meshes to enable smooth day1 and day2 operations.

Description

a service mesh is a dedicated infrastructure layer for facilitating service-to-service communications between services or microservices, using a proxy (often as a sidecar). Examples of popular service meshes are Linkerd, a CNCF project, and Istio

blips.name: ShellCheck, bats, shunit2
blips.description:
Why?

Bash code deserves the same treatment as other programming languages. Linting and Unit Testing always make our code better.

Description

These tools serve unit tests and lint in Bash code. Easily installed with a fast learning curve.

blips.name: Testcontainers
blips.description:
Why?

  1. Reliable and Repeatable Tests
  • Your tests run in the same environment every time, reducing "works on my machine" problems.
  • No need to rely on shared or pre-configured databases or services.
  1. True Integration Testing
  • You test against real versions of databases, message queues, browsers, etc., not mocks or in-memory stand-ins.
  • This increases confidence that your system works in production-like conditions.
  1. Ephemeral and Isolated
  • Containers are started before the test and destroyed afterward.
  • Ensures clean state for each test or test class, preventing flaky tests due to leftover data.
  1. Cross-Technology Support
  • Supports databases like PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB.
  • Also supports Kafka, Elasticsearch, Redis, Selenium browsers, and even custom Docker containers.
  1. Easy to Configure and Use
  • Libraries are available for Java (most mature), Python, .NET, Node.js, and others.
  • You don't need deep Docker knowledge to get started.

Description

Testcontainers is an open source library for providing throwaway, lightweight instances of databases, message brokers, web browsers, or just about anything that can run in a Docker container.

blips.name: Skaffold
blips.description:
Why?

Skaffold is great tool to support local development in kubernetes , You can use the same tool in your CI process too.

Description

Skaffold - CLI tools for developer helping develop application running on Kubernetes by managing the workflow of build, push, deploy of application. Do it continuously for local /remote Kubernetes

It can be used in the CI server to manage the same workflow.

Skaffold has a pluggable architecture, allowing you to create your implementation, and come with support to many tools in each of the steps: Image build - Dockerfile, maven/Gradle (JIB) Deploy - kustomized, helm, Kubernetes manifest

blips.name: SOPS
blips.description:
Why?

Using SOPs (Secrets Operations Protection) to secure secrets ensures consistent, secure management of sensitive information, reducing human error and safeguarding against data breaches. By standardizing procedures for handling secrets, organizations enhance their security posture and compliance, protecting critical assets and maintaining trust.

Description

SOPS is an editor of encrypted files that supports YAML, JSON, ENV, INI and BINARY formats and encrypts with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, age, and PGP.

blips.name: Turborepo
blips.description:
Why?

Turborepo is a modern monorepo tool that impressed us with its remote caching and parallel execution, significantly cutting down CI times. It’s simpler to adopt for some projects than Nx (less configuration needed if we just want caching and basic task running).

Description

Turborepo is a high-performance build system for JavaScript and TypeScript monorepos. It focuses on caching and optimizing task running – for example, if nothing changed in a package since the last build, Turborepo can skip rebuilding it and even reuse cached results from a remote cache (like on CI or a shared cache server).

blips.name: TypeScript
blips.description:
Why?

TypeScript has become the default for us because it catches errors at compile time that would otherwise only surface at runtime.

Description

TypeScript is a superset of JavaScript that introduces optional static typing and other language features (like interfaces, enums, generics). It compiles to plain JavaScript and helps developers catch errors early and write more self-documented code.

blips.name: UnJS
blips.description:
Why?

UnJS is a collection of JavaScript/TypeScript utilities and tools (coming from the Nuxt community) that aim to solve common problems in a framework-agnostic way. Because these tools are designed to be lightweight and composable, they can potentially replace heavier solutions in our stack.

Description

UnJS is an open-source initiative that provides a suite of utilities for Node.js and JavaScript projects, many of which originated from the Nuxt.js ecosystem. Examples of UnJS libraries include ohmyfetch (a light-fetch wrapper), consola (for logging), and unstorage (a uniform storage API).

blips.name: uv
blips.description:
Why?

uv (a fast Python package manager) significantly speeds up dependency resolution, installation, and virtual environment creation—making development workflows much faster and more efficient. Built as a drop-in replacement for pip and venv, uv combines performance with reliability, handling complex dependency graphs quickly without compromising accuracy. As projects grow in size and complexity, uv continues to offer a smoother experience with consistent builds, modern tooling support, and improved developer productivity.

Description

Uv is a relatively new Python package manager that is gaining traction due to its speed. Uv is written in Rust, a language known for its performance. This makes it significantly faster than Python's standard package manager, pip. Benchmarks show it can be 10-100 times faster

blips.name: v0
blips.description:
Why?

An essential generative UI tool by Vercel for rapid prototyping and AI-driven component scaffolding.

Description

v0 is an AI-driven development tool that converts natural language descriptions into code and UI. Essentially, it's a pair programming assistant: you describe an idea (e.g., “a Next.js blog with a signup form”), and v0 generates the necessary code for you.

blips.name: Valtio
blips.description:
Why?

Valtio provides a very straightforward way to manage state using JavaScript proxies – you just mutate an object and the UI updates. This aligns with how developers naturally think, lowering the learning curve for global state.

Description

Valtio is a tiny state management library that uses ES6 proxies to make an object reactive. With Valtio, you create a proxy state (e.g., const state = proxy({ count: 0 })) and then directly mutate it (state.count++), and any React components that use that state (via the useSnapshot hook) will re-render automatically.

blips.name: StackStorm
blips.description:
Why?

StackStorm is a mature and powerful automation tool with a broad user base and extensive integrations.
