Its ability to handle complex automation workflows and event-driven tasks makes it a valuable asset for maintaining operational efficiency and reducing manual intervention. Its proven track record justifies its continued use.

Description

StackStorm is an open-source event-driven automation platform that allows users to automate routine tasks, respond to events, and manage workflows across various systems and applications.

blips.name: Syft
blips.description:
Why?

A CLI tool and Go library for generating a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) from container images and filesystems. Exceptional for vulnerability detection when used with a scanner like Grype.

Description

A very simple tool to explore docker images and generating Software Bill Of Materials.

blips.name: VectorDB
blips.description:
Why?

Teams should keep using Vector Databases (VectorDBs) because they are essential for powering high-performance semantic search, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and other LLM-driven applications. VectorDBs are optimized for storing and querying high-dimensional embeddings, enabling fast and accurate similarity search over text, images, code, and more. As AI systems increasingly rely on contextual retrieval to ground responses in relevant data, VectorDBs provide the speed, scalability, and fine-tuning capabilities needed to support real-time, intelligent experiences. With continued improvements in indexing, filtering, and hybrid search, VectorDBs remain a foundational component of modern AI infrastructure.

Description

A vector database efficiently stores and retrieves information in the form of high-dimensional vectors, making it particularly suitable for handling unstructured data that has been transformed into vectors, such as text, images, or audio. DB's such as: Chroma, Milvus, Pinecone and many more.

blips.name: Taskfile
blips.description:
Why?

More stable, easier to use and install (one binary rules them all), in that category.

Description

Task is a task runner / build tool that aims to be simpler and easier to use than, for example, GNU Make. Since it's written in Go, Task is just a single binary and has no other dependencies, which means you don't need to mess with any complicated install setups just to use a build tool.

blips.name: Vert.x
blips.description:
Why?

We highly recommend this micro-framework as it is the fastest framework around with a very low footprint.

Description

Vert.x is a toolkit to build distributed reactive systems on the top of the Java Virtual Machine using an asynchronous and non-blocking development model. As a toolkit, Vert.x can be used in many contexts: in a standalone application or embedded in a Spring application. Vert.x and its ecosystem are just jar files used like any other library: just place them in your classpath and you are done. However, as Vert.x is a toolkit, it does not provide an all-in-one solution but provides the building blocks to build your own solution.

blips.name: Tekton - Pipeline
blips.description:
Why?

Powerful Kubernetes-native open-source framework for creating continuous integration and delivery (CI/CD) systems with Tekton custom k8s objects that allow flexible abstraction to common tasks.

Description

Tekton is a powerful yet flexible Kubernetes-native open-source framework for creating continuous integration and delivery (CI/CD) systems.

blips.name: Vite
blips.description:
Why?

Vite has transformed our development experience with its instantaneous server start and near-instant hot module replacement. It uses native ESM in the browser and bundles with lightning-fast tools (esbuild/Rollup) for production, which drastically shortens build times.

Description

Vite is a modern frontend build tool that provides a dev server and bundler. In development mode, Vite serves native ES modules to the browser, which means it doesn’t need to bundle the whole app – it just transforms individual files on the fly with esbuild (extremely fast).

blips.name: Vitest
blips.description:
Why?

Remains the primary recommendation for modern testing due to its native Vite integration and superior speed compared to Jest.

Description

Vitest is a unit testing framework that serves as a Vite-native alternative to Jest. It’s designed to run within a Vite environment, meaning it can leverage Vite’s module resolution, transformers, and esbuild for extremely fast test execution.

blips.name: vLLM
blips.description:
Why?

vLLM's PagedAttention, continuous batching, and best-in-class throughput make it the de facto standard for self-hosting open-source LLMs at production scale — nothing else comes close for teams serious about inference performance and cost efficiency.

Description

A fast and memory-efficient inference engine for large language models, featuring PagedAttention for optimized memory management and high throughput serving.

blips.name: Vue.js
blips.description:
Why?

Vue.js continues to thrive, especially after the release of Vue 3 which introduced the Composition API and other performance improvements. It combines the best ideas from frameworks like Angular (templates, directives) and React (component-based, virtual DOM) while remaining very approachable.

Description

Vue.js is a progressive JavaScript framework for building user interfaces. It emphasizes approachability (easy to pick up) and incrementally adoptable architecture.

blips.name: Telepresence
blips.description:
Why?

When you develop a microservice application that runs on Kubernetes Teleprences gives you a very good environment to debug and run the microservice that you developed locally and support the integration with all other microservices. We find Teleprences a very good tool that improves your development velocity when an application runs on Kubernetes.

Description

Telepresence gives developers infinite scale development environments for Kubernetes. With Telepresence:

  • You run one service locally, using your favorite IDE and other tools
  • You run the rest of your application in the cloud, where there is unlimited memory and compute This gives developers:
  • a fast local dev loop, with no waiting for a container build / push / deploy
  • ability to use their favorite local tools (IDE, debugger, etc.)
  • ability to run large-scale applications that can't run locally

blips.name: WebAssembly
blips.description:
Why?

WebAssembly (WASM) enables near-native performance in the browser by allowing code in languages like C++ or Rust to run in a safe, sandboxed environment.

Description

WebAssembly (WASM) is a binary instruction format for a stack-based virtual machine that runs in the browser. It allows developers to compile code written in languages like C, C++, or Rust into a format that can execute with near-native speed inside web apps.

blips.name: WebMCP
blips.description:
Why?

An experimental tool for implementing the Model Context Protocol to enhance AI agent capabilities within the browser.

Description

A browser extension or web-based client that enables AI assistants to interact with web applications through the Model Context Protocol.

blips.name: Webpack
blips.description:
Why?

Webpack remains one of the most powerful and widely used module bundlers in the JavaScript ecosystem. It is highly configurable and has a large plugin ecosystem that can accommodate virtually any build requirement.

Description

Webpack is a module bundler for modern JavaScript applications. It processes and bundles various assets (JavaScript, CSS, images) into optimized files for deployment.

blips.name: WebRTC
blips.description:
Why?

WebRTC provides peer-to-peer communication capabilities (audio, video, data) directly between browsers.

Description

WebRTC (Web Real-Time Communication) is a technology that enables direct peer-to-peer communication between browsers. It supports real-time audio, video, and arbitrary data transfer without requiring intermediate servers for the media (only a signaling server is needed to establish connections).

blips.name: Terraform
blips.description:
Why?

The king of provisioning tools is still here. Robust. Popular. Evolving.

Description

Terraform is a provisioning tool (as opposed to a Configuration Management tool), working with Immutable Infrastructures, using a declarative language, is masterless and agentless

Being a popular tool, from a well established vendor, HashiCorp we should certainly keep offering Terraform as an alternative to our customers

Terraform has recently announced the support of Kubernetes, going to show that HashiCorp is on its feet and adapting to changes

blips.name: Terragrunt
blips.description:
Why?

As Terragrunt provides functionality that Terraform currently lacks (might be adopted into Terraform in the future) we should suggest this tool as an extension for Terraform which allows for better coding practices and convention constraining.

Description

Terragrunt is a thin wrapper for terraform which provides further capabilities for organisations using terraform to provision resources.

Terragrunt allows us to further abstract terraform components to extend reusability of terraform configurations across environments and organisations

blips.name: Apache Zeppelin
blips.description:
Why?

Apache Zeppelin is a web-based notebook for data exploration and visualization, built around Spark and offering multi-language interpreter support — but largely overshadowed today by Jupyter and Databricks notebooks.

Description

Apache Zeppelin is a notebook for managing and visualizing Data and Data-lake. With Apache Zeppelin, one can perform Data Ingestion, Data Discovery, Data Analytics and also have Data Visualization & Collaboration. Apache Zeppelin is a Java runtime and supports the following languages and frameworks: Scala as Apache Spark, Python, JDBC, Markdown and Shell. It also supports many plugins The results of the queries can be shown in nice built-in visuals like graphs, pie charts and more.

Apache Zeppelin supports many additional interpreters that can be loaded or integrated using Helium, Among those interpreters are for example Cassandra, Elasticsearch, Flink, Ignite, bean, angular and many more.

blips.name: Terratest
blips.description:
Why?

Terratest is a Go library that makes it easier to write automated tests for your infrastructure code. It provides a variety of helper functions and patterns for common infrastructure testing tasks. https://github.com/gruntwork-io/terratest

Description

Terratest is a Go library that makes it easier to write automated tests for your infrastructure code. It provides a variety of helper functions and patterns for common infrastructure testing tasks https://github.com/gruntwork-io/terratest

blips.name: Zustand
blips.description:
Why?

Elevated to the industry standard for lightweight, hook-based global state management with minimal boilerplate.

Description

Zustand is a small, fast state management library for React. It creates a global store that components can subscribe to via a hook (without the need for context providers). You define state and actions in one place and then simply use the store hook in components to read or update state.

blips.name: Tilt
blips.description:
Why?

Tilt is a very good solution to improve developer productivity when working with cloud-native environment, By supporting the deployment in a native way to the local cluster

Description

Tilt - Client-side tools help develop an application for Kubernetes. Tilt using Tiltfile is written in Starlark, a dialect of Python. Tilt know to generate Kubernetes manifest, install helm and kustomized installation, execute builds, etc ..     Tilt know to work with a variant of the local and remote cluster Tilt Is live application detects a change on your local env and reflect the change to Kubernetes

blips.name: vCluster
blips.description:
Why?

A mature tool. It's cheaper than creating separate full-blown clusters and it offers better multi-tenancy and isolation than regular namespaces.

Description

Create fully functional virtual Kubernetes clusters - Each vcluster runs inside a namespace of the underlying k8s cluster.

blips.name: Vector
blips.description:
Why?

Vector is a very good and robust data pipeline tool.

Description

Vector is a high-performance, end-to-end (agent & aggregator) observability data pipeline that puts you in control of your observability data. Collect, transform, and route all your logs, metrics, and traces to any vendors you want today and any other vendors you may want tomorrow. Vector enables dramatic cost reduction, novel data enrichment, and data security where you need it, not where it is most convenient for your vendors. Additionally, it is open source and up to 10x faster than every alternative in the space.

blips.name: Velero
blips.description:
Why?

While Kubernetes resources should be managed as code, there are use cases where one needs to back it up as data. Velero gives a good solution for backing up and recovering Kubernetes resources when (for example) there is no time to wait for the CD process.

Description

Velero is an open source tool to safely backup and restore, perform disaster recovery, and migrate Kubernetes cluster resources and persistent volumes.

blips.name: VictoriaMetrics
blips.description:
Why?

VictoriaMetrics is a game changer in the observability space due to its exceptional performance, scalability, and simplicity. It efficiently processes data with minimal resource consumption, resulting in cost savings and improved operational efficiency. Its seamless integration with popular observability tools makes it a powerful and flexible solution for gaining insights and optimizing system reliability.

Description

VictoriaMetrics is a powerful open-source time series database and observability platform that is revolutionizing the field of observability. It is designed to efficiently handle large volumes of time series data, making it ideal for monitoring, analyzing, and visualizing metrics, logs, and traces in real-time. What sets VictoriaMetrics apart as a game changer is its unique combination of speed, scalability, and simplicity. It excels in ingesting, storing, and querying massive amounts of data with minimal resource consumption, making it highly efficient and cost-effective. With its high-performance querying capabilities and built-in support for popular observability standards like Prometheus and Grafana, VictoriaMetrics empowers organizations to gain deep insights into the performance and health of their systems. It enables faster troubleshooting, efficient capacity planning, and proactive monitoring, ultimately leading to improved reliability, reduced downtime, and enhanced user experiences. Moreover, VictoriaMetrics offers a range of advanced features, such as data retention policies, data replication for high availability, and support for distributed deployments, making it a flexible solution that can scale with the evolving needs of any organization.

blips.name: Warp
blips.description:
Why?

As the terminal is a major tool in the DevOps day to day, this product demonstrates strong capabilities comparing to others in that category.

Description

An excellent terminal for Mac, built with Rust for speed, intuitive out of the box. WARP is using modern editing, and many more feature such as ChatGPT embedded.

blips.name: Apache Zeppelin
blips.description:
Why?

Zeppelin is one of the best tools out there to experiment in Spark, and as such it makes Spark accessible for Data scientists (via PySpark).

Description

Apache Zeppelin is a notebook for managing and visualizing Data and Data-lake. With Apache Zeppelin, one can perform Data Ingestion, Data Discovery, Data Analytics and also have Data Visualization & Collaboration. Apache Zeppelin is a Java runtime and supports the following languages and frameworks: Scala as Apache Spark, Python, JDBC, Markdown and Shell. It also supports many plugins The results of the queries can be shown in nice built-in visuals like graphs, pie charts and more.

Apache Zeppelin supports many additional interpreters that can be loaded or integrated using Helium, Among those interpreters are for example Cassandra, Elasticsearch, Flink, Ignite, bean, angular and many more.

blips.name: Beanie (mongo ORM)
blips.description:
Why?

Beanie is an async Python ODM for MongoDB that lets you define documents as Pydantic models, giving you type safety, validation, and clean async queries without writing raw MongoDB dicts. It's a natural fit if you're already using FastAPI, since it plugs into the same Pydantic layer you're already working with — no extra mental model needed.

Description

Beanie - is an asynchronous Python object-document mapper (ODM) for MongoDB. Data models are based on Pydantic.

When using Beanie each database collection has a corresponding Document that is used to interact with that collection. In addition to retrieving data, Beanie allows you to add, update, or delete documents from the collection as well.

Beanie saves you time by removing boilerplate code, and it helps you focus on the parts of your app that actually matter.

Data and schema migrations are supported by Beanie out of the box.

There is a synchronous version of Beanie ODM - Bunnet

blips.name: HELM / Umbrella Chart
blips.description:
Why?

Once you have multiple services that need to be deployed together consistently across environments, the Umbrella Chart becomes the thing that guarantees they always go out as a unit, with the right versions and config. Removing it means going back to coordinating individual releases manually, which breaks reproducibility and makes environment parity much harder to maintain.

Description

Helm, short for Helm Charts which help manage Kubernetes applications — Helm Charts helps you define, install, and upgrade even the most complex Kubernetes applications.

Charts are easy to create, version, share, and publish. There are Helm Registry offerings from both Quay.io and Artifactory. HELM helps to manage Services, Deployment, Secrets and all parts related to Kubernetes ready applications. **Umbrella chart **, To install a complex application with helm — There is something called umbrella chart Umbrella chart is a chart with dependency (requirements.yaml) on other charts. and value.yaml (override charts values) To install umbrella-chart you run “helm dep update” will download depended on chart , then “helm install” or “helm upgrade” will install the charts

blips.name: Hugging Face
blips.description:
Why?

If you're working with LLMs or any ML models, it's the default starting point for finding pretrained models, running quick experiments, and staying current with what's available. Dropping it means either paying for proprietary APIs or rebuilding discovery and access workflows from scratch.

Description

Hugging Face is a leading AI company providing a platform for model sharing and collaboration, fostering a vibrant community of developers and researchers. Additionally, it supports integration with popular frameworks like TensorFlow and PyTorch. This makes Hugging Face a key resource for those working in AI and machine learning.It offers pre-trained models for tasks like text generation, sentiment analysis, and translation, simplifying the implementation of advanced NLP applications. Hugging Face's ecosystem includes tools for fine-tuning models and a hub for hosting and discovering models, datasets, and metrics. Its commitment to open-source development and community engagement accelerates innovation in the field of natural language processing.

blips.name: Agno
blips.description:
Why?

If your guild's AI Agents quarter is moving toward production-grade patterns — not just demos — Agno is one of the more complete frameworks out there. It handles the parts that most frameworks skip: session isolation, streaming, human-in-the-loop, audit logs, and tracing. It's also model-agnostic and runs in your own infrastructure, which matters when you're teaching real-world agentic system design rather than toy examples.

Description

A Python framework for building, running, and managing AI agents in production. It covers the full stack — from defining agents with tools, memory, and guardrails, to serving them as a scalable FastAPI backend, to monitoring them via a built-in UI. It supports single agents, multi-agent teams, and structured workflows, all on one architecture.

blips.name: Open Table Formats
blips.description:
Why?

The data engineering world has largely converged on this layer as the standard foundation for lakehouses. If you're building or teaching modern data pipelines, open table formats are no longer optional knowledge — they're the default assumption in most serious data stacks. They're also the underlying technology behind AWS S3 Tables, Snowflake's open catalog push, and most of the momentum around Apache Polaris and Unity Catalog, so staying current here keeps you relevant across the whole ecosystem.

Description

Open Table Formats (Apache Iceberg, Delta Lake, Apache Hudi) are open specifications that bring table-like semantics to files stored in object storage — giving you ACID transactions, schema evolution, time travel, and efficient query planning on top of plain Parquet files in S3 or GCS, without locking you into a proprietary storage engine.

blips.name: AWS Lambda for Data Pipelines
blips.description:
Why?

Lambda works well for small, event-driven triggers, but it hits real walls in data contexts — 15-minute execution limit, memory cap, cold starts, and poor fit for anything stateful or iterative. As pipelines grow, you end up fighting the runtime constraints more than solving data problems. Tools like AWS Glue, Step Functions, or even containerized jobs on ECS/Fargate give you more headroom with less friction, and frameworks like Airflow or Dagster handle orchestration far more cleanly than chaining Lambdas together. It's a reasonable starting point, but rarely the right long-term foundation for serious data pipelines.

Description

AWS Lambda for Data Pipelines is the practice of using serverless functions as processing units within a data pipeline — triggering transformations, file conversions, or lightweight ETL steps in response to events like an S3 upload, a Kinesis record, or an API call, without managing any underlying infrastructure.
